interventions.speaker_label: Thomas Byrne, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, Commissioner McGrath, let me thank Parliament for the opportunity to address you on what is an urgent matter and to thank you, Mr Tobé, for your work as rapporteur. This is a major priority for the Irish Presidency indeed.

The Special Committee on the European Democracy Shield has done excellent work over the last 19 months, and I admire its comprehensive findings and recommendations as to how to strengthen our democracies. Indeed, on behalf of the Council, I look forward to meeting the committee, I hope next month.

I am aware that the report of the Special Committee will only be voted on later today, but I think there is one finding that we can all agree on: that our democracies are under threat from outside and, indeed, inside. Nobody can deny the hybrid threats by Russia and disinformation campaigns that extend beyond individual Member States. As the report states, such attacks target the very essence of the European project and the core values enshrined in Article 2 of the Treaty.

These values are the respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law, and respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities. Upholding these values is an indispensable foundation of our Union, and indeed is one of the three pillars of the Irish Presidency.

When it comes to the protection of democracy, this includes protecting free and fair elections, protecting freedom of speech, and protecting the free and independent media. But all of our efforts can only be effective if we empower our citizens. They are the centre of our democracies and our elections, and we must look beyond elections by increasing citizens' participation and engagement in general.

Citizens must know that they can influence real outcomes. Especially marginalised groups of citizens are likely to perceive themselves as lacking political influence. Citizens' participation and engagement is a particular priority for our presidency because we cannot ignore that there is democratic disengagement.

The Irish Presidency is working to achieve conclusions that will send a clear signal of the Council's support for citizens' inclusion in democracy as essential to European societal and community resilience. Moreover, we cannot ignore that such disengagement might also be linked to decreasing trust in democratic institutions. It is our duty as elected politicians to work every day for democratic institutions that are transparent, accountable, inclusive, resilient and genuinely responsive to our citizens' needs.

We also need to act against the threats and harassments of politicians and people active in politics that risk distorting our democracies. The Irish Presidency organised a productive exchange with the Member States at the margins of the last General Affairs Council on good practices in the area, and this yielded valuable contributions.

Let me highlight one more duty that we have towards our citizens: their protection online. We need to address online disinformation, online criminality and child safety in the online environment. In this context, the European Council back in March stressed the legal responsibility of online platforms in fighting the dissemination of disinformation and illegal content.

When it comes to such dissemination, notably by foreign actors aiming at interfering in elections, Member States have already stepped up significantly their efforts, but also malicious foreign actors have stepped up their efforts. A clear sign of escalation is the increased use of hybrid warfare. This is no longer just a threat to our democracy, but also to our very security.

We are therefore thankful for the dedicated debate on hybrid attacks by Russia and the presence of the High Representative that will take place later today. The Irish Presidency has also worked with Member States on projects, including on combating FIMI, being prepared with the European Centre on Democratic Resilience, and we will host exchanges at an autumn Council on onboarding candidate countries to this centre.

Let me assure this House that the Irish Presidency continues the endeavours of previous presidencies in bringing Member States together in their united efforts to strengthen democratic resilience, and in supporting the European Commission and Commissioner McGrath in implementing the European Democracy Shield.

interventions.speaker_label: Michael McGrath, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear Minister Byrne, honourable Members, let me first of all thank the Special Committee – in particular, its chair, the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs – for their immense amount of work that has gone into the preparation of this report.

The European Democracy Shield was presented some ten months ago against a backdrop of growing threats to democracy. Malign actors continue to adapt their tactics, seeking to interfere in elections, to erode trust in institutions, to deepen divisions and to instrumentalise conflicts.

Threats evolve, but our preparedness, resilience and response tools are also getting stronger every day. Europeans see democracy as an EU strength, so we must deliver for them and for our democracies.

The European Democracy Shield is our strategic framework to strengthen and protect our democracies across three key priorities: safeguarding the integrity of the information space; strengthening democratic institutions, ensuring free and fair elections, and free and independent media; and bolstering societal resilience and the engagement of our citizens.

We are turning these objectives together into actions. The European Centre for Democratic Resilience is operational since February. It enables Member States and institutions to strengthen cooperation and improve our collective resilience. All Member States have joined the Centre – a clear testament, I believe, to its value. Soon also, candidate and potential candidate countries will be associated, to strengthen democratic resilience together.

Let me give you some examples of projects led by Member States or through collective expertise under the Centre: a train-the-trainer programme for upskilling government officials across Member States; a project on common concepts, methodologies and standards for detection; as well as the Blueprint for countering FIMI and disinformation.

A stakeholder platform is also being set up to support the Centre through the expertise of a range of independent stakeholders. We are working resolutely in all of the priority areas of the European Democracy Shield, within the Centre, but also beyond.
We are making our elections more resilient, including by reinforcing the excellent work of the European Cooperation Network on Elections.

We're also strengthening the resilience of our media information environment through the ongoing implementation of the European Media Freedom Act, the anti-SLAPP EU framework and the review of the Audiovisual Media Services Directive.
The DSA, the AI Act and the Regulation on political advertising equally contribute to the protection of the information space.

The European Digital Media Observatory is now covering also candidate countries. The European network of fact-checkers is being rolled out. We have updated the guidelines for teachers on how to tackle disinformation.
Looking ahead, we will present a package on safety in politics, and guidance on the responsible use of AI in electoral processes.
Under the leadership of the High Representative, the External Action Service is also strengthening our external response to foreign information manipulation and interference.

For the next MFF, several proposed programmes would support the objectives of the European Democracy Shield, notably Agora EU. Our ambition to strengthen our democracies should be matched by an equally ambitious budget, in my view.
We will continue to take forward the European Democracy Shield, as well as to embed protection of our democracies in other policy areas.
I want to assure the Members that your recommendations will provide very valuable insights to inform our work, and I look forward to the contribution of all of the honourable Members today.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, in recent months, Russia has changed radically its playbook. It no longer only spreads lies using AI-enabled support networks across all main platforms. It sabotages cables, blows up weapons factories, threatens assassinations and carries them out as well. It jams aviation, flies drones over our airports, pushes migrants across our borders and pays criminals inside our Union to do its dirty work. Arson for hire, interference by proxy: this is not propaganda anymore; it is operational and it is active. Testing, probing and finding routes to escalate its war beyond Ukraine.

The Democracy Shield must answer in kind. Awareness is not enough. We need enforcement. We need resources. That means updating mandates. Europol must be able to investigate foreign hybrid operations proactively, not only assist afterwards. Europe needs the tools to prosecute state-directed sabotages across borders, as what it is: organised crime in service of a hostile power. And Frontex must be empowered to counter instrumentalism of migrants as weapons, not only to manage things, but proactively as it happens.

interventions.speaker_label: Ana Catarina Mendes, em nome do Grupo S&D.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário, caros colegas, eu julgo que é particularmente oportuna a discussão deste relatório no Dia Internacional da Democracia. Este não é um dia apenas para celebrarmos, mas sim para continuarmos a aprofundar e a defender as nossas democracias. E, num momento em que as democracias enfrentam vários desafios, como a desinformação, a manipulação, a ingerência estrangeira, os ataques digitais cada vez mais sofisticados com o recurso à inteligência artificial, o relatório que apresentámos — aproveito para saudar o papel do relator no compromisso alcançado — é particularmente relevante por quatro razões.

Em primeiro lugar, porque determina uma melhor coordenação entre as instituições europeias, os Estados‑Membros e as autoridades nacionais na resposta europeia à ingerência estrangeira através da criação do Centro Europeu de Resiliência Democrática. Em segundo lugar, uma maior capacidade europeia para responder às campanhas de manipulação de informação, de reforço da integridade do espaço informativo. Em terceiro lugar, a defesa de uma imprensa livre, independente e plural, que também assegure a segurança dos jornalistas. E, por último, uma sociedade civil mais forte, mais robusta e mais participativa junto dos poderes de decisão.

Proteger a democracia é proteger a liberdade, a verdade e a dignidade dos cidadãos europeus, promovendo uma democracia mais forte, mais participativa e mais transparente. Eu espero que este relatório seja esse contributo, porque eu venho de um país que teve uma ditadura de 48 anos, e é bom viver em democracia há 52 anos. Celebremos a democracia.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! A Demokráciapajzs-program elvileg a külső beavatkozások elleni védelemről szól. Mindezt úgy, hogy ha a Bizottságnak nem tetsző kormány van egy tagállamban, akkor folyamatosak a beavatkozások. És ez nem minden. Magyarországon az új kormány eltávolította a köztársasági elnököt és több alkotmánybírót. Eltiltották az újraindulástól az ellenzék vezetőjét, egy 12 éves mandátumkorlátozás miatt az ellenzéki képviselők nagy része egyszerűen nem indulhat el a következő választáson. Ha itt, ebben a Házban ilyen szabályt vezetnének be, akkor önök közül 164-en nem indulhatnának újra.

Hol van ilyenkor a híres demokráciapajzsuk? Egyetlen szavuk nincs. A további csend egyvalaminek lenne a bizonyítéka: annak, hogy pont nem a demokrácia érdekli az itteni nagykoalíciót, hanem az, hogy cseléd módjára engedelmes kormányok legyenek a tagállamokban. Jogállamisági Biztos Úr, McGrath Úr! Két hónapja Ön azt mondta nekünk, hogy monitorozzák ezeket a lépéseket. Szóval kérdezzük Önt, mire jutott. Belefér ez? Belefér, hogy kizárják az ellenzék jelentős részét a következő választásról? Mindezt egy uniós tagállamban? Belefér ez? Várjuk szíves válaszát.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Szanowny Panie Komisarzu! Szanowni Państwo! Bardzo chciałabym poprzeć to sprawozdanie, ponieważ zawiera ono szereg bardzo trafnych diagnoz, szczególnie tych dotyczących wpływów i ingerencji ze strony Rosji, wpływów chińskich czy białoruskich na to, co się dzieje, i na procesy demokratyczne w Unii Europejskiej. Chciałabym je poprzeć, ale nie mogę. Mamy bowiem w Unii doświadczenia, kiedy pod osłoną szlachetnych wartości i wzniosłych haseł podejmowano działania niemające z tymi wartościami wiele wspólnego. Tak było chociażby z mechanizmem praworządności, który w przypadku Polski stał się narzędziem politycznego nacisku, blokowania należnych nam funduszy oraz wymuszania zmiany rządu.

Dlatego mamy podstawy obawiać się, że dzisiejsze sprawozdanie może jutro stać się wytrychem otwierającym drogę do ingerencji instytucji europejskich w suwerenne wybory państw członkowskich. Przypomnijmy sobie chociażby to, co wydarzyło się po pierwszej turze wyborów w Rumunii. Dlatego, Szanowni Państwo, muszę zadać pytanie: kto będzie pilnował strażników demokracji? Musimy bronić Europy przed rosyjską dezinformacją, cyberatakami i obcą ingerencją. Ale odpowiedzią na ingerencję z Moskwy czy Pekinu nie może być stworzenie możliwości ingerencji z Brukseli. Demokracji nie obroni się poprzez ograniczenie demokratycznego wyboru. Grupa EKR nie będzie mogła zatem poprzeć tego sprawozdania.

interventions.speaker_label: Helmut Brandstätter, im Namen der Renew-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, sehr geehrter Herr Kommissar, sehr geehrter Herr Minister, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Eineinhalb Jahre haben wir gearbeitet an diesem Schutz für unsere Demokratie. Und wir müssen eingestehen: In diesen eineinhalb Jahren sind die Herausforderungen noch viel größer geworden.

Wir haben gesehen: Ja, Putins Desinformation wird schlimmer. Wir haben aber auch gesehen: Mehr Cyberattacken, und zuletzt in Leipzig einen Terroranschlag Putins gegen Menschen in Europa. Das sind die Fakten.

Was wir in dem Bericht auch haben: Migration wird auch als Waffe verwendet, und auch Islamismus ist eine Gefahr für unsere Demokratie. Putin will die Destabilisierung. Er kann seinem Land nichts anderes bieten; er ist ein KGB-Mann. Er will die Zerstörung unserer Demokratie, unserer freien Gesellschaft.

Und das Traurige ist: Hier sitzen Rechtsextreme, die das gemeinsam mit ihm machen – wo wir sehen, in den amerikanischen Plattformen, wo dieselben Botschaften zum Teil von Rechtsextremen kommen, zum Teil von Putin kommen. Und auch ein interessanter Satz, den wir gehört haben: „Das Ziel der amerikanischen Plattformen ist die Verbreitung von Hass.“ So funktionieren diese Algorithmen. Und wir wissen auch: Manche in Amerika, manche Denkfabriken, wie es so schön heißt, wollen die EU zerstören, weil wir einfach so stark sind.

Jetzt müssen wir etwas tun, Herr Kommissar. Das resilience centre muss arbeiten; da ist viel zu tun. Wir müssen die Aufklärung haben, und wir müssen auch Medien, freie Medien stärken. Das können wir. Das können wir nur gemeinsam. Und so retten wir unsere Demokratie.

interventions.speaker_label: Kim Van Sparrentak, on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, social media algorithms are turning the mere existence of refugees, queers, migrants, religious minorities and women into 'rage bait'.

Political actors who want to erode our democracies are using it: we saw it 10 years ago around Brexit, we saw it a year ago in Romania, we saw it recently in Ceuta, and we saw it last week in Saxony-Anhalt.
Today, Parliament agrees on what many Europeans already know: social media in its current form is a threat to democracy.

The rage-baiting algorithms of social media turn us into toys of Putin and the far-right. And 'tech bros' like Musk and Zuckerberg keep you hooked to your phone and fill their pockets with the spread of disinformation.

Divisive messages top our timelines, then they seep through to our media, our politics, and our dinner tables. But finally, now, we have a majority for action: we will limit polarising algorithms so people can see what connects us, not what divides us.

And we will move away from these anti-European companies: we will take our democracy out of the hands of Elon Musk, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin and put it back in the hands of the people and our democratic institutions.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, l'elefante ha partorito un topolino perché le conclusioni di questa commissione speciale dovrebbero essere studiate come esempio dell'utilizzo di doppi standard.

Invece di uno studio sui rischi reali per le nostre democrazie, siamo dinanzi sempre al solito schema: da una parte i Paesi come Russia, Cina, Iran, Corea del Nord, eccetera, eccetera, che sono le principali minacce e dobbiamo armarci contro il pericolo imminente.

Però, mentre parliamo e cerchiamo questi attacchi ibridi, veri o presunti, e queste ciberminacce da parte di questi Paesi, chiudete gli occhi per l'ennesima volta verso le ingerenze, già note all'opinione pubblica, che provengono da quelli che dovrebbero essere i nostri alleati.

Perché, quando l'ex premier della Slovenia, Golob, chiedeva l'applicazione di uno scudo democratico contro le ingerenze nelle elezioni slovene da parte di una società gestita da ex agenti dei servizi segreti israeliani del Mossad, qual è stata la vostra risposta? Assolutamente nessuna.

Siamo totalmente dipendenti dalle infrastrutture tecnologiche statunitensi e siamo esposti alla loro sorveglianza costante. Ma la cosa più preoccupante è il proliferare di spyware di fabbricazione israeliana, che hanno più volte spiato giornalisti, politici, cittadini dell'Unione europea illegalmente, con l'intento palese di destabilizzare l'opinione pubblica. Ecco, la parola "Israele" non viene citata nemmeno una volta in questa relazione.

State sottovalutando il vero pericolo, perché quello che è successo a Ceuta, contro la Spagna, è solo l'anteprima di ciò che potrebbe succedere e succederà ai Paesi che scelgono di non allinearsi alla politica estera di Washington o Tel Aviv.

Questa commissione è servita solo per giustificare nuove censure e altre spese militari, mentre sanità e istruzione muoiono. Altro che scudo per la democrazia: questo è lo scudo della vostra ipocrisia!

interventions.speaker_label: Christine Anderson, on behalf of the ESN Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the ESN Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, what a dangerous report. You call it a Democracy Shield. A shield? It is a declaration of war on two fronts.

First, abroad. You demand offensive abilities. Against whom? And on whose authority? This Parliament recklessly picks fights. And when – not if – this escalation backfires, the citizens will have to pay the price.

Second, at home. You invoke freedom of expression, but you are building a machinery to restrict, monitor, steer and manipulate domestic public debate. Your Orwellian language fools no one. Your defence is an attack and your freedom is, in fact, totalitarian control.
A shield is meant to protect, but you are not building a shield. You are building a weapon pointed at the very people that you were elected to protect. Shame on you. Shame on you.

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedající, nejprve mi dovolte poděkovat všem, kteří se na této práci podíleli. Je skutečně dobrá a musím říct, že silná a jasná. Ale mám jednu velikánskou výhradu – promiňte –, a to k bodu 27. Ten se týká transparentnosti na sociálních sítích a boji proti falešným účtům a trollím farmám. Ve dvou částech se ale zároveň prosazuje údajné právo na anonymitu online.

Vážení kolegové, proč mají trollové, kteří podporují AfD nebo kteří pocházejí z Ruska a Číny, kteří tam vytvářejí obsah, desetitisíce falešných účtů, mít právo na anonymitu? Myslíte si, že trollí farmy v Rusku nebo v Číně jsou demokraticky řízené? Myslíte si, že občané v Rusku a v Číně si můžou říkat, co chtějí? Proč mají mít tito lidé stejný názor jako vy nebo já? Proč lidé, kteří ničí demokracii, chodí nám a našim dětem každý den vyhrožovat smrtí, mají být v anonymitě? Zbláznili jsme se?

Kolegové, kamarádi, přátelé, opravdu nechci, aby fašisté a nacisté vyhrávali další volby. Pojďme udělat něco s anonymitou internetu a pojďme jednou provždy říci, že demokracie je dobrá v momentě, když ji umíme chránit. Jinak tento boj prohrajeme.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Fru formand! Demokrati er den grundsten, vi har bygget hele det europæiske samarbejde på, og lige nu er det under angreb. Der er krig på vores kontinent, udenlandske magter forsøger at skabe frygt og splittelse, og gamle allierede er ikke længere de sikre venner, vi engang kunne regne med.

Og truslen har fået nye våben. Desinformation, kunstig intelligens og algoritmer bliver brugt til at manipulere vores offentlige debat, påvirke valg og splitte vores samfund. Derfor skal vi stå fast på vores europæiske regler og demokratiske institutioner. Techgiganterne skal leve op til deres ansvar, og vi skal behandle det europæiske demokrati som det, det er, nemlig kritisk infrastruktur, og det skal beskyttes.

Når demokratiet bliver angrebet på tværs af vores grænser, skal vi også forsvare det på tværs af vores grænser. Derfor skal vi sikre et stærkt og effektivt demokratiskjold med et europæisk center for demokratisk modstandsdygtighed. Det kan være med til at styrke vores fælles forsvar mod udenlandsk indblanding.
Demokratiet forsvarer ikke sig selv, men det gør vi.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedající, já souhlasím s tím, že demokracie je potřeba chránit. Já souhlasím s tím, že musíme bojovat proti vměšování se do našich záležitostí, bojovat proti dezinformacím. V čem se ale neshodnu, je to, jakým způsobem to budeme dělat.

K této zprávě i k tomu, když představila Komise svoji část Štítu pro demokracii, jsem byl velmi skeptický. Protože pokud my se budeme zaměřovat na to, že budeme centralizovat, jakým způsobem budeme podporovat občanskou společnost, média, o kterých dnes nemáme ani jasnou informaci o tom, jakým způsobem jsou financovány, pokud budeme podporovat fact-checking, který už několikrát selhal, a pokud se budeme snažit i řídit volby v členských státech, tak si myslím, že to není ta správná cesta. Centralizace takovéto moci spíše představuje nebezpečí pro naši demokracii.

Musíme také chránit naše hodnoty, a to i v rámci boje například proti migraci, protože naše hodnoty dostávají díky migraci na frak. Já bych chtěl žít ve svobodné, kriticky myslící a vzdělané společnosti, ale ne v orwellovském světě.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, credo che tutti qua siamo convinti del fatto che bisogna evitare qualsiasi forma di interferenza esterna e penso che le nazioni europee siano assolutamente in grado di farlo. Certo, ognuno con le sue modalità, ognuno con la sua sovranità: ma quello che non possiamo accettare è che quello che ci state proponendo qua, con questo scudo europeo per la democrazia, è di costituire un centro che andrà a violare la sovranità dei singoli Paesi, dicendogli quanto sono democratici.

L'anno prossimo avremo elezioni in Italia, avremo elezioni in Spagna, avremo elezioni in Francia e in tanti altri Paesi fondamentali della nostra Europa. Ci sarà un centro comandato da Bruxelles che andrà a giudicare quello che accade in ogni singola nazione? Beh, no, questo noi non possiamo accettarlo, perché purtroppo abbiamo avuto una pessima esperienza in passato, quando l'Europa cercava di violare la sovranità delle nazioni e, guarda caso, sempre di attaccare qualche governo di destra o qualche formazione politica che a qualcuno di Bruxelles non piaceva.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, nous votons aujourd'hui le rapport de la commission spéciale que je préside sur le Bouclier démocratique européen. Je voudrais remercier le rapporteur Tomas Tobé pour son travail et pour proposer à notre Parlement un texte qui fait un bilan honnête des attaques que subissent nos démocraties, comme des moyens d'y répondre. Je voudrais aussi saluer l'esprit de responsabilité dans lequel les groupes politiques attachés à la démocratie dans notre assemblée ont su travailler ensemble. Ce n'est malheureusement pas toujours le cas sur d'autres sujets. Il est heureux que sur la défense de la démocratie, nous ayons su nous retrouver.

Il est tout de même malheureux qu'il faille qu'elle soit à ce point prise d'assaut pour que nous nous souvenions de ce qui nous rassemble. Il est encore plus malheureux qu'à l'extrême droite de cette Chambre on n'ait cessé de considérer que le Parlement n'avait pas à s'y intéresser, que les ingérences n'étaient pas une menace, qu'il fallait renoncer à lutter contre le mensonge et à réguler ceux qui aident à le propager. C'est malheureux, mais c'est ainsi et chacun jugera. Ce qui est certain, c'est que la protection de la démocratie ne s'arrêtera pas avec le vote de ce rapport. Ce qui est avéré, c'est que les mesures proposées et mises en place par la Commission sont insuffisantes, insuffisamment mises en œuvre, trop peu appliquées par nos gouvernements. Ces mesures sont pourtant le strict nécessaire et sur ce plan-là, le compte n'y est pas.

paragraphs.text: Европа има нужда от защита. Тя трябва не просто да отразява ударите на всички онези, които искат да отнемат на европейските граждани свободата да мислят и говорят различно, да действат според собствените си убеждения, а не според нарежданията, спускани от официозните говорители. Ние, европейците, трябва да се борим активно, за да съхраним най-висшите постижения на европейската цивилизация.

А кой всъщност е нашият противник? Не, не са руснаците, не са китайците, не са иранците, нито който и да било друг от нарочените за врагове. Хората, които искат да унищожат уникалността на Европа, са тук. Това са ръководителите на Европейския съюз. Разположили са се удобно ето тук, в луксозните си офиси в Брюксел и Страсбург и се изживяват като абсолютни монарси, чиито заповеди всички трябва безпрекословно да изпълняваме.

Да, Европа има нужда от щит, подобен на онзи, който бог Хефест изковава за Ахил в Омировата Илиада. Трябва ѝ обаче и копие като това, с което Ахил сразява враговете си. Само така Европа може да победи евроначалниците, които похитиха европейската идея.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, nos démocraties sont attaquées sur tous les fronts: cyberattaques, désinformation, financements politiques hostiles, instrumentalisation des migrations, comme récemment en Espagne, à Ceuta. L'objectif est clair: déstabiliser nos sociétés. Face à ces menaces, nous devons adopter une vigilance à 360 degrés. Se focaliser sur une seule menace serait une erreur stratégique. Notre dépendance technologique nous fragilise. Trop souvent, les plateformes numériques deviennent des auxiliaires passifs des déstabilisations. Nous devons les confronter à leurs responsabilités.

Chers collègues, une part de réponse passe par la fin de l'anonymat en ligne. Ayons le courage de franchir ce pas. Mais notre exemplarité est essentielle. Pluralisme politique, médias libres, liberté d'expression, protection des communications privées des citoyens sont des impératifs. Enfin, aucune démocratie ne peut résister si ses élus sont intimidés, manipulés ou espionnés. C'est pourquoi la suppression des logiciels espions doit devenir une priorité absolue.

Într-adevăr, cu toții am reușit să aducem prin acest raport un lucru fundamental – recunoaștem că apărarea democrației se află în centrul securității, al sistemului de securitate al Europei.

Într-adevăr, acest raport are multe merite, acordă un rol important presei independente, societății civile, educației media și participării cetățenilor. Susține și reducerea dependențelor tehnologice față de exterior, care limitează autonomia Europei în acest moment. Am contribuit la aceste direcții prin amendamente privind controlul parlamentar al centrului, reprezentarea tuturor statelor, autonomia digitală, responsabilitatea platformelor și pregătirea întregii societăți.

Putem însă, în viitor, să fim și mai ambițioși. Sper că în viitor vom face asta. Europa va deveni însă mai rezilientă nu doar prin centre, instituții și reglementări, ci mai ales în momentul în care cetățenii au încredere, competențe și motive concrete să considere că sistemul democratic îi reprezintă.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidente, pues oyendo lo que se ha oído aquí, hay que decir que qué peligrosa es la libertad para la democracia. Ahora sacamos este informe que, como la Comisión, tiene un nombre enormemente sarcástico de Escudo de la Democracia, cuando se trata de un instrumento de una mayoría que ya solo existe aquí, que solo existe ya en este Parlamento, para criminalizar a una oposición conservadora y patriota que gobernará pronto en muchas naciones europeas y que será mayoría aquí también en 2029.

La lucha legítima contra las amenazas híbridas y la injerencia de potencias hostiles se convierte en pretexto para centralizar competencias, cercenar derechos y liquidar libertades. Instrumentaliza el miedo a Rusia y a China, pero calla injerencias y corrupción como el Qatargate o la bien pagada protección a Marruecos —ese agresor que ha invadido parte de España en Ceuta—. El Centro Europeo para la Resiliencia Democrática es un ministerio de verdad orwelliano, un monstruo hiperburocrático diseñado para desviar aún más dinero público a sus propias redes clientelares de ONG, medios y censores.
Termino: este informe huele a miedo. Ustedes saben que su tiempo ha acabado. Su batería de armas antidemocráticas contra las fuerzas patriotas no podrán evitarlo.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Szanowni Państwo! Zagrożenia, jakie płyną ze strony autorytarnego reżimu Putina i komunistycznych Chin są realne. Trzeba im się przeciwstawiać zdecydowanie, gdyż dotyczą sfery bezpieczeństwa narodowego i uderzają w istotę demokracji. Trzeba jednak w tym zakresie rozwijać i wzmacniać kompetencje państw członkowskich.

Nie jest właściwą odpowiedzią na wrogie działania Chin i Rosji tworzenie niejasnego, chaotycznego instrumentu unijnego nazywanego pretensjonalnie „tarczą demokracji”. To, czego się obawiamy, to możliwość manipulacji tym instrumentem ze strony unijnego polityczno-urzędniczego establishmentu. Za publiczne pieniądze ma zostać stworzona sieć organizacji mających pilnować politycznej poprawności w przestrzeni publicznej.

Nie chcemy, aby pod szczytnymi hasłami obrony demokracji, ograniczano pluralizm polityczny i wolność słowa. Nie chcemy, aby powstał nietransparentny mechanizm, który może być wykorzystany do ingerencji zewnętrznej w wybory krajowe. Tak właśnie, w wyniku takiej zewnętrznej ingerencji establishmentu brukselskiego w Polsce, rządzi dziś w naszym kraju reżim Tuska.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, quand j'entends certaines interventions de nos collègues, surtout à l'extrême droite, j'hésite à y voir une naïveté confondante ou une complaisance coupable. Car ne nous trompons pas, l'Europe est sous la pression extrême des ingérences et des attaques hybrides de la part d'organisations, voire même de puissances, étrangères. Et parmi celles-ci, en haut de la liste – pas seulement, mais en haut de la liste – se trouve la Russie.

C'est vrai que le Kremlin n'a pas besoin d'avoir des chars postés sur le rond-point Schuman pour utiliser tous les moyens en sa possession pour nous intimider, pour tenter de nous influencer. Nous tester aussi: tester notre défense, tester notre résilience et tester aussi nos acquis démocratiques.

Demain, j'ai bon espoir qu'une majorité lucide dans ce Parlement votera les recommandations présentées pour renforcer la stratégie du bouclier démocratique. Car l'autonomie stratégique de l'Europe, que j'appelle de mes vœux, ce n'est pas seulement le soutien à nos champions industriels et notre indépendance énergétique. C'est avant toute chose notre capacité à faire notre propre choix démocratique, en toute indépendance et surtout en toute liberté.

Hagyjuk az újbeszédet, és mondjuk ki nyíltan, a pajzs az Önök hatalmát védi az európai polgárok véleményével szemben.

paragraphs.text: Szanowni Państwo! Szanowna Pani Przewodnicząca! Sprawozdanie o tarczy demokracji mówi wprost, ile Rosja dziś ma na nas sposobów, jak eskaluje we wszystkich możliwych domenach. Ale to sprawozdanie Parlamentu Europejskiego odpowiada na propozycje Komisji i tym samym dziedziczy wszystkie jej ograniczenia. Zakłada zbudowanie nowego centrum koordynacyjnego, które poświęci najbliższy rok na budowanie planu działania. Logika działania Komisji Europejskiej jest zbyt wolna i nieadekwatna do sytuacji. W niedzielę dwa drony rosyjskie uderzyły w pociąg Kijów-Warszawa, wczoraj polskie wojsko wyłowiło rosyjskiego drona z Bałtyku, a duński helikopter został ostrzelany przez Rosjan na Bałtyku.

NATO, sparaliżowane przez Trumpa, odpowiada na to strategią, którą jeden z dyplomatów bardzo trafnie określił „keep calm and carry on”. I właśnie to jest sednem problemu. My w Europie, w Unii Europejskiej, wciąż budujemy struktury, a potrzebujemy decyzji. Centrum koordynacji to nie jest odpowiedź polityczna, lecz administracyjna. Putin nie boi się kolejnego organu unijnego. Putin boi się konsekwencji, które przychodzą dziś, a nie za dwa lata. Dobrze, że zajęliśmy się ochroną demokracji w Unii Europejskiej, ale to nie rozwiązuje problemu toczącej się wojny wypowiedzianej Europie przez Moskwę. To nie struktury, ale decyzje polityczne rozstrzygną tę wojnę.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señor comisario, ¿estamos de acuerdo en que la idea europea de democracia requiere de una ciudadanía libremente informada, capaz de deliberar racionalmente, libre de interferencias extranjeras, desinformación y la manipulación de los algoritmos adictivos en manos de plataformas tecnológicas? ¿Estamos de acuerdo en que eso puede hacer muchísimo daño, como hemos visto en Ceuta, donde actores estatales y no estatales han utilizado la mentira en las redes sociales para intentar debilitar la convivencia, e incluso la integridad, de la Unión Europea y de un Estado miembro como es España?

¿Estamos de acuerdo en que hemos puesto en vigor algunas leyes muy importantes y decisivas como son el Reglamento sobre la Libertad de los Medios de Comunicación, la Ley de Servicios Digitales, el Reglamento de Mercados Digitales y el Reglamento de Inteligencia Artificial, precisamente para disciplinar esas plataformas tecnológicas, porque no solamente hace falta reglas sólidas e instituciones fuertes, sino también una ciudadanía capaz de defenderse frente a sus amenazas?

Pues bien, este informe de la Comisión Especial sobre el Escudo Europeo de la Democracia es el producto de años de trabajo muy serio para intentar fortalecer esa idea europea de democracia frente a sus amenazas. Ahora hace falta que la Comisión Especial sea capaz de tomar las iniciativas para que cada una de las decisiones de este informe del Escudo de la Democracia sea correctamente ejecutada en el futuro.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, le rapport de Tomas Tobé sur le bouclier européen de la démocratie est une vaste blague. Sous prétexte de protéger la démocratie, il encourage en réalité une dérive profondément orwellienne et dessine les contours d'un véritable ministère européen de la vérité. Car au nom de la lutte contre la désinformation, la Commission veut contrôler toujours davantage notre espace informationnel avec les fameux «fact checkers» et des ONG privées qu'elle gave de millions d'euros d'argent public.

Vous êtes entrés dans un délire qui menace directement la liberté d'expression de dizaines de millions d'Européens. Et après l'annulation de l'élection présidentielle en Roumanie, nous savons jusqu'où cette logique peut conduire. Demain en France, en Pologne, en Espagne ou en Italie, que se passera-t-il si les électeurs placent en tête des patriotes, des conservateurs, des souverainistes ou des eurosceptiques?

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, dragi colegi, raportul Comisiei speciale pentru Scutul european pentru democrație putea fi un raport de referință făcut profesionist și echilibrat, însă nu e. Raportul are multe părți bune, însă per ansamblu este extrem de ideologizat și ignoră chestiuni foarte serioase, cum sunt controlul reflexiv și războiul cognitiv deja operat de Rusia împotriva Europei.

Sub pretextul apărării democrației, raportul propune conferirea Comisiei Europene puteri de influențare a alegerilor, ceea ce nu este democratic. Europa nu are nevoie de „un minister sau comisar al adevărului‟, ci de idei în dezbatere și pragmatism. Europa nu are nevoie de mai multă cenzură, birocrație și centralism. Europa are nevoie de mai multă libertate, transparență și de protecția drepturilor fundamentale.

Libertatea de exprimare nu este un privilegiu conferit europenilor de către Comisia Europeană, ci un drept fundamental al tuturor europenilor. De aceea, apărarea democrației nu este făcută prin cenzură, ci prin deciziile bune luate de politicieni în favoarea oamenilor.

So close the loophole. Secure Europe with biometrics. Secure Europe by keeping Putin's assassins out.

paragraphs.text: Г-жо Председател, два са основните проблема в цифровите платформи. Това е бизнес алгоритмите на големите компании, насърчаващи негативните емоции и конспирациите, и другото е анонимността. Руската пропаганда използва и двата проблема изключително умело, за да може не само с оръжие да завладява територии, но и да окупира душите и сърцата на милиони европейски граждани и да ги прави техни последователи.

Основният принцип на Закона за цифровите услуги е, че всичко, което е незаконно в реалния свят офлайн, трябва да бъде незаконно и онлайн. Но как може да прилагаме този принцип, ако не знаем кой стои зад даден профил или група в социалните мрежи, без дори да сме сигурни дали това наистина е човек? Нито една конституция в Европейския съюз или закон не признава право на анонимност онлайн. Имаме право на личен живот, защита на личните данни и свобода на словото, но тези права не означават право да нарушаваш закона и да се криеш зад анонимен профил, както нямаш право напълно маскиран да вървиш по улицата и да разпространяваш лъжи, обиди и конспирации, така и нямаш право да имаш тази привилегия онлайн.

Както в реалния живот, така и онлайн трябва да носим отговорност за действията си. Ако някой онлайн разпространява незаконно съдържание, сее омраза, заплашва или извършва престъпление, трябва да можем да установим кой е този, който седи зад този профил. Затова се нуждаем от надлежна верификация на самоличността в социалните мрежи, основана на европейските платформи за потвърждаване на самоличност. Не можем да позволим анонимността да се превърне в щит за руската пропаганда, престъпни мрежи, които искат да манипулират обществото, да разпространяват омраза и да влияят върху изборите в демократичните държави.

Oroszország, külföldi beavatkozások, álhírek, közösségi, a média közösségi média algoritmusai, dezinformációs kampányok. Szóval volt dolgunk bőven. Aztán mostanában valami egészen új, egészen rémisztő jön szembe, a mesterséges intelligencia. Mielőtt legyintenénk, hogy ó, ez is csak egy újabb technológia, érdemes feltennünk a kérdést, hogy mi történik akkor, ha valaki már nem ezer embert tud félrevezetni, hanem százmilliót? Nem egy álhírt tud gyártani, hanem minden embernek egy-egy külön neki szánt hazugságot. Éppen ezért most már új feladatunk van, közös európai szabályozást kell alkotnunk, azonnal le kell állítani a mesterséges szuperintelligencia fejlesztését és a jelenlegi AI-fejlesztéseket pedig érdemben lassítani kell egészen addig, amíg ki nem dolgozzuk közösen a védelmi rendszereket, mert az AI rossz kezekben veszélyt jelent a biztonságunkra, és veszélyt jelenthet a demokráciánkra is. Sőt, ha elszabadul, ha elveszítjük felette az irányítást, akkor veszélyt jelenthet akár az életünkre is.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, during the last debate on the EU Democracy Shield, I gave you a copy of Nineteen Eighty-Four. Not as a manual, but as a warning.

Today, I remind you again: free citizens do not need permission to think for themselves. People have the right to impart information and to decide for themselves whether that information is true, foolish or credible. They also have the right to challenge information, to debate it, and even to ridicule it.

Because free speech is not the freedom to hear only what someone in authority has decided is true. I do not want to live in a democracy that is frightened of its own citizens. I am not interested in freedom of speech with an asterisk attached and I do not accept that democracy is somehow strengthened by giving authorities even greater influence over what people say, read or believe.
Democracy is sometimes noisy, offensive, inconvenient. Good: that is what freedom sounds like, and that is the freedom we Patriots will continue to defend, whether the Commission likes it or not.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, hoy damos un paso muy importante con el Escudo Europeo de la Democracia para combatir la desinformación, responder a las injerencias extranjeras y protegernos frente a los ataques híbridos, herramientas que habrían sido muy útiles en mi país, en Ceuta, cuando cerca de 80 000 personas asaltaron la frontera en apenas una hora.

Pero de poco sirven las herramientas si no hay voluntad política para utilizarlas. La frontera se desbordó no porque España o Europa carecieran de medios, sino por falta de previsión y determinación. El ataque híbrido no tuvo éxito no porque quien lo promovió fuera más fuerte que España o Europa, sino porque comprobó que podría actuar prácticamente sin consecuencia.

El Escudo es un buen primer paso, pero solo eso: ahora hay que pasar del papel a la acción. Europa tiene medios suficientes para dejar claro que atacar o presionar a un Estado miembro tiene un coste muy elevado. Debemos asegurarnos de que todos nuestros vecinos sean conscientes de ello.
Europa no debe permitir que una invasión como esta que se acaba de producir en Ceuta vuelva a repetirse.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, I truly cannot understand – watching at you, the right side of this House – how you can be against this report and all of the findings and recommendations of the European Democracy Shield? Who are you protecting? Tell us.

Europe needs an efficient shield against modern and extremely dangerous measures of attacking our democracy, its institutions and values. Our citizens need a protection, efficient protection. We are at war with those who want to destroy our democracy, with those who are interested in our weakness, our division and, finally, destruction of the single market and our Union. This is a critical moment for us.

The Russian totalitarian regime does not only fight in a hybrid and cyber way. They are at our borders. A Russian drone has just struck a passenger train on a Polish border. Don't you know that? Who are you protecting?

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, abbiamo bisogno di regole, di vigilanza, di uno scudo per combattere disinformazione, attacchi ibridi e interferenze. La difesa della democrazia è la difesa dell'Europa.
Con l'avvento delle piattaforme digitali, miliardi di persone vengono escluse dal flusso informativo in base a decisioni di un ristretto gruppo di tecnocrati.

Chi decide cosa vediamo, cosa leggiamo, cosa diventa virale? Un algoritmo e quell'algoritmo non è neutrale: è opaco. Ecco perché non basta rincorrere ogni singola fake news. Dobbiamo avere il coraggio di intervenire sui meccanismi che consentono alla disinformazione e alle interferenze straniere di diffondersi su scala industriale.
La sfida democratica del XXI secolo si gioca qui. Per questo servono sovranità digitale europea, trasparenza degli algoritmi, piattaforme più responsabili.

Con l'avvento delle piattaforme digitali, miliardi di persone vengono escluse dal flusso informativo in base a decisioni di un ristretto gruppo di tecnocrati.

Chi decide cosa vediamo, cosa leggiamo, cosa diventa virale? Un algoritmo e quell'algoritmo non è neutrale: è opaco. Ecco perché non basta rincorrere ogni singola fake news. Dobbiamo avere il coraggio di intervenire sui meccanismi che consentono alla disinformazione e alle interferenze straniere di diffondersi su scala industriale.

La sfida democratica del XXI secolo si gioca qui. Per questo servono sovranità digitale europea, trasparenza degli algoritmi, piattaforme più responsabili.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, commissaris, beschermen wij onze democratie tegen echte buitenlandse dreigingen, cyberaanvallen uit Rusland en China en aanvallen op onze kritieke infrastructuur? Juist daarom mogen we onze democratie niet uithollen onder het mom van bescherming. Dit verslag overschrijdt een grens.

EU fact-checkers, een Europees centrum voor democratische weerbaarheid met eigen personeel, budget en monitoringmacht. Brussel schuift zo steeds dichter naar controle over het vrije debat en over onze nationale verkiezingen.
Samenwerking tegen buitenlandse inmenging? Ja. EU-inmenging in nationale verkiezingsdebatten en nog meer EU-uitgaven? Nee.

Verzwak onze parlementaire democratie niet van binnenuit. Democratie wordt weerbaar door te luisteren naar kiezers, niet door extra Brusselse regels en geldstromen. Nationale verkiezingen blijven een soevereine nationale bevoegdheid.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Az Európai Néppárt és baloldali szövetségeseik mindent megtesznek azért, hogy a nemzeti választásokba való brüsszeli beavatkozást intézményesítsék. Ezt hívják önök cinikusan demokráciapajzsnak. Az önök terve a demokratikus értékek legfontosabb pontját hagyta ki, és nem véletlenül. Hogy hogyan biztosítanák a szólásszabadságot és a vélemény pluralizmust. Helyette több milliárd eurót terveztek be a következő uniós költségvetésbe, ebből tömik majd tovább a balliberális sajtót és erősítik tovább a már létrehozott európai cenzúrahálózatot, amelynek a működése homályos, fellebbezésnek pedig nincsen helye. Józan ésszel mindenki számára világos, hogy ez mélyen antidemokratikus, és ellentétes az európai értékekkel is. Ez valójában egy dologról szól, a brüsszeli globalista elit kritikusainak elhallgattatásáról. Ha tényleg meg akarnák védeni a demokráciát, akkor nyilvánosságra hoznák az EU-s NGO- és médiatámogatási szerződéseket. Erről is szavazni fogunk.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, democracy cannot defend itself if we leave its digital infrastructure in the hands of private interests without transparency or accountability. This is why the Regulation on political advertising must be firmly enforced, Commissioner.

It tells citizens who is trying to influence them, who is paying for the advert, and how their personal data are used to target them. These are not bureaucratic details. These are democratic safeguards. Protecting personal data is not an obstacle to political debate. It protects citizens from domestic manipulation and foreign interferences.

And we should say it very clearly to Meta and other big tech companies who come also to your office, Commissioner, that lobbying against these rules is totally unacceptable. European democracy is not negotiable, so no retreat, no regulatory blackmail. Our rules, our democracy, our sovereignty.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señor comisario, usted nos habla de Rusia como amenaza a nuestra democracia, estamos de acuerdo, pero ¿qué pasa con la amenaza de la internacional reaccionaria dirigida por Trump y Netanyahu? Fue Trump quien amenazó con invadirnos en Groenlandia y son Trump y Netanyahu quienes tienen un aparato digital de desinformación.

¿Cuántas elecciones —aquí y fuera— se han decidido bajo la influencia de esa máquina de desinformación? ¿Cuántos de los escaños de los ultras —que están ahí— se habrían conseguido sin esa máquina de desinformación?
Hemos visto el caso de Cerimedo, detenido por intentar asesinar a su mujer, y todas las granjas de VOX que trabajan por los ultras, que están ahí. ¿Cuántas personas que están ahí no habrían estado?

Por eso nos hablan del totalitarismo, porque ellos quieren el totalitarismo de Putin, Trump y Netanyahu. Antes lograban el poder con golpes de Estado —Bolsonaro y Trump lo intentaron—, ahora lo hacen con la máquina de desinformación. Y lo estamos viendo en Ceuta: cómo la internacional reaccionaria intenta derribar al único Gobierno de izquierdas que queda en Europa y les planta cara.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Es ist schön, wie groß die Einigkeit hier im Haus ist, dass Demokratie und Rechtsstaatlichkeit geschützt werden müssen. Ich sage Ihnen, wo sie am meisten Schutz braucht. Sie braucht am meisten Schutz in Deutschland, wo der Opposition fundamentale Rechte vorenthalten werden. Sie braucht Schutz in Ungarn, wo eine neue Regierung einen Unrechtsstaat sondergleichen installiert. Sie braucht Schutz in Frankreich, wo eine Präsidentschaftskandidatin unter fadenscheinigen Gründen eventuell einen Wahlkampf im Hausarrest machen muss.
Die Demokratie in Europa muss geschützt werden. Und sie muss vor allem geschützt werden gegen die Parteifreunde derjenigen, die glauben, uns hier etwas vom Schutz der Demokratie erzählen zu können.

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedající, kolegové, já se nestačím divit, co všechno jste někteří z vás byli schopni zahrnout do zjištění a doporučení zvláštního výboru pro Evropský štít pro demokracii. Totiž vaše snahy omezovat veřejnou debatu jsou již dlouho známé. A že se tedy dočtu o potřebě ještě víc cenzurovat, s tím jsem tak trochu počítala. Ale že přijdete s tím, že musíme v kybernetické válce přejít do ofenzívy a podnikat hybridní akce proti některým státům, to tedy překvapilo i mě. Nebo tvrzení, že naše demokracie je ohrožena narativem, že se některé evropské země dopouštějí neokolonialismu v západní Africe, kterého se například Francie zcela očividně dopouští.

Pokud chcete bránit demokracii, tak nepotřebujeme žádné středisko pro odolnost demokracie. Hlavní ohrožení pro demokracii neleží v zákeřných aktérech mimo Evropskou unii a ochrana demokracie nepotřebuje být militarizována. Hlavní nebezpečí pro demokracii představují ti, kteří omezují svobodnou diskusi, kteří nechávají potlačit pokojné demonstrace a kteří se snaží nepohodlné politiky vyřadit z veřejného prostoru. A také samotný systém, kde miliardáři mají v pozadí větší vliv na běh států než řadový občan.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Ma felszólalt ebben a Házban a Fidesz egyik képviselője, aki 2014 és 24 között az előző magyar kormányban dolgozott, 2015-től a legmagasabb szinten a Miniszterelnöki Kabinetiroda államtitkáraként. Egy olyan ember panaszkodik a demokrácia leépítése miatt, akinek a kormánya orosz módszerekkel üldözte a sajtót, orosz módon használta a titkosszolgálatokat az ellenzéki pártok megfigyelésére, a külügyminisztere pedig telefonon jelentett Szergej Lavrovnak az uniós egyeztetésekről. És csak egy plusz példa, amikor az orosz hackerek feltörték a magyar külügyi szolgálatok összes szerverét, és hozzáfértek minden szenzitív információhoz, az akkori magyar külügyminiszter még csak be sem hívatta az orosz nagykövetet, miközben az orosz külső hírszerzés fiának adott letelepedési engedélyt Szergej Nariskin fiának. Ne szolgálják az orosz érdekeket! A magyar emberek nem véletlenül zavarták el önöket. Szolgáljanak magyar érdeket, és az Európai Uniót is támogassák!

Is it 'racist' to notice that in Europe, migrants from the Middle East and Africa are vastly overrepresented in sexual crime? Is it Islamophobic to not want to get a knife in your neck while someone shouts 'Allahu Akbar'?
No, it is not. It is about wanting to get Europe back.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, this report worries me.

It rightly condemns American sanctions on a former commissioner for a lack of any process and punishing him for merely doing his job. It rightly condemns Russia's blacklist of MEPs, officials and others as arbitrary and a breach of mutual respect between our jurisdictions.
But it also goes on to ask us to sanction EU politicians and lobbyists who are judged to be working for other countries without any mention of any process, no rule of law, no process whatsoever.

And the Council has already begun sanctioning the European Union's own citizens without any process, without any recourse to courts: no charge, no trial, no hearing, accounts frozen – including those of spouses – travel bans, livelihoods gone and mort civile.

I agree, colleagues, that our democracy is under threat. But if we become that which we criticise and that which we oppose, then those threats have won. We lose our way if we adopt the policies and the way of our enemies, we must be resolute in defence of the rule of law and not adopt these willy-nilly sanctions. Lastly ...

paragraphs.text: Madam President, thank you very much. Again, can I thank the rapporteur, Tomas Tobé, and all of the colleagues who contributed to the work of this report. Unsurprisingly, we have heard a diversity of opinions and views, and that itself is the essence of democracy. Once this Chamber comes to a democratic view in relation to this report, the Commission stands open to further engagement with Parliament in relation to the recommendations.
In relation to the democratic centre that we have set up, participation by all of the Member States, which we currently enjoy, is voluntary in nature. We fully respect the allocation of competences.

Can I say, finally, Madam President, that we should not be naive to the reality that the European Union is facing a threat to its democracy, because there are actors in the world who see our democracy as a threat to their authoritarian regimes and way of life.

Yes, we want democracy to be noisy, to be vibrant, to be about debate and about disagreement, to be about diversity of thought and of opinion. But fundamentally, we need to ensure that all of our citizens in the EU enjoy the privilege of participating in free and fair elections that are free of any interference and disinformation. Thank you very much for your consideration.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, let me conclude with one simple point. The threats to our democracies are not going away. Russia will continue to test our resilience. Other hostile actors will continue to look for weaknesses. And technology will continue to give them ways to exploit divisions in our societies.

We must be better prepared. We need the political will to protect our election. We need the capacity to identify foreign interference. We need to protect critical infrastructure and strengthen cooperation in Member States. And perhaps above all, we need to protect the trust in our democratic institutions.

I heard during the debate today that we are talking about freedom of expression. And let me be very clear: we shall have a vibrant political debate all over Europe like we have just had in this plenary today.

But let me be very clear: Russian troll factories, Russian bots are not free speech. And the far right needs to answer the question: why is it so important to protect these Russian troll factories and bots? They are designed to try to influence Europe.

It is extremely important that we remain open, but not naïve. We must remain democratic, but not defenceless. So let us make sure now that European democracy is not only worth defending, but it should also be strong enough to defend itself.
Thank you to all the pro-European groups. Today we send a clear signal: we will protect European democracy.

paragraphs.text: Kinga Gál (PfE), írásbanA Patrióták számára a tagállami szuverenitás és a véleménynyilvánítás szabadsága a demokrácia alapja. Az Európai Demokráciapajzsot a demokrácia védelmének eszközeként mutatják be. Ez az állítás hamis, hiszen ez sokkal inkább pajzs a valódi demokrácia ellen. Lehetőséget adhat az Európai Bizottságnak arra, hogy beavatkozzon a tagállamok belügyeibe, és fellépjen a brüsszeli fősodort megkérdőjelező politikai erőkkel szemben.A külföldi beavatkozás elleni küzdelem ürügyén a migrációról, Európa versenyképességének hanyatlásáról vagy az elhibázott szankciókról megfogalmazott legitim véleményeket is „dezinformációnak” minősíthetik az uniós pénzekből finanszírozott tényellenőrök és civil szervezetek. Kiválasztásuk, finanszírozásuk és elszámoltathatóságuk mindeközben továbbra is átláthatatlan. Ez nem a demokráciát védené, hanem korlátozná a politikai vitát, és befolyásolná a választási versenyt a tagállamokban. Brüsszel képmutatása különösen szembetűnő: miközben a demokrácia védelméről beszél, hallgat, amikor az új magyar kormánya korlátozza a demokráciát, és megpróbálja kizárni ellenfeleit a demokratikus versenyből.Mi, Patrióták elutasítjuk a központosított brüsszeli véleményellenőrzés és a közvetlen vagy közvetett cenzúra minden formáját. Kiállunk a szabad választások, a nyílt vita és az európai polgárok azon szuverén joga mellett, hogy szabadon mondhassák el véleményüket és az uniós intézmények ideológiai beavatkozása nélkül dönthessenek saját kormányukról.

Az Európai Demokráciapajzsot a demokrácia védelmének eszközeként mutatják be. Ez az állítás hamis, hiszen ez sokkal inkább pajzs a valódi demokrácia ellen. paragraphs.text: Sandra Kalniete (PPE), in writingIn recent months, Russia has radically changed its playbook. It no longer only spreads lies through AI-enabled networks across our platforms. It sabotages cables, attacks weapons factories, threatens and carries out assassinations, jams aviation, flies drones over our airports, pushes migrants across our borders and pays criminals inside our Union to do its dirty work.This is not propaganda anymore. It is operational, active and increasingly aggressive—testing our resilience, probing our weaknesses and looking for ways to extend its war beyond Ukraine.Europe has been too slow to respond. For too long, fear of provoking Moscow has led to hesitation. But the Kremlin sees hesitation as weakness.The Democracy Shield must therefore deliver more than awareness. We need enforcement, resources and stronger mandates. Europol should be able to proactively investigate foreign-directed hybrid operations and help prosecute cross-border sabotage. Frontex must have the tools to respond proactively when migration is weaponised.And we need a stronger focus on the Eastern Flank: faster Eastern Flank Watch, tougher sanctions, including against Russia’s shadow fleet, and adequate funding to counter FIMI.Europe must deter—not merely react.

paragraphs.text: Urmas Paet (Renew), kirjalikultVälissekkumine ja desinformatsioon tähendavad rünnakut ühtse Euroopa vastu ning selle peamised ohvrid on tavalised eurooplased. Peame kaitsma oma demokraatiat välisriikidest lähtuva mõjutustegevuse eest. Euroopa Liidu jaoks on peamine välisoht Venemaa, aktiivsed on ka Valgevene, Hiina, Iraan ja Põhja-Korea. Sõnavabadus ei tähenda Vene juturobotite propaganda või välissekkumise lubamist. Ja päris kindlasti ei tähenda sõnavabadus, et välisriigid võivad sekkuda Euroopas toimuvatesse valimistesse. Olukorra parandamiseks peaksid digiplatvormid tõkestama robotite kasutamist valimistesse sekkumiseks. Välissekkumise vastu võitlemiseks tuleks luua spetsiaalne ELi tasandi asutus. Tähtsaim on kaitsta sõltumatut meediat ning võidelda valimistesse sekkumise vastu veebis.

paragraphs.text: Jadwiga Wiśniewska (ECR), na piśmieWybory potrzebują ochrony przed obcą ingerencją. Jednak pod tym pretekstem nie można pozwolić instytucjom unijnym wpływać na krajowe procesy wyborcze.Raport przewiduje nowe mechanizmy monitorowania wyborów, działania w trakcie kampanii, wsparcie dla mediów, organizacji pozarządowych i fact-checkerów. Kto będzie decydował, które treści są wiarygodne, które media zasługują na wsparcie, a które opinie zostaną uznane za dezinformację?Ingerencja w wybory to nie tylko ordynarne fałszerstwa. To też wpływ na środowisko informacyjne, finansowanie wybranych organizacji i ograniczanie zasięgu legalnych poglądów.Rosyjska ingerencja jest realnym zagrożeniem. Ale nie można walczyć z ingerencją zewnętrzną, tworząc mechanizmy ingerencji wewnętrznej.Bezpieczeństwo wyborów: tak. Unijny nadzór nad debatą polityczną: nie.Demokracja należy do obywateli, a nie do instytucji, które chcą za nich decydować.

paragraphs.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.text: – Before the vote:

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, today's vote is not about whether or not to support ETS2. It is about protecting our citizens from its potential impacts as they are already facing high prices of energy.

This legislation will lower the price of ETS2 allowances, but this will not be enough, which is why we agreed during the negotiations that the Commission will come forward with a general assessment of ETS2 next year and work on strengthening the social safeguards. Thank you for your support.

interventions.text:
Mr President, colleagues, today's vote is not about whether or not to support ETS2. It is about protecting our citizens from its potential impacts as they are already facing high prices of energy.

This legislation will lower the price of ETS2 allowances, but this will not be enough, which is why we agreed during the negotiations that the Commission will come forward with a general assessment of ETS2 next year and work on strengthening the social safeguards. Thank you for your support.

paragraphs.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.text: – Before the vote:

paragraphs.text: Sur President, illum se nivvutaw dwar regoli tas-sajd li ġew maqbula reġjonalment biex nipproteġu l-baħar u niżguraw li s-sajjieda Ewropej, jew mhux, jimxu mal-istess regoli. Imma regoli mingħajr infurzar ma jagħtux protezzjoni. Għal sajjied li jinsab waħdu f'nofs il-baħar, il-protezzjoni ma tistax tibqa' wegħda fuq il-karta. Irid jaraha u jrid iħossha.

Iva, qegħdin nimxu 'l quddiem fil-ħidma tagħna diplomatika u teknika f'dawn l-għaqdiet reġjonali. Imma nappella sabiex l-Ewropa ssaħħaħ is-sorveljanza tagħha, inkluż b'investiment f'użu permanenti ta' drones biex bastimenti ta' pajjiżi terzi li qed jistadu illegalment jinqabdu fil-fatt qabel jaħarbu. Is-sajjieda tagħna jridu Ewropa li tinħass preżenti fuq il-baħar, spalla ma' spalla magħhom.

Kollegi, aħna m'aħniex qegħdin hawn biex nimponu liġijiet u multi biss. Qegħdin hawn biex is-sajjieda tagħna ma jħossuhomx weħidhom quddiem kompetizzjoni inġusta. Ħbieb, ejja nkunu Ewropa li tiddefendi lil min qed jimxi mar-regoli, imma wkoll turi snienha kontra min jibqa' jiksirhom.

paragraphs.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.speaker_label: Magnus Brunner, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, thank you very much and sorry for the delay.
Honourable Members, the Commission's proposal provides for the granting of temporary and exceptional autonomous trade measures to Armenian imports into the European Union for a two‑year period.

Should the Commission consider that extending the granting of autonomous trade measures to Armenian imports into the European Union beyond that two‑year period is warranted in view of the situation at that point of time, the Commission will endeavour to submit to the European Parliament and the Council any proposal to that effect no later than six months before the end of the application of this regulation.

paragraphs.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.text: – Before the vote:

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Ja, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen, ich höre schon leichtes Stöhnen, aber dann, wenn es um junge Menschen geht, dann sollten wir jedoch alle aufmerksam zuhören. Denn es ist der Europäischen Union nicht egal, wie es jungen Menschen geht. Zu oft habe ich persönlich gehört: „Komm du erst mal in mein Alter, dann siehst du die Dinge schon ganz anders“. Aber es geht nicht darum, dass junge Menschen erwachsen werden. Es geht darum, dass junge Menschen in ihrer Lebensrealität ernst genommen werden, dass sie einen Platz an unserem Tisch verdient haben. Darum geht es heute. Und darum sollte es auch in der kommenden Jugendstrategie gehen.

Wir sehen, dass viele junge Menschen das Vertrauen in Politik verloren haben und auch in unsere Demokratie. Das haben wir erst bei den jüngsten Wahlen in Sachsen-Anhalt gesehen, als eine rechtsextreme Partei von jungen Menschen massiv Stimmenzuwachs bekommen hat. Und deswegen – deswegen – brauchen wir eine starke Jugendstrategie, die die jungen Menschen ernst nimmt, die nicht polarisiert, die nicht Ängste schürt, sondern die ganz konkret ihre Herausforderungen angeht. Es geht nämlich ganz konkret darum, um steigende Lebenshaltungskosten. Es geht darum, ob Kinder und Jugendliche eine gute Ausbildung erhalten, ob alle die gleichen Chancen haben. Darum geht es. Es geht nicht darum, Angst, Hass und Hetze zu schüren, sondern ganz konkret für junge Menschen an den Herausforderungen zu arbeiten.
Und genau das ...
(Lebhafter Beifall)

Und genau das werden wir mit der kommenden Jugendstrategie machen. Wir haben evaluiert, wie die jetzige Jugendstrategie abläuft und wie wichtig es ist, dass wir genau diese neuen Herausforderungen angehen. Es ist aber auch wichtig, dass die Jugendstrategie nicht nur auf dem Papier besteht, sondern dass sie ganz konkrete Handlungsempfehlungen vorsieht. Dass die Jugendstrategie tatsächlich diesen jungen Menschen eine Zukunftsperspektive eröffnet. Liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen, daran werden wir gemeinsam arbeiten. Ich fordere die Kommission auf, diese Handlungsempfehlungen auch entsprechend umzusetzen.

interventions.speaker_label: Thomas Byrne, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, Commissioner, let me begin by extending my deepest condolences on behalf of the Council to the families of those who died trying to reach Ceuta on the 30 and 31 July.
Those deaths are a stark reminder of the dangers of irregular journeys such as this. Loss of life at this scale is a human tragedy that we need to keep at the forefront of our thoughts.

Faced with such an incredible tragedy, we must continue to work to address the root causes of irregular migration, dismantle smuggling networks and ensure safe, orderly and controlled migration management.

The incident was also an extraordinary challenge for Spain and for the people of Ceuta. The Spanish authorities acted quickly to restore control, and the vast majority of those who crossed irregularly returned to Morocco within 48 hours.

The European Union moved fast to offer support to Spain and to coordinate a unified response. The Presidency, under my colleague Jim O'Callaghan, the Irish Minister for Justice, convened the integrated political crisis response round table, Coreper and an informal videoconference of home affairs ministers.

The message that emerged was unambiguous: the European Union is united in solidarity with Spain and is committed to protecting our external borders against all threats. Ministers also agreed that we need to relentlessly continue fighting migrant smuggling networks, reinforcing returns, strengthening EU borders, building partnerships with third countries and improving situational awareness.
The Presidency remains in close contact with Spain, with the Commission, with the EEAS and EU agencies to monitor the evolution of the situation on the ground.

Ceuta and Melilla are under a special Schengen regime and perform Schengen checks on exit. Spain has confirmed that none of those remaining in Ceuta after crossing irregularly have moved onward or been transferred to mainland Spain. Spain also reinforced maritime barriers, deployed additional law enforcement officers and strengthened reception, registration and return capacity in Ceuta.

interventions.speaker_label: Magnus Brunner, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Minister, Honourable Members, the Spanish city of Ceuta has just over 80 000 inhabitants. In the last two days of July, almost the same amount of people entered illegally from the other side of the border. This was unprecedented, of course. It severely tested the resilience of the people of Ceuta, and I want to assure them of our respect and our sympathy for the challenges they are facing. I also want to express my deepest condolences to the families and friends of those who lost their lives in the attempt to get to Ceuta. This tragic loss of life confirms again what we actually already know – smugglers kill people, and we must do everything we can to stop them.

This was a stress test for our Union, for our system and for our resilience. But most of the people who entered Ceuta illegally went back to Morocco within a matter of hours, and – this is important – nobody entered the Schengen area. Its integrity was preserved. This was the result of the action taken by the Spanish authorities and also the cooperation with Morocco. However, there are many more challenges which are still ahead of us.

Firstly, thousands remain in Ceuta, including more than 2 000 unaccompanied minors. This brings high pressure and also public order challenges on a territory of less than 20 km². A solution must therefore be found as a matter of urgency. For this, our priority is clear: all those who entered illegally and have no right to stay must swiftly return to Morocco. Morocco has made the commitment, which we of course very much welcome, to take back all migrants that arrived illegally to Ceuta. Secondly, we need to step up our efforts to prevent this from happening again.

Before setting out the necessary next steps, let us also recall what our new approach to migration policy has actually achieved already. Building on the Pact on Migration and Asylum, we have opened a new chapter with fair but also firm rules on the screening of people arriving illegally, the border procedure, new return rules, safe countries reforms and other things. We also have an assertive migration diplomacy and stronger external borders. So altogether we have put our European house in order, and the results actually show that it works.

There is a significant decrease in illegal arrivals and asylum applications across the European Union. In the last two years, illegal migration has decreased by more than 50 %. This year alone, we are seeing a further reduction by more than another third already. As a result of all that, asylum applications are following the same trend. In 2025, they were down by 20 %. There are a lot of examples across the European Union where the numbers are at a historic low. Our returns system is of course working much better. Effective return rates are now close to 30 %. This is not enough, but we are working on that and it's definitely getting better. This means that last year around 30 000 more people returned than the year before.

Europe has made significant progress in addressing illegal migration and in getting control back, but the events and the images from Ceuta show that we must double down on our efforts. Both the smugglers and illegal migrants must understand that our Union will step up to defend itself. Most of all, our citizens must be reassured that things are under control, so restoring control and providing support to Spain have been key objectives from day one of the crisis. I have been in close contact with Spain since the very first day, and tomorrow I will be in Madrid again for discussions with ministers Torres, Grande-Marlaska and Saiz. I also had a very useful exchange with the Mayor-President of Ceuta, Juan Jesús Vivas, last week, and we have now set up a coordination mechanism with Spanish authorities and EU agencies for regular exchanges to assist Spain there as well.

EU support has also become very concrete. Last week, after Spain's request in late August, the Commission granted EUR 114.7 million in emergency assistance. This will reinforce border surveillance and protection, border security infrastructure, as well as the deployment of additional staff and equipment. It will also serve to set up facilities for screening, assistance for unaccompanied minors in the city and to support returns from Ceuta.

Furthermore, Frontex, Europol and the Agency For Asylum are also going to increase their operational support and presence, as requested by Spain in late August. Of course, we will not and cannot stop here. We will continue insisting on the full implementation of the Pact and, in addition, we will work on key areas set out by President von der Leyen. First of all, to prevent illegal migration, migration diplomacy is key. There, I think we will reinforce our comprehensive approach using incentives, using leverages also including funding, including trade. Visa policy is very important there. And when it comes to Morocco, we are committed to continuing to work together on the returns of those remaining in Ceuta.

More efforts, of course, have to be made when it comes to illegal departures, when it comes to fighting smuggling, ensuring effective returns and readmission. In addition, we have been actively coordinating with major online platforms to combat disinformation in relation to the events in Ceuta.

The second important point is that we will reinforce the external borders with a stronger Frontex to make it more agile and faster in anticipating and responding to events. A third point, we will improve early warning and situational awareness with the better monitoring of what happens online, especially because the mobilisation happens very fast. A strengthened Frontex will need to work on this too.

The fourth point, we will continue fighting against smugglers. We made a lot of progress already with the Global Alliance to Counter Migrant Smuggling, and now it is time to agree on new EU rules. So I call on you all to speed up the work on the anti-smuggling directive tabled already three years ago. It's really time to get that done. The last point, we will step up on returns. This is important with the new Return Regulation, which will be in force soon. There is also the revision of the Frontex mandate will be key.

Let me be clear. Ceuta's borders and every Member States borders are European borders. The Commission is definitely ready to do everything possible to support Member States in protecting those borders. We need to learn our lessons from Syria to close gaps, control our borders, preserve the Schengen area. Our work needs to continue to implement the Pact rules. Cooperation with our neighbours is also important, as is always defending our interests.
We will also reinforce our toolbox so that we can deal with similar events more effectively and swiftly, and there I count on the Parliament's support for the work ahead of us. Thank you.

interventions.speaker_label: Jeroen Lenaers, on behalf of the PPE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PPE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, for the EPP, today's debate is about a simple yet important message – and this is a message for the people of Ceuta: Ceuta is Spain, Ceuta is Europe, and we stand with you.
The sovereignty and territorial integrity of Member States are non-negotiable, borders are non-negotiable, and order must be restored, so that the people of Ceuta can return to their normal lives.

Because when Europe's external border is breached at such an unprecedented scale, this is not simply a Spanish problem, it is a European security challenge. And the warnings were there. The declassified documents make this very clear. Police and intelligence services did their job. The government failed to act.

Now, Prime Minister Sánchez is asking for solidarity in a crisis, after continuously resisting the common tools needed to prevent one: opposing more effective measures at the European level, like the returns regulation; initiating unilateral mass regularisations, even though agreements in Europe are there to not do so.

It's an interesting approach. But let us be very clear. Solidarity is needed, and our solidarity is first and foremost with the citizens of Ceuta. The European Commission did its part. It offered Spain support from day one. Yet it took weeks before the Spanish Government formally requested that European support – which is, quite frankly, unbelievable.

Now, we've had experience. We've seen instrumentalisation and weaponisation before: in Greece, in Poland, in the Baltic states and in Finland. But what is new is the scale and the fact that it is now happening on Europe's southern flank.

So what do we need to do? Three points. First, strengthen Frontex. Two, we need a genuine European emergency mechanism – Member States need exceptional tools to deal with exceptional situations. Third, implement what we already agreed. The Pact is there: screening, border procedures, solidarity, effective returns. They must work in practice, not just on paper.
Our goal is simple. Instead of debating the next crisis after it happens, let us make sure we are ready to prevent it.
