interventions.speaker_label: Marta Kos, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, the past weeks have reminded us of how difficult it remains to confront one of the darkest chapters of recent European history and the immense suffering caused by the wars in the former Yugoslavia, where I come from.

The European Union stands in solidarity with all victims of those war crimes, survivors and their families. Stability and prosperity in the Western Balkans are in Europe's strategic interest. Serbia has a central role and responsibility in this regard. By applying for EU membership, Serbia committed to our standards, principles and values. The European Commission has been clear that the glorification of war criminals, genocide denial and revisionism are fundamentally incompatible with these values. They have no place in the EU. They have no place in the EU candidate countries.

Last year in Srebrenica, I witnessed the burial of seven more victims. Thirty years after the genocide, many are still missing and their families continue to suffer unimaginable pain. It is incomprehensible that anyone responsible for such crimes should be honoured as a hero.

The images from Ratko Mladić's funeral were profoundly disturbing. They show a failure to confront the past and contradict the values at the heart of European integration. It was especially disturbing to see Serbian ministers, state officials and military representatives, alongside leaders and politicians from Republika Srpska, attend the funeral and publicly honour a war criminal.

The European Commission calls on the Serbian authorities, as well as all actors in the region, to contribute to reconciliation and good neighbourly relations. Stop using the past as a barrier to the future, and start genuine reconciliation, so that all countries of the region can build a peaceful and prosperous future together in the European Union without hatred and conflict.

I thank you, dear Members of the European Parliament, that you care. But the images we have seen do not represent Serbian society as a whole. Numerous citizens from Serbia and the region wrote to me, rejecting the glorification of war criminals. This is why I know that Serbia is much more. Serbia is its people. It is its young generation, its entrepreneurs, its civil servants, its artists, its journalists – citizens who want their country to move forward, who want to confront the past, who want to live in a free, democratic and European country. That Serbia deserves to be heard. That Serbia deserves to be supported. And that Serbia has a place in Europe.

Being a friend of Serbia also means being honest with Serbia. We can disagree about politics. We can have difficult conversations about reforms and about Serbia's European path. But we cannot negotiate about the dignity of the victims of genocide and war crimes. Europe will never ask Serbia to deny its identity or its history, but Europe will ask Serbia to confront its history honestly, including its darkest chapters. Because I remain deeply convinced that progress on Serbia's EU path is in our shared interest. The Commission will therefore continue to do everything in its power to support Serbia's European path.

interventions.speaker_label: Davor Ivo Stier, u ime kluba PPE.

paragraphs.text: Poštovani predsjedavajući, unatoč svim upozorenjima Ratko Mladić je pokopan uz vojne počasti.

Zbog žrtava Srebrenice ne možemo umanjiti odgovornost srpskih vlasti, a niti zbog Mladićevih žrtava na tlu EU-a, u hrvatskoj Škabrnji, Kijevu, Vrlici, Šibeniku, Zadru. Zbog svih tih žrtava ne možemo niti olako prijeći preko uvreda upućenih čelnicima i građanima susjednih zemalja, europskoj povjerenici za proširenje, našim institucijama u cjelini.

U vječitom balansiranju između Europe i njenih neprijatelja, srpski predsjednik je odlučio ne ići na pogreb, ali ipak poslati vlastitog sina i ministre. Odlučio je ne uključiti sve elemente državnog pogreba, ali je ipak kao vrhovni zapovjednik izravno odgovoran za vojne počasti Mladiću.

Dakako, mediji pod kontrolom vlasti su se pobrinuli da najotvorenije veličaju Ratka Mladića. Tome se, nažalost, pridružio i patrijarh Srpske pravoslavne crkve. Ovo je stanje duha u Srbiji, ne samo kod vlasti, nažalost i kod dijela društva pa i oporbe.

Na građanima Srbije je da odluče kakvu zemlju žele, ali na nama je da odlučimo kako će se EU postaviti. Nemamo iluzije da će proraditi svijest onih koji su i devedesetih bili inertni, ali zato mi u Parlamentu moramo biti još glasniji i reći da je dosadašnja politika EU-a bila mlaka i neučinkovita.

Trebamo jasno poručiti i odlučiti da nema mjesta u europskoj obitelji za one koji veličaju Ratka Mladića, a ne treba biti niti europskog novca za one koji se ne žele distancirati od politike Slobodana Miloševića.

Srpski građani imaju pravo na europsku perspektivu i ne bismo htjeli da se Mladićem pokopa europska budućnost, ali toj europskoj perspektivi nećemo pomoći gledajući kroz prste onima koji slave Mladića.
Vojne počasti Mladiću bile su velika greška. Njegove žrtve su zaslužile našu solidarnost, ali i to da EU povuče sve potrebne poteze.

Zbog žrtava Srebrenice ne možemo umanjiti odgovornost srpskih vlasti, a niti zbog Mladićevih žrtava na tlu EU-a, u hrvatskoj Škabrnji, Kijevu, Vrlici, Šibeniku, Zadru. Zbog svih tih žrtava ne možemo niti olako prijeći preko uvreda upućenih čelnicima i građanima susjednih zemalja, europskoj povjerenici za proširenje, našim institucijama u cjelini.

U vječitom balansiranju između Europe i njenih neprijatelja, srpski predsjednik je odlučio ne ići na pogreb, ali ipak poslati vlastitog sina i ministre. Odlučio je ne uključiti sve elemente državnog pogreba, ali je ipak kao vrhovni zapovjednik izravno odgovoran za vojne počasti Mladiću.

Dakako, mediji pod kontrolom vlasti su se pobrinuli da najotvorenije veličaju Ratka Mladića. Tome se, nažalost, pridružio i patrijarh Srpske pravoslavne crkve. Ovo je stanje duha u Srbiji, ne samo kod vlasti, nažalost i kod dijela društva pa i oporbe.

Na građanima Srbije je da odluče kakvu zemlju žele, ali na nama je da odlučimo kako će se EU postaviti. Nemamo iluzije da će proraditi svijest onih koji su i devedesetih bili inertni, ali zato mi u Parlamentu moramo biti još glasniji i reći da je dosadašnja politika EU-a bila mlaka i neučinkovita.

Trebamo jasno poručiti i odlučiti da nema mjesta u europskoj obitelji za one koji veličaju Ratka Mladića, a ne treba biti niti europskog novca za one koji se ne žele distancirati od politike Slobodana Miloševića.

Srpski građani imaju pravo na europsku perspektivu i ne bismo htjeli da se Mladićem pokopa europska budućnost, ali toj europskoj perspektivi nećemo pomoći gledajući kroz prste onima koji slave Mladića.

Vojne počasti Mladiću bile su velika greška. Njegove žrtve su zaslužile našu solidarnost, ali i to da EU povuče sve potrebne poteze.

Podpredseda

interventions.speaker_label: Tonino Picula, u ime kluba S&D.

paragraphs.text: Poštovani predsjedavajući, poštovana povjerenice, kolegice i kolege, od Škabrnje, preko opsade Sarajeva do Srebrenice, u Hrvatskoj i Bosni i Hercegovini se komemoriraju neki od najgorih zločina počinjenih na europskom tlu nakon Drugog svjetskog rata. A iza tih zločina stoji onaj koji je pred Međunarodnim sudom u Haagu osuđen za genocid i zločine protiv čovječnosti. Zato ne smijemo šutjeti o njegovom sramnom ispraćaju.

Ali pogreb Mladića je medij preko kojeg se još jednom identificirala ukupna politika službenog Beograda. Ispraćaj ratnog zločinca ne govori samo o potpuno neprihvatljivom odnosu prema nedavnoj i tragičnoj prošlosti, nego o tome u kom pravcu ta vlast usmjerava Srbiju danas.

Vučić je jednog ratnog zločinca ispratio s državnim počastima, a s drugim je, Šešeljem, dogovorio predizborni savez. Mi se u Europskoj uniji kontinuirano borimo protiv lažnih vijesti i dezinformacija, ali moramo se boriti protiv povijesnog revizionizma i relativizacije zločina.

Ako već srbijanska vlast programirano luta, Europska unija treba prestati lutati u odnosu prema takvoj vlasti, ne smije se izolirati od činjenica koje jasno govore da Vučićevoj Srbiji nije mjesto u Europskoj uniji. Ratni zločinac Ratko Mladić je pokopan, ali s njim nisu pokopane ideje o velikoj Srbiji, odnosno tzv. srpskom svijetu. S Mladićem moraju biti pokopane iluzije o nekoj europskoj Srbiji pod današnjom vlasti.
Zato je potpuno opravdano postaviti pitanje treba li Europska unija uopće nastaviti pregovore sa Srbijom dok ima ovakvu vlast.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Thierry Mariani, au nom du groupe PfE.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, tous les crimes de guerre doivent être condamnés sans la moindre réserve et sans la moindre ambiguïté. C'est le cas pour Ratko Mladić, dont les agissements ont justifié sa condamnation devant le Tribunal pénal international.

Mais, Madame le Commissaire, une condamnation unanime que l'Union européenne oublie de brandir quand l'Ukraine de monsieur Zelensky célèbre les collaborateurs nazis et antisémites notoires comme Stepan Bandera ou Andriy Melnyk. Sur ce cas, ce Parlement garde le silence et les protestations de la Pologne et du Mémorial de la Shoah de Yad Vashem n'ont rien changé. Silence, d'ailleurs, que ce Parlement avait gardé au moment de l'agression de l'OTAN, quand celle-ci attaquait la Serbie sans mandat de l'ONU.

Voilà donc une complaisance à laquelle la Serbie n'a pas le droit. En deux ans, c'est le troisième débat de ce Parlement européen pour déstabiliser ce pays. Il s'agit, de toute évidence, d'une ingérence étrangère à la veille d'une élection, comme en Géorgie, comme en Moldavie. Hier, Belgrade n'a jamais accepté de prendre ses ordres à Moscou. Pensez-vous que demain, elle acceptera de les prendre à Bruxelles?

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear Commissioner, Ratko Mladić was a war criminal, a convicted war criminal, and he was responsible for genocide. Who does not know that should go to Srebrenica.

We cannot tolerate the celebration of a war criminal. A government that glorifies such atrocities can never be part of the European Union. President Vučić has best relations with China and with Russia. He just wants our money. And I think the colleagues from the EPP really have to cut the ties with his party. Thank you very much, Commissioner Kos, for not going there now. I think we have to stop the financing.

You are completely right: Serbian society, they are Europeans like we are. Serbia should be part of the European Union, but with a democracy. Of course, Vučić held those snap elections because he wants to split society. He wants to have a small majority again to get our money and friendship with Russia, and that cannot happen. The Serbs are welcome here, but their authoritarian regime is not part of the European Union.
Thank you again, Commissioner Kos, for being very strong. Please tell President von der Leyen to be as strong as you are as far as this is concerned.

paragraphs.text: Gospod predsednik! Vladno letalo, vojaki v uniformah, ki nosijo krsto, prisotnost vladnih predstavnikov in slovo z vsemi vojaškimi častmi. To je neposreden pljunek v obraz Evropi, predvsem pa družinam žrtev in vsem dostojnim ljudem. In medtem ko so najvišji predstavniki Evropske unije izražali zaskrbljenost, je zgolj ena oseba zmogla pogum, moč in dostojanstvo ter zavzela stališče na primeren način. Izkazovanje državniških časti vojnemu zločincu je nesprejemljivo in nedostojno, predvsem pa nima nič opraviti z evropskimi vrednotami.

Zato se zahvaljujem komisarki Kos za obrambo dostojanstva in časti Evropske unije ter zaščito spomina žrtev Ratka Mladića. Za Evropsko ljudsko stranko pa imam samo eno vprašanje: kje je vaša rdeča črta? Ali mora SNS storiti še kaj, da vas bo prepričala, da je prišel čas, ko z njimi več ni mogoče sodelovati?
Genocid in vojni zločini ne smejo imeti ideološkega predznaka, zato besede obžalovanja tokrat ne bodo dovolj.

paragraphs.text: Урсула фон дер Лайен и други висши евробюрократи се оплакаха, че изпаднали в шок, когато видели кадрите от Белград с поклонението пред Ратко Младич. Ама много избирателно изпадате в шок, скъпи брюкселски чиновници.

Напоследък в Украйна имаше редица случаи на възхвала на нацистки престъпници, но от ваша страна ни дума, ни вопъл, ни стон. На 25 май тази година с тържествен ритуал и в присъствието на президента Зеленски в Киев беше препогребан Андрей Мелник, създател на Организацията на украинските националисти и сътрудник на нацистка Германия. Тогава никакво възмущение нямаше нито от страна на Урсула, нито на Кая, нито от Вас, г-жо Кос.

Малко по-късно Зеленски даде на една военна част името на украинско подразделение, чиито членове също са сътрудничили на нацистите и са участвали във волинските кланета. И този път брюкселските началници не изпаднаха в шок. Радват се те на любителите на нацистите и на нациста Зеленски и му пращат още милиарди евро, за да продължава с тези церемонии.
За голямо съжаление именно тези двойни стандарти се превърнаха в запазена марка на Европейския съюз.

interventions.speaker_label: Marta Kos, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, when we talk about Serbia today, we talk also about our Europe.

Reconciliation led the ground for the European Union because French and German leaders decisively turned the page of history and healed the most painful wounds their societies were facing. It is the reason why we are all here today.

The countries of the Western Balkans can decide, of course, to overcome divisions and build a common future. This must include Serbia. We must not turn our backs on Serbia and its people who want to live in a free, democratic and European country.

At the upcoming elections, the citizens of Serbia will have the opportunity to decide which path they want to pursue. We expect the elections to be free, fair and transparent in accordance with European and international standards. In late October, on the 28th, the European Commission will present this year's annual enlargement reports. Developments relevant to Serbia's European past will be reflected in our assessment.

Progress remains in the hands of the incoming Serbian Government. I will do all in my powers to ensure that Serbia can advance on its EU path. But I tell you, respect for our values will remain non-negotiable.

paragraphs.text: Mariusz Kamiński (ECR), na piśmieOkropieństwo zbrodni w Srebrenicy wciąż nami wstrząsa, mimo upływu ponad 30 lat. Upamiętnienie z honorami państwowymi człowieka prawomocnie skazanego za ludobójstwo, odpowiedzialnego za śmierć tysięcy niewinnych ludzi, jest niedopuszczalne. Oddanie honorów Ratko Mladiciowi nie było zwykłym elementem ceremonii pogrzebowej. Było publiczną deklaracją władz i elit Serbii, próbą rehabilitacji zbrodniarza i bolesnym ciosem w pamięć jego ofiar. Sposób, w jaki Mladić został pożegnany, mówi nam niestety wiele o dzisiejszym państwie serbskim, o jego elitach politycznych, wojskowych i duchowych, o ich stosunku do tej okropnej zbrodni, ale także o drodze, na którą pchają dziś Serbię. Nie jest to droga europejska. Wręcz przeciwnie. Gloryfikując zbrodniarzy wojennych, Serbia oddala się od Europy.Pani Komisarz słusznie powiedziała, że gloryfikacja zbrodniarzy wojennych, negowanie ludobójstwa i rewizjonizm historyczny są fundamentalnie sprzeczne z europejskimi wartościami. Tak, na takie postawy nie ma miejsca ani w Unii Europejskiej, ani w państwach kandydujących. Ale ta zasada musi obowiązywać wszystkich jednakowo. Musi więc dotyczyć również Ukrainy, gdzie gloryfikowani są przywódcy UPA odpowiedzialni za masowe zbrodnie na Polakach. Nie możemy potępiać rehabilitacji zbrodniarzy w jednym państwie kandydującym, a milczeć, gdy dzieje się to w innym.

Gloryfikując zbrodniarzy wojennych, Serbia oddala się od Europy.Pani Komisarz słusznie powiedziała, że gloryfikacja zbrodniarzy wojennych, negowanie ludobójstwa i rewizjonizm historyczny są fundamentalnie sprzeczne z europejskimi wartościami. Tak, na takie postawy nie ma miejsca ani w Unii Europejskiej, ani w państwach kandydujących. Ale ta zasada musi obowiązywać wszystkich jednakowo. Musi więc dotyczyć również Ukrainy, gdzie gloryfikowani są przywódcy UPA odpowiedzialni za masowe zbrodnie na Polakach. Nie możemy potępiać rehabilitacji zbrodniarzy w jednym państwie kandydującym, a milczeć, gdy dzieje się to w innym.

interventions.speaker_label: Roxana Mînzatu, Executive Vice-President of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, I'm coming directly from the College where we have just adopted our fair labour mobility package.

I'm happy that I can immediately come here to exchange with you on the very important topics of this package. We often say that the single market is one of Europe's best and most important achievements. Almost 20 million Europeans live in another EU country across the border from their work, or are sent abroad temporarily by their employer.

Over the years, we have built detailed rules so that we can protect the rights of these mobile workers, including their access to healthcare, pensions and, overall, social security. Just a few months ago, after ten years of complicated negotiations, we reached an historic agreement to update our social security rules in the European Union. That means that we have made important progress.

But the stories of the people tell us that we still have more barriers to face. People face challenges in getting the protections that they need. Companies, especially SMEs, struggle with complicated procedures in getting access to the talent that they require. Today, we are taking a concrete step to really simplify our internal market and make labour mobility fairer for workers. The fair labour mobility package that we just adopted is composed of six legislative proposals: a regulation establishing the ESSPASS (the European Social Security Pass), a regulation on strengthening the European Labour Authority, the skills portability act, a directive on professional qualifications in the European Union, a delegated directive on physiotherapists and a proposal for a directive for third-country national qualifications.

I would summarise this entire complex legislative package in five messages, if you'll allow me. First, we move from a paper-based to a digitalised labour mobility. Every company, every worker in Europe knows about the lengthy processes to get the famous portable document A1 that is necessary for posting, and how much time and how much money this complicated process costs. With the introduction of the ESSPASS, we fully digitalise the process to request and receive social security documents. We are starting with a portable document A1, and will continue with healthcare, pensions, unemployment and sickness benefits. This is indeed a game-changer because we move from endless paperwork to one mobile phone app with standardised, verifiable, documents that can be checked in real time. That saves time. That saves money for workers, for companies and for authorities.

My second message is that better enforcement through a stronger European labour authority is being delivered. For our businesses to perform and for our workers to be protected, we need to make sure that rules are clear and that rules are actually implemented. This means, firstly, stronger inspections: the European Labour Authority will have better data analysis capacity and should be clearly supported by national inspectorates. Secondly, clear competences on third-country nationals. Migration is a reality in the European Union and when the European Labour Authority performs its controls, they need to be able to inspect the working conditions of migrant workers. It is about combating labour exploitation, about fighting social dumping. Thirdly, we are providing personalised information and counselling through the strengthening of ELA. The Authority will be able to fund organisations that advise workers and employers about their rights and obligations, and this is indeed inspired by fair mobility.

The third big message to you is that wherever you move in Europe, your skills will move with you. And this should be a revolution, a real single market of skills. With the skills portability act, we will digitalise all qualifications from secondary school to PhD level across the European Union. This will be to the benefit of all European citizens. Again, all will be standardised, secured and verifiable in real time in a digital app on mobile phones, and accessible, so people will no longer need to produce and send scanned copies of their qualifications, or pay for the certification of the authenticity of those documents, or run around to obtain the proof of their qualification level.

A fourth message about this package: we deliver on faster recognition of qualifications inside the European Union. Of course, digitising qualifications was the first step. The second is making it easier to access the 5 700 regulated professions that we have in the EU, making it easier for companies to hire talent critically needed, such as engineers, electricians, IT experts. I'm just giving a few examples: today, for an Italian engineer to be able to work in Germany, it takes – and here we look at the legal provisions – at least four months to get their title recognised. For a Spanish nurse to work in Belgium, it takes at least three months. But so many times the wait is much longer and the complexity is much higher, with negative consequences for those professionals and for the economy. With the revision we propose for the Professional Qualification Directive, we accelerate internal mobility for EU nationals by reducing the duration of recognition procedures with clear timelines and deadlines, we create one single interface available in all EU official languages, which is digital and which each citizen can use to apply for recognition in any Member State. And thanks to artificial intelligence, we will also allow citizens to upload their documents in any EU language, while translation will be automatically provided inside that platform.

We then propose to expand the automatic recognition of qualifications to an eighth profession. Today it is about physiotherapists, but we have identified also ten new professions – such as civil engineers, biomedical laboratory technicians, and electricians – for which we will work with Member States so that they too will be covered by automatic recognition. I remind you that, today, only seven professions benefit from automatic recognition.

Fifth and last message: attracting and making the most of the talent of non-EU professionals. Here we have two types of problems: for somebody wants to come from, say, the United States to work in the European Union as an engineer, it will take around 14 months, according to the law, to have their qualifications recognised – or probably more in many parts. At the same time, in Europe, 40 % of highly educated third-country nationals who are already in the European Union are working below their qualification level, which is double than the same indicator for EU nationals. With the proposed directive on the qualifications of third-country nationals, we will create common rules across the European Union to get these qualifications recognised with the same timelines in all Member States with rights to appeal, adaptation measures and the same document requirements. The proposal also includes an EU certification system that will apply to universities outside of the European Union, so that they prove that they do comply with European standards. If they meet the standards, their graduates will be able to work in the European Union in those professions. If not, they won't.

Honourable Members, the message we want to convey with the fair labour mobility package is that wherever you move in the European Union, your social rights are protected and your talent is recognised and, as a consequence, European SMEs and businesses are supported.

I am ready to work with you and with this House right away. I count on your support to take these proposals forward so that they can deliver the concrete results we want for our citizens and for our economy.

interventions.speaker_label: Dennis Radtke, im Namen der PPE-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Frau Kommissarin! Liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Das, was die Kommission jetzt hier gerade vorgestellt hat, hat wirklich das Zeug dazu, ein echter Quantensprung nach vorne zu sein – ein Quantensprung sowohl für Beschäftigte als auch für Unternehmen –, sowie die konsequente Fortsetzung dessen, was wir in den Veränderungen bei der Entsenderichtlinie und bei dem Durchbruch nach fast zehn Jahren bei der Verordnung (EG) Nr. 883/2004 zur Koordinierung der Systeme der sozialen Sicherheit endlich erreicht haben.

Denn das eine ist es – und darum ging es beispielsweise bei den Veränderungen in der Entsenderichtlinie –, Regeln zu ändern, zu mehr Fairness und zu mehr Fairness im Wettbewerb beizutragen. Aber jetzt geht es eben auch darum, die Lücken, die wir vor allen Dingen bei der Rechtsdurchsetzung haben, auch zu schließen. Denn das beste Recht auf dem Papier bringt natürlich wenig bis gar nichts, wenn es nicht durchgesetzt wird, wenn es nicht kontrolliert wird. Und da haben wir, glaube ich, im Fair Labour Mobility Package jetzt wirklich Anknüpfungspunkte.

Dieses Parlament hat sich schon 2024 in der letzten Legislaturperiode sehr, sehr klar positioniert. Wir haben deutlich gemacht, was unsere Erwartungen sind an ein neues ELA-Mandat, gerade auch mit Blick auf Beschäftigte aus Drittstaaten.

Es kann einfach nicht sein, was sich bei uns in Europa auf einigen Baustellen, auf Autobahnen, im Logistikbereich abspielt, wie dort Menschen aus Drittstaaten ausgebeutet werden – das hat ja mit Menschenwürde nichts zu tun, aber das hat auch mit einem fairen Wettbewerb an vielen Stellen nichts zu tun; es kann einfach nicht sein, dass derjenige am Ende der Stärkste im Wettbewerb ist, der am klügsten die Lücken in der europäischen Regelung, die Lücken bei der Kontrolle ausnutzt.

Deswegen hat dieses Paket wirklich Riesenchancen. Auch der Schub bei der Digitalisierung; das macht vieles einfacher, und das muss unser Anspruch sein. Mehr Rechtssicherheit nicht nur für Arbeitnehmer, sondern vor allen Dingen auch: Es muss einfacher werden und schneller werden für die Unternehmen, die sich an die Regeln halten.
In diesem Sinne freue ich mich sehr auf die konkrete Gesetzgebung in den nächsten Wochen und Monaten.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Gabriele Bischoff, im Namen der S&D-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen, werte Frau Exekutivvizepräsidentin, liebe Roxana. Ich möchte erst einmal starten mit einem wirklich großen Lob, Dank und Anerkennung für die Arbeit, für dieses Paket, weil es heute eine gute Nachricht an die über 14 Millionen Beschäftigten ist, die mobil sind innerhalb der EU, dass wir sagen, wir wollen für faire Bedingungen sorgen. Und nach dem guten Ergebnis zur Verordnung (EG) Nr. 883/2004, das ist schon gesagt worden, wollen wir weitere Schlupflöcher schließen, wollen Kontrollen, wollen Informationen in Echtzeit bereithalten. Deshalb begrüßen wir das sehr.

Wir wollen keine Malls of Shame auf dem Rücken von Bauarbeiterinnen und Bauarbeitern. Wir wollen einen funktionierenden Binnenmarkt mit klaren Rechten. Deshalb, der ELA Zähne geben, ist so wichtig – mit Blick auf die Kompetenzen – für Drittstaatsangehörige, aber auch für Risikobewertungen von Unternehmen, damit wir präventiv viel stärker tätig werden können.
Der ESSPASS: Wie lange haben wir im Beschäftigungsausschuss dafür Druck gemacht, damit hier ein konkreter Vorschlag kommt? Über die Pilotprojekte sind wir jetzt da.

Und auch als Drittes: Dass wir den Unternehmen sagen können, die qualifizierte Beschäftigte suchen, und den Beschäftigten, die in Europa einen Job suchen, „das dauert jetzt nicht mehr 100 Jahre, bis ihr die Anerkennung kriegt, wir machen das schneller, effizienter, unbürokratischer, digitaler“, ist eine gute Nachricht. Und dass wir am Ende als Parlament das voll beherzt aufgreifen werden in den Verhandlungen, ist ganz klar. Denn unsere Botschaft ist Arbeitsausbeutung, Sozialdumping darf es ...

Deshalb, der ELA Zähne geben, ist so wichtig – mit Blick auf die Kompetenzen – für Drittstaatsangehörige, aber auch für Risikobewertungen von Unternehmen, damit wir präventiv viel stärker tätig werden können.

Der ESSPASS: Wie lange haben wir im Beschäftigungsausschuss dafür Druck gemacht, damit hier ein konkreter Vorschlag kommt? Über die Pilotprojekte sind wir jetzt da.

Und auch als Drittes: Dass wir den Unternehmen sagen können, die qualifizierte Beschäftigte suchen, und den Beschäftigten, die in Europa einen Job suchen, „das dauert jetzt nicht mehr 100 Jahre, bis ihr die Anerkennung kriegt, wir machen das schneller, effizienter, unbürokratischer, digitaler“, ist eine gute Nachricht. Und dass wir am Ende als Parlament das voll beherzt aufgreifen werden in den Verhandlungen, ist ganz klar. Denn unsere Botschaft ist Arbeitsausbeutung, Sozialdumping darf es ...

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Julie Rechagneux, au nom du groupe PfE.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, depuis des années, vous faites de la mobilité des travailleurs un horizon en soi. Mais à force de vouloir rendre le travail toujours plus mobile, on finit aussi par rendre les salariés toujours plus interchangeables. On connaît déjà les conséquences désastreuses de cette politique: dans plusieurs secteurs le travail détaché a pesé à la baisse sur les salaires et a alimenté une concurrence sociale que nos compatriotes ont directement subie.

Le problème social de la France, ce n'est pas que les Français ne bougent pas assez, c'est qu'on a détruit trop d'emplois là où ils vivent. Et la reconnaissance des qualifications ne doit pas conduire à niveler nos exigences par le bas. La mobilité transfrontalière, certes, fait partie de la vie de nombreux territoires. Elle doit bénéficier à leurs habitants, mais pas devenir un moyen supplémentaire de banaliser le travail détaché.
En résumé, nous n'accepterons jamais votre vision consistant à penser que tous les peuples sont interchangeables dans un immense marché mondial du travail.

interventions.speaker_label: Chiara Gemma, a nome del gruppo ECR.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, signor Commissario, onorevoli colleghi, dietro ogni laboratorio che si sposta da uno Stato membro all'altro c'è una storia fatta di competenze, sacrifici e aspettative.

Il compito delle istituzioni europee dovrebbe essere quello di accompagnare questi percorsi, non di complicarli. Per questo guardiamo con interesse al pacchetto per la giusta mobilità del lavoro: ridurre gli adempimenti amministrativi e favorire procedure digitali più efficienti significa offrire maggiore certezza ai lavoratori e alle imprese che operano oltre i confini nazionali.

Allo stesso modo, facilitare il riconoscimento delle qualifiche significa valorizzare il merito, le competenze e il lavoro delle persone, riducendo gli ostacoli che limitano le opportunità di crescita e occupazione.

Per quanto riguarda l'ELA, il suo valore aggiunto risiede nel coordinamento e nella cooperazione tra amministrazioni nazionali. Eventuali revisioni del mandato dovrebbero preservare il ruolo delle autorità nazionali nell'attività ispettiva e di controllo, nel rispetto dell'equilibrio istituzionale previsto dai Trattati.

La mobilità è una risorsa quando aiuta le persone a mettere a frutto il proprio talento e le imprese e a trovare le competenze di cui hanno bisogno: è questo è il risultato che ci aspettiamo dalle proposte della Commissione.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Renew Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Madam Vice-President, congratulations on the skills portability initiative. I really think that digitalisation and making sure that we can travel with our skills across borders is a step in the right direction.
But it doesn't address the real issue at stake here. And that is trust – simple trust that our European craftsmen are well trained and highly skilled across our borders.

Isn't it strange that when it comes to a bachelor's or a master's, we've all known for years what this degree means – across the borders, every university recognises them from each other – but when it comes to vocational education and training, we don't?

The difference is that the universities have a true European community and the vocationally educated and trained don't. So can we use this initiative to really build on that European community of craftsmen and skilled people? Because a digital certificate only has a value if the qualifications behind it are valued.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, since the elections in Saxony-Anhalt, for the first time I question whether there is a safe future for me and my children in Germany or if we should build a life somewhere else, and I know I'm not the only one feeling this grief seeing fascism rise all over Europe. I worry about the nurse in Italy who may no longer provide reproductive healthcare, about the teacher in Germany who may no longer teach children to question their own history, or about the woman in France who may no longer be allowed to wear the hijab at work. I worry that if someone has the courage to leave their life's work, their diplomas will not be recognised. Worst case, their talent will be lost at the border because they get stuck in an endless admin cycle. Today we talk about the Labour Mobility Package – thank you, Roxana, for that one. We have to see it as a democratic backbone. Yes, it's great for our economy. Yes, it's great for the people's freedom. But in times of nationalism, it's also important for European democracy.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: em nome do Grupo The Left

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, Senhora Comissária Mînzatu, deste pacote de medidas sobre a mobilidade laboral que hoje apresenta, registamos aspetos que podem ser positivos para a valorização dos trabalhadores e o respeito e o cumprimento dos seus direitos. Mas queremos também sublinhar preocupações que temos quanto ao enquadramento destas medidas pela lógica liberal dominante relativamente ao dito mercado de trabalho.

Podem, de facto, ser positivas as medidas que vierem a ser tomadas que contribuam para o combate à precariedade laboral e à subcontratação, para a proteção dos trabalhadores migrantes que são vítimas de exploração e para a aplicação efetiva dos regimes de proteção social dos trabalhadores vigentes em cada Estado‑Membro, bem como as medidas para o reconhecimento mútuo de diplomas, certificados e outras qualificações profissionais ou até as medidas para o reforço da ação inspetiva, desde que isso não implique retirar capacidade operacional às autoridades nacionais competentes nesta matéria.

Mas queremos sublinhar também as preocupações que temos com o enquadramento mais geral, que, de alguma forma, é contraditório em relação a estas medidas. E por isso perguntamos: como é que as intenções proclamadas de valorizar os trabalhadores se articulam com as orientações da União Europeia em matéria laboral, que vão exatamente em sentido contrário, nomeadamente no âmbito do Semestre Europeu?

Como é que a intenção de reforçar os direitos dos trabalhadores se compatibiliza com políticas como, por exemplo, as do 28.º regime jurídico, que se arriscam a nivelar por baixo e a liquidar as medidas da legislação nacional de proteção dos direitos dos trabalhadores? Ou como é que as medidas relacionadas com a proteção social se articulam com o assalto aos sistemas públicos de segurança social que está em marcha por via da União da Poupança e dos Investimentos?

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señora vicepresidenta Mînzatu, la movilidad laboral es uno de los grandes pilares del proyecto europeo, pero debemos sincerarnos: moverse por Europa no siempre es una elección libre para muchos jóvenes; a veces, es la consecuencia de no encontrar oportunidades en su país o en su región, y eso lo conocemos bien en España.

Tenemos una generación preparada, formada y con ganas de trabajar, pero demasiadas veces se encuentra con desempleo, precariedad, dificultades para emanciparse y un mercado laboral que no le ofrece estabilidad. Por eso este paquete es importante, porque cuando un joven decide trabajar, formarse o emprender en otro Estado miembro, Europa debe facilitarle el camino, no llenarlo de obstáculos. Necesitamos que la movilidad funcione de verdad, que las competencias se reconozcan, que los derechos acompañen al trabajador y que cambiar de país no signifique empezar de cero.

Pero no olvidemos lo esencial: la movilidad europea debe ser una oportunidad y no la consecuencia del fracaso de algunos Gobiernos para ofrecer futuro a sus jóvenes. Europa debe abrir las puertas, los Gobiernos deben crear oportunidades y los jóvenes europeos deben poder elegir libremente dónde construir su futuro, sin verse obligados a marcharse por falta de empleo, vivienda o estabilidad.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Madame la Vice-Présidente exécutive, chère Roxana, je tiens à vous remercier car dans une Europe de la dérégulation et du tout à la compétitivité, vos propositions pour une mobilité juste prouvent qu'il est possible et nécessaire d'adapter les législations pour protéger et aussi simplifier la vie des travailleurs. Les 14 millions d'Européens et d'Européennes qui vivent ou travaillent dans un autre État membre comptent sur nous pour sortir de situations parfois pires que Kafka.

On ne peut donc que se réjouir du projet de passeport européen de sécurité sociale, ou des propositions pour sécuriser et faciliter la reconnaissance des qualifications partout en Europe, y compris pour les ressortissants d'États tiers. La libre circulation des travailleurs est un droit et la mobilité une force. Mais elle conduit encore trop souvent à des situations d'exploitation choquantes, particulièrement au regard du projet européen.

Les socialistes et les représentants des travailleurs se sont battus pour obtenir en 2019 la création d'ELA, l'Agence européenne du travail. Cette agence a pour objectif de mettre fin à des systèmes frauduleux complexes, souvent construits à l'échelle de plusieurs États membres. Sept ans après sa création, le constat est clair: il faut renforcer les compétences d'ELA, et en particulier ses pouvoirs d'investigation et d'enquête.

Vos propositions vont dans le bon sens, comme l'accès des données et le renforcement de la collaboration avec les autorités nationales, mais il faut également lui donner une capacité d'initiative, ce qui est nécessaire en cas de situation avérée de violation des droits des travailleurs.
J'espère que nous pourrons ensemble travailler en ce sens.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Madame la Vice-Présidente, merci pour ces propositions pour faciliter la mobilité des travailleurs en Europe. Cette mobilité, c'est une liberté fondamentale de l'Union européenne et peut-être la moins développée. Donc, merci.

C'est une solution à la fois pour répondre aux besoins des secteurs en tension partout dans l'Europe, c'est aussi une offre qui s'ouvre aux jeunes d'aller vivre de nouvelles expériences de vie, plus simplement.

Je salue donc vos propositions, qu'elles soient en matière de sécurité sociale, pour la portabilité des droits de santé, sur les compétences renforcées de l'Autorité européenne et sur la numérisation. Cependant, en la matière, faisons attention notamment aux risques de trucage par l'IA, c'est tout notre sujet de vigilance.

Quand même, un sujet sur la reconnaissance des compétences: oui, on doit reconnaître les qualifications mais, avant tout, il faut reconnaître les diplômes au sein de l'Union européenne – ça a déjà été dit – et particulièrement dans le secteur de la formation professionnelle, de l'apprentissage. Nous attendons donc que cet élément renforce les textes que vous avez présentés.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Pani Komisarz! Szanowni Państwo! Mobilność pracowników jest jednym z fundamentów naszego jednolitego rynku. Dlatego powinniśmy patrzeć na ten pakiet przede wszystkim przez pryzmat jednego pytania: czy ułatwi on ludziom pracę, a przedsiębiorstwom – zatrudnianie w całej Europie? Popieram kierunek zaproponowany przez Komisję. Cyfryzacja zabezpieczenia społecznego, szybsze uznawanie kwalifikacji i skuteczniejsza współpraca państw członkowskich mogą realnie usunąć bariery, z którymi dziś mierzą się pracownicy i firmy.

Jak zawsze diabeł tkwi w szczegółach. W tym wypadku ważne jest, aby zachować właściwy balans. Fair mobility nie może oznaczać więcej biurokracji. Nowe przepisy powinny upraszczać procedury, a nie tworzyć kolejne obowiązki dla pracodawców, pracowników czy administracji. Jeśli wprowadzamy cyfrowe narzędzia, muszą one zastępować papier i dublujące się procedury, a nie tworzyć dodatkową warstwę wymogów.

Potrzebujemy również jasnych i przewidywalnych zasad. Pracodawca powinien wiedzieć, jakie ma obowiązki, pracownik – jakie ma prawa, a państwa członkowskie – kto i za co odpowiada. Naszym celem powinien być prawdziwie europejski rynek pracy, przyjazny dla pracowników i przedsiębiorców. Mniej barier i mniej zbędnych obciążeń, ale więcej mobilności i więcej możliwości.

paragraphs.text: Herr talman! Kommissionären. Vecka efter vecka delar fackligt förtroendevalda exempel på hur oseriösa och kriminella företag utnyttjar arbetare.

Ett färskt exempel rör 29 personer från Uzbekistan som skuldsatt sig för att få arbeta i Europa. Man anställs av ett litauiskt bolag i fjärde entreprenadledet och utstationeras till Sverige. I slutändan blev man blåst på lönen och fick återvända hem med skulder och pantsatta hus. Det är den här verkligheten vi måste bekämpa.

För att lyckas med det måste Europeiska arbetsmyndigheten utvecklas till ett verkligt center för att bekämpa arbetslivskriminalitet. Vi behöver fler gemensamma inspektioner, bättre informationsdelning och gemensam riskanalys. Och vi behöver bättre möjligheter att agera när samma företag och samma metoder återkommer i flera medlemsländer.
Skitföretagen rör sig över gränserna. Då måste vi också kunna göra det.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, doamnă comisar, stimați colegi, am citit mărturia unei tinere care muncește în fiecare vară în turism, într-un alt stat. Vrea să termine o facultate pentru a avea o viață mai bună. Tânăra spunea (și vreau să ascultăm toți): „Ne angajează pentru că suntem mai ieftini.”

În spatele acestor cuvinte sunt zeci sau sute de mii de europeni. Unora li se interzic salariile, li se inventează penalități, sunt cazați în condiții degradante sau umiliți verbal. Asta se întâmplă astăzi cu cetățenii noștri în Uniunea Europeană.

De aceea susțin întărirea Autorității Europene a Muncii, dar vreau ca autoritatea să ajungă efectiv la omul vulnerabil când este abuzat, nu doar la finalul dosarului. În același timp, inițiativa privind recunoașterea abilităților trebuie să le ofere oamenilor șansa de a crește, de a prospera conform calificărilor.

Libera circulație face Europa mai puternică. Da, dar avem obligația să ne asigurăm că omul care muncește într-o altă țară europeană nu o face ca să fie cumpărat mai ieftin. Felicitări doamnei comisar și tuturor colegilor care au muncit la acest pachet.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señora vicepresidenta, la movilidad de una persona debería implicar que sus cualificaciones, competencias y derechos sociales viajen con ella. Por eso este es un paso tan importante, porque demuestra que profundizar en el mercado único y reforzar los derechos sociales no son objetivos incompatibles.

La seguridad social con ESSPASS significa menos burocracia, pero también más garantías para los trabajadores, y es un gran éxito gracias al empeño de los socialistas. La Autoridad Laboral Europea debe ser la garante del empleo seguro y de calidad, combatiendo el fraude. Facilitar el reconocimiento de cualificaciones significa que cambiar de país no te suponga empezar de cero.

Este paquete, junto con el futuro paquete de la Ley de Empleo de Calidad, debe marcar la agenda social de esta legislatura. Completar el mercado único con su dimensión social nos hará mucho más fuertes y más competitivos. Enhorabuena, comisaria. La tarea es ahora nuestra en esta Cámara: trabajar los acuerdos para conseguir mejorar, si cabe, esta propuesta.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Frau Kommissarin! Ein funktionierender Binnenmarkt ist kein theoretisches Konzept. Er muss sich an der Praxis unserer Betriebe messen lassen. Und diese Praxis sieht leider zurzeit so aus, dass jeder zweite Betrieb in Europa nicht die passenden Fachkräfte findet. Das bremst Wachstum, Innovation und vor allem auch den Standort.

Wir müssen die Chancen der Arbeitsmobilität ganz schnell pragmatisch nutzen. Wer Fähigkeiten mitbringt, muss unkompliziert über Grenzen hinweg einsetzbar sein. Aber klar ist auch, dass das bewährte duale Ausbildungssystem nicht unterwandert werden darf. Darüber hinaus garantiert der digitale Sozialversicherungspass faire Regeln, um möglichen Sozialbetrug zu verhindern. Wir wollen echte Erleichterungen für unsere Betriebe statt zusätzliche Nachweispflichten. Machen wir es unseren Betrieben nicht schwer, helfen wir ihnen! Fachkräfte sind schwer zu finden. Setzen wir auf Hausverstand und auf die Stimme der Vernunft.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, dank u wel en dank vicevoorzitter voor de presentatie van uw programma. Eerlijke arbeidsmigratie is heel belangrijk in de Europese Unie, en u heeft zelf ook aangegeven hoe belangrijk arbeidsmigratie is voor werknemers en voor bedrijven.

We zien echter tegelijkertijd ook dat het een keerzijde heeft. We zien dat sommige bedrijven en sommige sectoren, zoals landbouw, transport, toerisme drijven op goedkope arbeid, op uitbuiting van gewone mensen. Werknemers worden tegen elkaar uitgespeeld en bedrijven draaien op zo goedkoop mogelijke arbeid in hun bedrijfsvoering. Daar hebben we een stevige inspectie voor nodig. Die ELA-inspectie moet versterkt worden. Daarom wil ik ook aan u vragen: op wat voor manier ziet u dat de mandaatherziening van de ELA ook daadwerkelijk ervoor zorgt dat het meer tanden krijgt? Dat het ervoor kan zorgen dat het ook over de grenzen heen inspecties kan doen, samen met nationale autoriteiten uiteraard. Dat ook die derdelanders, die werknemers die van buiten de Europese Unie komen, daarbij kunnen worden ondersteund. Om te zorgen dat die uitbuiting voor gewone mensen stopt in de Europese Unie.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, meet Martin, a worker who is ready to go from one European country to another. He crosses the border, but soon hits a wall – social security, paperwork, forms for it all. He finds a new job, but when things go wrong, cross-border enforcement can take far too long. His skills are impressive, his training is great, but recognition leaves him stuck at the gate. A worker can move, but his paper stays still. We call that free movement. But is that the will? 27 systems should not block the way when Europe needs workers to move here today. So, Roxana, free Martin and tear down this wall. Make freedom of movement mean freedom for all. Let workers cross borders without paying the cost, and make our single market single at last.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Welches Europa wollen wir sein? Wollen wir ein Europa, eine Europäische Union sein, die Europäerinnen und Europäer und Menschen darüber hinaus willkommen heißt? Bisher sagt eine OECD-Studie: Nein. Sind wir wirklich der heiße Scheiß in der Europäischen Union, sind wir attraktiv genug? Da reden wir einmal über Bürokratie, aber reden wir auch über eine Willkommenskultur in der Europäischen Union? Was macht uns so attraktiv, abgesehen von Bürokratie oder Bürokratieabbau? Kann ich meine Partnerin mitbringen, meinen Partner? Gibt es eine Schule vor Ort? Und wie ist eigentlich die Stimmung?

Das hat das Wahlergebnis in Sachsen-Anhalt gezeigt. Schon da sieht man, was es wirtschaftlich bedeutet, wenn Faschisten drohen an die Macht zu kommen. Dann ist dieser Standort Deutschland, Sachsen-Anhalt, eben nicht mehr attraktiv. Dann siedel ich da kein Unternehmen an, und dann kommen vielleicht auch keine Kolleginnen und Kollegen mehr.

paragraphs.text: Hr. formand! Det er dejligt, at der nu er kommet et udspil med titlen fair arbejdsmobilitet, men jeg synes, det er ærgerligt, at det er svært at finde noget, som rent faktisk sikrer fairness. Jeg synes også, det er ærgerligt, at udspillet langt hen ad vejen mest består af snak om ting, der allerede er sat i gang.

Det er godt, at vi nu taler om fairness, men det er også nødvendigt med et reelt indhold. Europas arbejdere behøver ikke pæne ord, men en reel handling, og derfor er der mange ting, som kan og skal forbedres, før denne pakke gør det, den påstår, den vil.

Vi skal blandt andet sikre, at håndhævelsen via ESSPASS er koblet sammen med registrering af arbejdsgivere og arbejdspladser, så redskabet reelt kan bruges til at beskytte arbejderne. Også når det gælder styrkelsen af ELA, er det klart, at det vil ske ved hjælp af reelle yderligere værktøjer, herunder en klar forpligtelse til at samarbejde med de faglige organisationer om at bekæmpe social dumping.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, I would like to congratulate you on the fair labour mobility package and in particular on the skills portability initiative. It is a concrete step towards making mobility work better for people across Europe by making qualifications easier to recognise and use across borders.

But if we want this progress to reach everyone, we must also look at those in vocational education and training. Europe is facing serious shortages in many vocational occupations, while VET learners and skilled workers still face barriers when moving across the borders. This is why we are also awaiting the European strategy for vocational education and training. This strategy should be closely linked to the skills portability initiative so that qualifications and skills acquired are fully recognised and portable across Europe.
We now need to make sure that this momentum translates into concrete opportunities for learners and workers across the Union.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, many thanks for the many questions and observations.

I would emphasise ELA – the European Labour Authority – will really have enhanced capacity. I would give just some examples. It will be able to initiate inspections – of course, it has to do so with Member States' inspectors, but this is a reality.

It will have access to data so that it can assess very well the risks and go where it is mostly needed, in those construction sites or other types of workplaces that are most exposed to fraud and social dumping. So it is quite important that we move very fast with the ELA regulation, because of what it will do.

Trade unions. Yes, they can be among the organisations that can be funded by ELA to give counselling and advice. In fact, the provision was inspired by social partners in one of our Member States doing this exact thing.
VET qualifications – I answer just a few. They are part of the skills portability act. Maybe in my speech I mentioned from secondary to PhD, including VET qualifications.

Through this big pile of regulations we build trust. So all qualifications, frameworks – all the work – is detailed there, including for VET qualifications' recognition, and it will be clearly part of our VET strategy that we will adopt very, very soon.

Then, indeed, I would want to emphasise that it is very important that this package responds to shortages of labour. Being able to work in the profession in which you have been trained means that you get access to quality employment and you support the economy. But having decent work, no matter in which country you work, and being paid and having your social rights respected, means having a solid ESSPASS and a solid ELA.

I just want to say that what is, I think, very important is that we swiftly move to negotiations on these five initiatives. It is so important that hopefully, maybe even next year, we come to some sort of a conclusion so that we can then deploy all the IT and technical work.

We will launch a group with our Member States on the digitalisation of qualifications. We need to integrate them in this huge revolution of skills. We need really to be able to deliver, but to deliver, I think, we need our collaboration between us, you and the Council so that we start our work on the content as soon as possible and hopefully advance and finalise as soon as possible in this mandate.

For other types of details, because time is short, me and my team are at your disposal. We just launched the package. We can go into any type of information so that we can improve it if you find it necessary. What is important is that we deliver concrete results for our citizens, for our companies, for our EU nationals, but also third-country nationals that are qualified and can deliver results here in the European Union.
Thank you very much for this debate and let's work on these proposals.

interventions.speaker_label: Kaja Kallas, Executive Vice-President of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Honourable Members, let me start by thanking Rapporteur Rasa for her timely report on Russia's hybrid warfare in Europe. It captures well the situation we face and, more importantly, the urgency to act. Since Russia began its full‑scale invasion in Ukraine in 2022, there has been a steady increase in hybrid attacks against Europe. We have seen Russia's dangerous, reckless behaviour on full display in the past 48 hours. Russian warship fired flares at a Danish helicopter, NATO jets had to shoot down a drone over Lithuania, Russia struck a passenger train near the border with Ukraine, and Poland pulled a drone from its waters. We need to be clear‑eyed: those are not accidents; they are calculated attempts by Russia to weaken our resolve, test our unity and play with fears of escalation.

Europe will not dial back its support for Ukraine as Russia escalates. We stand firm in supporting Ukraine and adding more pressure on Russia. Russia adapts depending on the country it is targeting. In some, for example, it meddles in the information space, exploits societal divisions and interferes in elections. Elsewhere, attacks are physical, targeting military infrastructure, public transport and critical infrastructure. Because of this, our combined intelligence should cover the entire Russian hybrid toolbox. This is why, as the report underlines, intelligence sharing is vital. I can only encourage Member States to do more and to make the best use of our Intelligence and Situation Centre, INTCEN, to do so.

Despite international efforts to end the war, Putin chooses to intensify his war of aggression against Ukraine and hostilities against Europe. And one thing is very clear, Putin will not stop unless he is stopped. So as Russia is willing to take greater risks, Europe must impose a greater cost. Five examples of how we do this. One, we keep calling out Russia's attacks. Russia has always used ambiguity as a weapon. If we attribute these attacks, Russia cannot hide, and our citizens can see the patterns and understand their playbook too. For this reason, Germany's investigation, attribution and clear public communication following the Leipzig attack was important. In July, we collectively exposed the FSB for cyber aggression in Europe. We must do this work systematically.

Second, as the report also calls for, we sanction the instigators. More recently, we sanctioned nine individuals and four entities. This work must continue as well. Third, we cut Russia's funding off at the root. EU sanctions have already deprived the Russian economy of EUR 1 trillion. We are now finalising the largest number of listings yet. We are also steadily dismantling the shadow fleet. EU naval operations are taking the lead in boarding suspected vessels and, thanks to the diplomatic work across the globe of our EU delegations, fewer countries are allowing these vessels to sail under their flags. Hundreds of ships have been deflagged as a result of our efforts.

We have already cut Russia's diplomatic presence in the EU, put in place new requirements for intra-Schengen travel and capped the Russian mission to the EU at 40 members of staff. Member States are doing this as well. Most recently, Hungary expelled 10 Russian diplomats. There is potential to do more. We can tighten control further over the movement of Russian diplomats within Schengen. We can ban issuing visas for Russian ex-combatants, and we should review the issuance of tourist visas to Russian citizens. We must reduce the pool of people conducting attacks on European soil.

Fifth, we protect our information space. This means faster detection of FIMI, including with the use of AI‑powered tools, training staff in our delegations, mapping Russia's scam networks for recruitment and helping partners to dismantle them, and raising the impact of our countermeasures, including sanctions, law enforcement and takedowns.

Honourable Members, Europe is much stronger than it was. Our societies are better prepared, more aware, more vigilant, and more resilient. And our strategic partnership with NATO now means day-to-day work together. But the threat of Russian hybrid attacks across Europe is only growing. Putin is a textbook bully. Moscow's hybrid attacks are designed to intimidate us, paralyse our societies and make us hesitate to act. That is precisely what Putin wants. We should not let fear dictate our choices. We should match the level of these attacks with concrete action and a confident response. Europe's security requires it and its citizens expect it. Thank you very much.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, Madam Commissioner, Europe must move faster.

While preparing the report among colleagues from different political groups, I sensed deep concern for, and a strong focus on, European security. Thank you to everyone who worked so hard, especially our political group advisors.

Europe is already under attack in the grey zone. It is 'Phase Zero' warfare, and it is becoming more and more kinetic. The biggest mistake now would be to respond to it as if these were isolated incidents.

Fear of escalation has not prevented Russian escalation. It has encouraged Russia to test the next boundary. Russia is the gravest hybrid threat facing the EU. Russia is using hybrid tools directly and through Belarus, proxies and intermediaries. The objective is broader than simply causing physical damage: the aim is to weaken European unity, undermine democratic institutions, create fear and distrust, weaken support for Ukraine and undermine our ability to defend ourselves. Russia is testing our political will. The biggest weakness: Europe is too slow. The Kremlin exploits the time it takes us to decide. Europe must move from resilience to deterrence: resilience is necessary, but resilience alone is not deterrence.

The report therefore calls for the EU to move from a reactive to a proactive posture. The report calls for calibrated, proportionate and coordinated responses. The battlefield is not only our borders, it is also our citizens’ minds. The report explicitly treats societal resilience as a central pillar of security, not a secondary issue. Our citizens are our first line of defence.

On critical infrastructure: a cable pipeline, port, airport or satellite can be as strategically important as a military installation. Europe’s eastern flank is its first line of defence. The report calls for faster implementation of the Eastern Flank Watch, stronger border surveillance and defence, and dedicated funding for vulnerable eastern regions. NATO remains the cornerstone of collective defence. A stronger European Union is a stronger European pillar of NATO. The EU’s mutual defence clause – Article 42(7) – needs to become operational, not theoretical.

Ukraine, Moldova and Armenia matter to Europe. They are not simply victims of hybrid warfare: they are also teaching Europe how to resist it. Condemnation is not enough: if sovereignty is attacked, there must be a proportionate and coordinated response.
However, the most important measure to prevent Russian aggression against us is to help Ukraine. To help by all means possible. Russia must be defeated.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señora comisaria, gracias, Rasa, por este magnífico informe que pone de manifiesto, claramente, que estamos asistiendo a una escalada de la amenaza de vida de los ataques híbridos de Rusia contra la Unión Europea y que tenemos que reaccionar rápidamente.

Pero, por desgracia, no solo estamos sufriendo estos ataques híbridos en el Este, sino también en el sur de Europa, donde la ciudad de Ceuta ha sido invadida por más de 80 000 personas sin que el Gobierno español haya sido capaz de evitarlo ni sepa cómo gestionarlo.

A día de hoy no sabemos cuántos invasores están en las calles de Ceuta provocando inseguridad, violaciones, allanamientos de morada, etcétera. Es más, el Gobierno español dice que no es capaz de sellar herméticamente las fronteras y que, por tanto, la llave de la frontera sur de Europa depende de un tercer país, en este caso, de Marruecos.

Habrá que exigirle desde la Unión Europea, desde la Comisión y desde el SEAE que se comprometa a sellar el control de las fronteras españolas en Ceuta —porque es la frontera exterior de Europa— y que haya una investigación independiente y exhaustiva para saber quién estaba detrás de la organización, planificación y ejecución de esta invasión.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, High Commissioner, colleagues, as we debate this important report on hybrid warfare, we must be absolutely clear‑eyed about the nature of the threat we are facing. We are not just defending cables, pipelines or servers – not even just borders or territory. We are defending our fundamental values and our social and political order that is based on democracy and the rule of law, but also in no small part, on social inclusion and cohesion.

The multi‑domain, hybrid operations that Russians and others are running are part of a strategic campaign to undermine and ultimately destroy our liberal democratic system and the international rules‑based order that guarantees our collective peace and security.

Our enemy's strategy is insidious and calculated. It aims to exploit our vulnerabilities, to amplify pre‑existing fears, to divide our societies and the whole community of democratic nations. Our enemies know full well that a divided Europe is a weak Europe. That is why they are trying to discredit our social and political order, weaponise disinformation, provoke conflicts, and turn individual citizens as well as whole communities against each other.

Obviously, we must urgently build up stronger defences against hostile drone incursions into our airspace that create a sense of insecurity among people, against the instrumentalisation of migration that aims to put pressure on our borders, and against disinformation operations whose aim is to sway our elections. But beyond that, on a strategic level, we must adopt a holistic approach to security and build stronger societal resilience against the forces that are trying to make our own people doubt the benefits of living in a democratic society governed by the rule of law.

Obviously, we must urgently build up stronger defences against hostile drone incursions into our airspace that create a sense of insecurity among people, against the instrumentalisation of migration that aims to put pressure on our borders, and against disinformation operations whose aim is to sway our elections. But beyond that, on a strategic level, we must adopt a holistic approach to security and build stronger societal resilience against the forces that are trying to make our own people doubt the benefits of living in a democratic society governed by the rule of law.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, la guerre hybride est un concept populaire depuis plusieurs années, mais qui décrit une réalité déjà ancienne. Avant même, ou sans même, que les armes ne parlent, il est possible d'obtenir des résultats politiques par l'intimidation, la propagande, la démoralisation ou par des actions d'un faible niveau de violence.

Rappelons, chers collègues, qu'il ne s'agit pas d'une guerre pour autant, et que nous ne sommes donc pas en guerre aujourd'hui, même si, bien sûr, nous ne vivons pas dans une paix tranquille. Notre délégation RN a voté les résolutions de soutien à la Finlande, la Lituanie, la Pologne, la Roumanie. Nous continuerons de faire face à tous ceux qui s'en prendront à notre sécurité commune, à notre souveraineté ou à nos intérêts, comme ce fut le cas ces dernières semaines en Allemagne et en Espagne.

Nous rejetons en revanche les recommandations qui sont faites dans le rapport. Je citerai trois exemples: aller vers une authentique Europe de la défense, créer un centre de cyberdéfense de l'UE en demandant aux États de partager leurs renseignements, et enfin donner à la Commission le rôle de centre opérationnel de gestion de crise. Il n'y a aucune piste à chercher du côté de la Commission européenne pour renforcer la résilience de nos sociétés et accroître nos capacités de défense.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Ataki hybrydowe na Unię to niewątpliwie pokłosie inwazji Putina na Ukrainę, za którą w ogromnym zakresie odpowiada katastrofalna polityka appeasementu ze strony Berlina, z Angelą Merkel na czele, ale i Brukseli. Co gorsza, Unia Europejska wciąż pośrednio finansuje tę agresję. Od początku roku sprowadzono z Rosji rekordowe ilości gazu LNG za grubo ponad 7 mld euro, co już przekracza całość ubiegłorocznych wydatków. Musimy natychmiast zatrzymać te dostawy. Tylko odcięcie Kremla od funduszy zmusi go do pokoju.

Należy też skończyć z podważaniem autorytetu Waszyngtonu. Silne NATO i sojusz ze Stanami Zjednoczonymi to nasz fundament. Polska i kraje bałtyckie dawno spełniają swoje zobowiązania obronne, ale większość państw wciąż pozostaje w tyle. Dwa procent PKB na obronność w obliczu tak realnego zagrożenia to zdecydowanie za mało. Ukraina niewątpliwie walczy również o nasze bezpieczeństwo, dlatego jakiekolwiek wstrzymanie czy choćby ograniczenie pomocy dla niej byłoby podarunkiem dla Kremla.

paragraphs.text: Head kolleegid, hea välisasjade kõrge esindaja! Venemaa eesmärk on külvata Euroopa ühiskondades segadust ja hirmu. Ja riigijuhtide kätes on mitte lasta sel juhtuda. Vene hübriidsõjast on paraku saamas riiklikult toetatud terrorism, sest väga paljud viimased sündmused on otseselt ohustanud Euroopa kodanike elusid. Ja sellele kõigele saab vastu ainult Euroopa Liidu ühtsete tugevate sammudega.

Kahjuks me oleme näinud, et midagi peab juhtuma konkreetsetes riikides, et asjad hakkaksid muutuma, et saadaks aru, et tegemist ongi tõsise olukorraga. Aga tegelikult me ju teame, mida tuleb teha. Tuleb parandada infovahetust luureorganisatsioonide vahel. Tuleb panna viisakeeld Vene turistidele sõiduks Euroopa Liitu. Tuleb panna piirangud Vene kultuurikeskustele ja muudele sellistele asutustele. Adekvaatsed sanktsioonid. Toppida täis senised sanktsioonide augud. Külmutatud vene raha tuleb võtta kasutusele Ukraina hüvanguks. Meie idapiir tuleb adekvaatselt välja ehitada. Ukraina toetamist tuleb ulatuslikult jätkata ja oluline on muidugi muuta ka meie ühiskondade arusaamu. Oluline on lõpuks lõpetada illusioonides elamine.

paragraphs.text: Hr. formand! Mange af os oplever i de her uger, at Ruslands aggression ryger tættere på. Senest i går skød et russisk krigsskib signalblus mod en dansk militærhelikopter. Rusland angreb et tog med europæiske diplomater i Ukraine tæt på Polens grænse også i den her uge. Tidligere kom det frem, at Kreml planlægger sabotage mod vores danske virksomheder og hverver almindelige mennesker til at hjælpe dem. De står bag cyberangreb mod myndigheder, og de påvirker demokratiske valg i Europa.

Det er dybt alvorligt, men det er tid til, at vi ser i øjnene, at det ikke er enkeltstående episoder. Det er en hybrid krig mod Europa, vi ser på. Jeg synes faktisk, der gemmer sig et håb i den styrke og det sammenhold, Europa svarer med. Og når Putin nu eskalerer, skal vores svar være at stå sammen og hvæsse vores sanktionsvåben og sikre beskyttelsen af vores lande. For ved I hvad? Den seneste tid viser, at Rusland er desperate, og at Europa er stærk.
Thank you to the High Representative and to the rapporteur for brilliant cooperation.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, luottamus on myös yhteiskunnan kriittistä infraa. Venäjän hybridihyökkäykset EU-jäsenmaita vastaan eivät rajoitu kyberhyökkäyksiin tai väärän tiedon levittämiseen. Kohteena ovat kriittinen infra, rajat, energia ja liikenne sekä viime kädessä myös kansalaisten turvallisuudentunne.

Venäjän tavoitteena on synnyttää epävarmuutta, pelkoa ja vastakkainasettelua Euroopassa. EU:n on vastattava tähän yhdessä. Jäsenmaiden välinen tiedonvaihto, kriittisen infran suojaaminen ja kyky reagoida nopeasti eivät voi riippua yksittäisen maan resursseista.

Kun Eurooppaa pyritään hajottamaan sisältäpäin lietsomalla pelkoa ja epäluottamusta, vahvin vastauksemme on toimiva demokratia, vahva oikeusvaltio, luotettava tieto ja kansalaisten luottamuksen vahvistaminen yhteiseen tekemiseen.
Euroopan turvallisuus on yhteinen asia. Siksi meidän on pystyttävä ennakoimaan uhkia, eikä toimimaan vasta silloin, kun vahinko on jo tapahtunut.
Erityiskiitos, rakas kollega Rasa, upeasta yhteistyöstä.

paragraphs.text: Vážený pán predsedajúci, ďakujem pekne. Pani Kallas, ja som vás veľmi pozorne počúval, že musíme podporovať Ukrajinu, no ja sa vás chcem na rovinu spýtať, koľko miliárd eur ešte chcete ukradnúť európskym občanom a naliať ich do tej čiernej diery s názvom Ukrajina – do krajiny, ktorá je tak, áno, do krajiny, ktorá je tak presiaknutá korupciou, že včera z nej ušiel generálny prokurátor na služobnom aute spolu s manželkou, ktorí sú obvinení z korupcie. Dokedy chcete ešte ľuďom klamať, že Ukrajina porazí Rusko a že zvíťazí? Nezvíťazí! Veľmi dobre to viete, že sa to nestane, že je to vojensky nemožné, že tento konflikt nemá vojenské riešenie. A napriek tomu ľuďom klamete, pretože vám nezáleží ani na Ukrajine, ani na ľudských životoch. Jediné, čo obhajujete, je biznis zbrojárskych spoločností, ako to povedal ten kresťansko demokratický minister zahraničných vecí Nemecka, ktorý hrozil Ukrajine, že musí začať nakupovať ešte viac zbraní, lebo zbrojovky nie sú spokojné so svojimi profitmi. A o to tu ide. A my žiadame: prestaňme nalievať peniaze do tejto vojny a začnime konečne tlačiť na ukončenie tohto vojenského konfliktu a začnime žiadať mier.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Madam High Representative, ladies and gentlemen, Europe stands together and we are united in solidarity. That was the crucial signal sent out by the HR/VP and the foreign ministers of all 27 EU Member States, plus trusted partners, just two weeks ago at our informal meeting in Ireland.

It was the appropriate reaction to the attempted Russian drone attack on Leipzig/Halle Airport. This attack in Germany is part of a long series of Russian attempts to spread disinformation, to threaten, to sabotage and to show aggression towards Europe. It is further proof that the Kremlin has made a conscious decision to treat Europe with blatant hostility. But intimidation will not work.

Madam High Representative, I welcome your declaration to further step up the pressure on the Russian military industrial complex and to crack down on the circumvention of sanctions. It also remains crucial that we support Ukraine, whatever it takes and as long as it takes. Russia remains the main threat to our European security. Russia must pay for attacking Europe.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señorías, quiero primero felicitar el trabajo también de la ponente, con la que hemos podido trabajar de una forma intensa en algo que es real: que Europa está en guerra. Yo lo siento mucho, hay gente que lo intenta poner en entredicho, pero es una realidad.

Lamentablemente, en esta Cámara vemos dos actitudes distintas: la del señor McAllister —que precisamente ha hablado en este momento de lo que son las amenazas híbridas de verdad— y quienes intentan dividirnos desde dentro —como lo que acaba de hacer el señor Pascual de la Parte, hablando de cuestiones nacionales, intentando hacer de las amenazas híbridas y de los ataques rusos o extranjeros una cuestión netamente interna de política nacional—.

Yo sinceramente creo que lo que hace falta es —buena parte del informe lo deja en evidencia— trabajar de una forma intensa y muy seria lo que estamos sufriendo. Usted, señora Kallas, ya lo ha anticipado también con los grandes déficits que tenemos, por ejemplo, en materia de inteligencia —centros de coordinaciones cibernéticas, ante los ciberataques—.

Para terminar quiero hacer solamente una pregunta: el jueves 27 de agosto John Ratcliffe, el jefe de la CIA, se reunió con el jefe de la inteligencia rusa, Sergei Naryshkin, si mañana nos pidieran a Europa una interlocución, ¿quién sería el jefe de la inteligencia europea que podría hablar con los rusos?

Por ese funeral, la comisaria europea de Ampliación dejó de ir a Belgrado pero, a los dos días, el presidente de Francia recibió al presidente de Serbia. Es incoherente. Creo que ese es uno de los puntos que tenemos que enseñar: la coherencia en nuestra política.

paragraphs.text: Yo creo que la unión hace la fuerza. Y la realidad es que Europa tiene que estar mucho más unida. Por eso digo que la principal amenaza híbrida que estamos sufriendo, incluso también desde el interior, es algunas actitudes de algunos dirigentes que se están dejando llevar por la polarización —por, por ejemplo, la extrema derecha—. Lo que está provocando es una política cada vez más dividida en el seno de quienes realmente queremos hacer una Europa cada vez más fuerte, más potente y más coherente, como usted bien cita.

La CDU ha sufrido un fuerte revés electoral hace tan solo unas semanas en Sajonia y tiene mucho que ver con el sentido común, la coherencia y abandonar precisamente esos extremos que son los fieles amigos que están descomponiendo Europa y que, por cierto, hacen un flaco favor al conjunto de la Unión Europea en este momento. Claro que sí.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Ja, Migration wird von Drittstaaten als politische Waffe eingesetzt. Ich gratuliere zu dieser großartigen Erkenntnis, werte Kollegen. Das ist nichts Neues; das erleben wir nicht erst seit gestern. Die Türkei, Belarus, Marokko und viele, viele weitere Beispiele – diese Gefahr gab es schon immer, und es wird sie auch immer geben. Das eigentliche Problem ist, dass die EU diese Schwäche überhaupt zulässt.

Ich muss sagen, es ist schockierend für mich und Millionen von Bürgern da draußen, wie sehr uns die EU mittlerweile abhängig gemacht hat von Drittstaaten – und auch erpressbar. Anstatt endlich die Außengrenzen und damit auch die eigenen Bürger zu schützen, haben Sie Tür und Tor geöffnet für hybride Kriegsführungen. Europa hat sich massiv verwundbar gemacht, indem Sie unseren Grenzschutz ausgelagert haben.

Bestes Beispiel: Marokko. Solange Marokko will und kontrolliert, ist alles gut. Und wenn nicht, stehen binnen Stunden 80 000 Migranten in Europa. Ein Drittstaat kann also nach Belieben den Knopf aufdrehen und Europa in eine ernsthafte Gefahr bringen. Und das Schlimmste ist, jedes Mal, wenn wieder etwas passiert, gibt es vonseiten der EU keinerlei Reaktionen – keine Sanktionen, kein Einfrieren von Milliarden von Entwicklungshilfe, gar nichts.

Wie oft hat Erdoğan schon die Flüchtlingsschleusen aufgedreht, um uns politisch zu erpressen? Trotzdem fließen weiter Milliarden in den EU-Türkei-Deal. Ja, Kooperationen können sinnvoll und richtig sein – unter klaren Bedingungen und mit Sanktionen bei Verstößen. Aber wir dürfen uns nicht abhängig machen!
Solange Europa seine Grenzen nicht schützt, bleiben wir erpressbar. Das, was wir brauchen, sind Zäune, Mauern und vor allem eins: Pushbacks.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, dear Commissioner, the most sophisticated form of malign interference is not forcing people to act, but making them believe that the decision they are making is entirely their own. This is, in essence, what the reflexive control does. It is a concept developed by the Soviet Union during the Cold War. It shapes the information environment in a society through an adversary, influencing a decision-maker without that person even realising it.

This is why the hybrid warfare report is so important. It raises European-level awareness of the fact that our societies can be targeted by an adversary, not only by force, to conquer or to occupy parts of our land, but by manipulating information to change perceptions, beliefs and win hearts and minds.

The report recognises also that European security requires close cooperation between the Member States and the EU, while strengthening our ability to work with NATO. The report is very clear: Europe must become harder to manipulate, harder to destabilise and harder to coerce. I thank the rapporteur for it.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Hohe Vertreterin! Sie haben völlig recht mit dem, was Sie gesagt haben, nämlich wir sind nicht schnell genug. Wir erkennen die Lage, und Sie haben unsere volle Unterstützung, alles zu tun, um auch in Ihrer Rolle wirksam zu sein. Wir wissen aber, dass der Rat nicht schnell genug ist, dass unsere Länder nicht schnell genug sind. Und wenn wir keine Einigkeit haben, Leute, dann wird das nichts. Und genau das weiß Wladimir Putin. Er ist ein Mörder, ein Verbrecher. Und er will uns Angst machen. Und er will den Menschen Angst machen, damit sie wiederum auf uns Druck machen. Unter anderem, die Ukraine nicht mehr zu unterstützen. Und genau das muss unterbunden werden. Und dass man Flucht auslöst. Hybride Angriffe, Staatsterrorismus. Nichts anderes ist das. Das, was auch in Leipzig war. Und die vielen anderen Dinge. Das macht er, um uns auseinanderzubringen, um uns kaputt zu machen. Meine Damen und Herren! Europa ist das größte Friedensprojekt der Welt. Lassen wir es uns schützen. Und stellen wir uns Putin entgegen und sagen: „Bis hierher und nicht weiter!“ Das kann man aber nicht mit Worten. Da muss man klare Reaktionen folgen lassen.
