paragraphs.text: Es ist interessant, dass Sie sich immer melden, wenn ich spreche. Ich hoffe, Sie haben noch andere – Haben Sie verstanden? Okay, es ist interessant, dass, wenn ich mich melde, aus Ihrer Ecke immer so eine Frage kommt.

Es gab in Deutschland heftige Diskussionen zu Nord Stream 2, und die Liberalen in Deutschland haben immer gesagt, es ist indiskutabel, dass nach der Annexion der Krim Geschäfte mit Wladimir Putin gemacht werden. Leider haben nicht alle darauf gehört, und letztlich war das auch der Auslöser, dass Putin erahnen musste, dass sich keine Socke dafür interessiert, was auf der Krim passiert. Das war der Beginn von dem nächsten Krieg 2022. Und weil wir das wissen, müssen wir klar sein, aufhören damit. Wir müssen in Europa zusammenstehen. Keine Geschäfte mit Putin, sondern nur mit Demokraten, und vor allen Dingen ist es unsere Aufgabe, die Menschen zu schützen.

paragraphs.text: Pane předsedající, na letišti v Lipsku narazil ruský dron do křídla ukrajinského nákladního letadla. Nesl výbušninu a nevybuchl jenom proto, že selhala rozbuška. Zopakuji to. Evropu neochránila naše obrana, ale porucha. My v Česku tento scénář známe. V roce 2014 vybuchly muniční sklady ve Vrběticích a zemřeli dva lidé. Stála za tím ruská vojenská rozvědka. Vrbětice, Lipsko, mezi nimi 12 let a stovky dalších incidentů. Sabotáže, kybernetické útoky, drony nad letišti, dezinformace – to nejsou náhody, to je plán. Moskva testuje naše hranice i instituce.

Pokaždé, když Evropa zaváhá, Rusko se poučí a zkusí to znovu jinak. Otázka tedy nezní, jestli přijde další útok, ale jestli ho zase přežijeme jenom díky štěstí. Další prohlášení o hlubokém znepokojení Putina opravdu nezastaví. Musíme zavřít bezpečnostní mezery v Schengenu, zpřísnit sankce a na každý útok odpovědět tak, aby z toho Rusko vyšlo slabší, než do toho šlo. Přestaňme Putina varovat před následky, začněme mu je doručovat.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Im August fand ein Busfahrer auf dem Leipziger Flughafen eine mit Sprengstoff beladene Drohne. Dazu muss man wissen, Leipzig ist das zentrale Drehkreuz für Waffenlieferungen an die Ukraine. Wer also der Ukraine schaden möchte, muss den Leipziger Flughafen ins Visier nehmen. Ich halte deshalb eine russische Sabotageaktion für möglich. Und wenn es so ist, dann muss das auch Konsequenzen haben.

Nur, warum wurde die Drohne denn erst von einem Busfahrer entdeckt? Warum haben die deutschen Geheimdienste nichts davon mitbekommen? Ganz einfach – weil deutsche Regierungen falsche Prioritäten setzen. Im aktuellen Haushalt sind nur 50 Millionen EUR für Drohnenabwehr vorgesehen, aber 700 Millionen EUR für den Verfassungsschutz – das 14-Fache.

In Deutschland sind wir Terrorangriffen wie in Magdeburg oder in Berlin schutzlos ausgeliefert, weil CDU, SPD und Grüne unseren Geheimdienst lieber im Landesinneren einsetzen, nämlich gegen die Opposition. Größer als die Angst vor Russland ist offenbar die Angst vor Mandatsverlust.

Europas Demokratien werden nicht nur von außen bedroht, sondern auch von innen, und zwar von Politikern, die demokratische Wahlergebnisse nicht akzeptieren und die politische Konkurrenz verbieten wollen.

paragraphs.text: Κύριε Πρόεδρε, η Ευρώπη δέχεται υβριδικό πόλεμο και από την Τουρκία μέσω της πατρίδας μου, της Ελλάδας, που φυλάσσει ένα από τα σημαντικότερα εξωτερικά σύνορα της Ευρώπης. Το 2020, η Τουρκία εργαλειοποίησε δεκάδες χιλιάδες μετανάστες στον Έβρο, επιχειρώντας μαζική παράνομη είσοδο στην Ελλάδα. Στο Αιγαίο, οι μεταναστευτικές ροές και τα κυκλώματα διακινητών εξακολουθούν να χρησιμοποιούνται ως μέσο πίεσης.

Απαιτούνται ισχυρά σύνορα, αποτελεσματικές επιστροφές και απελάσεις, ενίσχυση του Λιμενικού και καμία υποχρεωτική μετεγκατάσταση στην Ελλάδα. Η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση οφείλει να δει με μεγαλύτερη προσοχή τις απειλές και τις προκλήσεις που δέχεται κράτος μέλος της από τρίτες χώρες. Η ευρωπαϊκή αλληλεγγύη δεν μπορεί να περιορίζεται μόνο σε λόγια. Και ας είμαστε ξεκάθαροι επιτέλους: Όταν η Τουρκία αμφισβητεί κυριαρχικά δικαιώματα της χώρας μου, της Ελλάδας, και κατέχει ευρωπαϊκό έδαφος στην Κύπρο, αυτό δεν είναι διμερές ζήτημα, είναι ευρωπαϊκό ζήτημα.

Απαιτούμε έμπρακτη στήριξη Ελλάδας και Κύπρου, διακοπή της ευρωπαϊκής χρηματοδότησης προς την Τουρκία και οριστικό τέλος στην ενταξιακή της πορεία. Τα ελληνικά σύνορα είναι ευρωπαϊκά σύνορα. Η υπεράσπισή τους είναι υπόθεση ολόκληρης της Ευρώπης.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, High Representative, dear colleagues, calling Russian actions against EU countries a hybrid operation is whitewashing the fact that Russia is waging a war against Europe.

According to the Commander of the Russian armed forces, General Gerasimov, there are eight phases of warfare when Russia uses its capabilities to force the adversary to bow to Russian interests. Phases 6 to 8 are traditional kinetic warfare, the five steps before that are tightly connected and coordinated actions leading to the use of force unless the adversary gives up. We are now in the phase three of Russian warfare, heading into the phase four: aggressive military exercises and activities.

Just yesterday, as the High Representative mentioned, a Russian Navy frigate sailing in the Baltic Sea shot two emergency flares toward a Danish Defence Forces helicopter on a normal legal recognition mission, a reckless escalation endangering the lives of Danish service members.

In order to stop these Russian actions, we need to react immediately with heavy sanctions that hurt Russian military industry. Thinking about adding extra sanctions to the next sanctions package some months from now is useless, this does not prevent Russian activities and gives the impression that we are weak and don't dare to defend ourselves.

These are messages that we should not send to Russia. Russia respects only force and those who are willing to use it. Unless we learn to do so, we will move to phase four in a very near future. Thank you for that. Slava Ukraini!

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Der russische Anschlagsversuch am Flughafen Leipzig/Halle hätte Menschenleben kosten können. Vereitelt hat den Anschlagsversuch nicht unsere Drohnenabwehr, nicht unsere Dienste, sondern eine abgerissene Zündschnur, ein technischer Defekt. Das sollten wir uns ehrlich eingestehen.

Und wir sollten verstehen, worauf dieser Angriff wirklich zielte, nämlich auf den Tag danach. Auf die Debatte, ob Solidarität mit der Ukraine zu gefährlich wird; auf das Misstrauen, ob der Staat seine Bürger noch schützen kann; auf den Riss, den Putin durch unsere Gesellschaften ziehen will, mit Desinformation und mit willigen Helfern.

Deshalb ist die wichtigste Antwort auf die einzelne Aktion nicht eine Sanktion, so richtig sie ist. Die wichtigste Antwort ist, Putin bekommt dieses Misstrauen innerhalb Europas nicht. Ein Angriff auf Leipzig ist ein Angriff auf Europa. Wir müssen bei Prävention, bei Drohnenabwehr, bei kritischer Infrastruktur und bei der Sanktionsdurchsetzung europäisch handeln. Nicht jeder für sich, mit bloßem Glück als Sicherheitskonzept, denn beim nächsten Mal kann die Zündschnur halten, und einen Knall dürfen wir nicht zulassen.

paragraphs.text: Herr Kollege, wir sehen hier ein übliches Spiel, und das Spiel ist: Lasst uns eine andere Frage stellen, um abzulenken von dem, was hier eigentlich ist – nämlich abzulenken von der Tatsache, dass Russland völkerrechtswidrig die Ukraine angegriffen hat; abzulenken von der Tatsache, dass Russland mit seiner hybriden Kriegsführung uns in Europa schwächen möchte; davon abzulenken, dass andere von innen Europa schwächen müssen, damit wir einem Diktator gegenüber noch schwächer sind.
Und dagegen gilt es zu handeln.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, la invasión de Ceuta es la última fase de una estrategia de guerra híbrida desde Marruecos contra España, que se ha ejecutado de forma sistemática desde la Marcha Verde sobre el Sáhara Español, aprovechando la connivencia de una clase política nacional y europea que ha abrazado la causa marroquí como si fuera la suya propia.

Ustedes hablan de Rusia y estoy de acuerdo. ¿Y Marruecos, señora Kallas? ¿Cómo llamamos a ilegítimas reivindicaciones territoriales, presión y soborno a políticos, presión demográfica sobre Ceuta, Melilla y las Islas Canarias, introducción en toda Europa de una quinta columna con millones de individuos nacionalizados, desestabilización en redes sociales los días 30 y 31 de julio, una agresiva acción diplomática aquí en Bruselas...? Y la muestra es esa cartita que les han enviado a todos los eurodiputados; pero a los de VOX, Marruecos no nos ha enviado nada porque sabemos la verdad.

No hay insignias ni saludos militares, pero hay órdenes, jefes y soldados. No hay armas de guerra, pero hay machetes, bombas incendiarias, piedras y palos agrediendo a nuestros jóvenes. Hay jóvenes entrenados infiltrados en Ceuta y manadas de violadores que imponen el terror sexual en las calles de Ceuta como modo de dominación de la población invadida. Hay infiltración de agentes marroquíes y cédulas yihadistas. Hay mezquitas en suelo europeo bajo control marroquí. Y, miren, hay políticos que en cancillerías y despachos trabajan para el enemigo. Todo eso debe también ser extirpado. Frente a la guerra que nos plantean: el derecho a defenderse.

paragraphs.text: Colleague, my question is very simple. You're saying here that we are not discussing the situation in Ceuta and yet the question is, did you see the plenary agenda? We spent half the day today – also with the support of your own group – discussing the so-called hybrid attack in Ceuta. So I don't know, the question would be whether you maybe missed some part of today's agenda because this was discussed, and now you've taken valuable time away from this plenary. Instead of talking about the Kremlin and its attack we talked about something we already spent the whole day talking about.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, Alta Rappresentante, onorevoli colleghi, la guerra ibrida è ormai una componente strutturale del confronto geopolitico e il Mediterraneo è pienamente esposto.

A maggio una petroliera russa sanzionata è stata individuata sopra una rete di cavi sottomarini, vicino a Creta. Nel Canale di Sicilia opera la cosiddetta flotta ombra russa. Ad agosto la Marina militare è intervenuta al largo di Pantelleria: sono episodi diversi ma che rivelano la stessa vulnerabilità. Energia, comunicazione, rotte commerciali e infrastrutture sottomarine sono parte integrante della sicurezza nazionale.

Serve una risposta concreta: più sorveglianza, intelligence, cibersicurezza, capacità di attribuire rapidamente le minacce e protezione delle infrastrutture strategiche. Ma non basta reagire dopo un attacco: dobbiamo anticipare i rischi, correggere la vulnerabilità e aumentare il costo per chi intende colpirci.

La resilienza è indispensabile: serve deterrenza. Però resteremo sempre un passo indietro se non acceleriamo. Ma su questo sono assolutamente fiducioso perché l'Europa nei momenti difficili ha sempre saputo reagire.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, avouons-le: nous avons de mauvaises habitudes. L'une d'entre elles consiste à mal nommer les choses. L'Union européenne s'est progressivement habituée à user d'euphémismes lorsqu'il s'agit de ce qui nous menace, tout en se payant de mots sur ce qu'elle fait vraiment pour y répondre.

Les menaces hybrides en sont l'un des meilleurs exemples, ou plutôt l'un des pires. L'attaque de drones explosifs déjouée à Leipzig n'est pas une menace hybride. C'est un projet d'attentat terroriste. Les sabotages, les cyberattaques, les manipulations de l'information, l'ingérence dans nos élections, ce ne sont pas de mauvaises manières d'un voisin mal élevé, ce sont des manières de nous faire la guerre sans la déclarer.

Face à cela, l'Union européenne est devenue championne en titres ronflants et en annonces creuses. Un Bouclier européen de la démocratie, ce serait formidable si c'était vrai. Aujourd'hui, on a à peine l'embryon d'un centre d'échanges de bonnes pratiques. Rien de plus. Un mur anti-drone, on en a rêvé: personne ne l'a fait. Une commission géopolitique, permettez-moi de sourire.

À la veille du discours sur l'état de l'Union, je voudrais rappeler à Ursula von der Leyen que le meilleur moyen de perdre la confiance des Européens consiste à promettre beaucoup trop et à faire beaucoup trop peu. Pour ma part, c'est la patience que je suis en train de perdre.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, hybrid attacks against the EU – the Kremlin must be laughing at us. A bomb almost exploded at an airport and we call it a 'hybrid attack'. No. Let us call an attack an attack. Russia is preparing for possible military aggression against the EU and NATO countries. And even the right wing agrees; even they know that. Let us call an attack an attack.

We need to tell this to our people – calmly, clearly, honestly, but let us call an attack an attack. Because people deserve to know, they deserve to know why we're spending so much money on defence, why we protect our infrastructure, why we support Ukraine. This is not about an abstract percentage of GDP; it is about our safety. It is about protecting our lives, our freedoms and our peace.

We need to secure our infrastructure and airports. We need to change our mindset. We need to change our language. We need to strengthen our chief diplomats and not fall into their back like the German Government is doing and many others in Brussels. We need more diplomacy and we need more foreign policy experts and we should not damage them. That's also part of admitting that this was an attack and we should be ready.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Liebe Kolleginnen, liebe Kollegen! Wer einen Krieg will, braucht einen Vorwand. Die Geschichte ist voll von Beispielen. Da war der angebliche polnische Angriff auf den Radiosender Gleiwitz 1939, da waren die angeblichen Massenvernichtungswaffen des Iraks, und jetzt sind es die angeblichen russischen Drohnen in Leipzig.

Leider werden wieder unbelegte Behauptungen als Fakten präsentiert, Herr Lagodinsky, obwohl Experten wie Politiker widersprechen. Als allererster der US-amerikanische Präsident Trump, der klar gesagt hat, Putin will Europa nicht angreifen. Und Sie, liebe Kollegen, wollen die EU vor fremden Angriffen schützen? Wo waren Sie denn, als Nord Stream gesprengt wurde – europäische Infrastruktur im Wert von 16 Mrd. EUR?

Die deutschen Ermittler waren das, die gesagt haben, das war ein ukrainisches Kommando. Bis heute, mehrere Jahre danach, keine Verurteilung durch das EU-Parlament. Stattdessen unterstützen Sie die Ukraine, die der EU nicht angehört, der NATO nicht angehört, und drängen unsere Menschen in einen Krieg. Wir brauchen Frieden und Diplomatie und keine Kriegsvorbereitungen!

paragraphs.text: Vážený pán predsedajúci. Najväčšou hybridnou hrozbou pre Európu nie je Rusko, vážení, ale tu prítomná pani Kallasová, ktorá nás chce nahnať do jadrovej vojny.

A viete, čomu sa povie zúfalstvo? Keď nemecký establishment iba preto, aby porazil AfD vo voľbách, zorganizuje spravodajskú hru v Lipsku a obviní Rusko. Totálne si zničili vzťahy s Rusmi a ešte tie voľby aj prehrali. Perfektné! Mr. Bean by to neurobil inak. Oni sú nielen lúzri, ale aj babráci.

Pani Kallasová, tárate o hybridných hrozbách a pritom je to všetko naopak. Ste to vy, kto celé roky vedie krvavú vojnu proti Rusku. Vaše zbrane zabíjajú Rusov, zbrojíte ako za Hitlera a vaša protiruská rétorika je na úrovni nacistov.

Krutá pravda je, že Rusi nenapadnú žiadnu z krajín Európskej únie. To vy ste napadli Rusko. To vy ste sa rozťahovali k ruským hraniciam. To vy ste sa celé desaťročia snažili o režimovú zmenu v Rusku a teraz sa bojíte, že ochutnáte vlastnú medicínu – ako malé rozmaznané deti! Vy ste extrémny vojnových štváč, pani Kallasová, choďte už kade ľahšie!

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Madam High Representative, today, NATO fighter jets were forced to shoot down a drone that entered Lithuanian airspace from Belarus. Its origin is still being investigated, but the warning is clear: Europe's security environment is becoming increasingly dangerous.

As today's two reports make clear, Russia remains the primary external threat to Europe's democratic integrity, and no Member State can counter this threat alone. They also underline that hybrid operations are not isolated incidents – apart from the speeches here that we hear as well – but are coordinated actions designed to weaken our states and our societies while remaining below the threshold of open armed conflict.
That is why Europe needs faster identification of perpetrators, stronger protection of critical infrastructure, effective sanctions and closer EU-NATO coordination.
Hybrid attacks rely on uncertainty. Our response cannot.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, stimați colegi, nimeni dintre noi nu și-a dorit acest război – nici România, nici Europa, nici cetățenii noștri. Un singur actor a ales agresiunea – regimul politic de la Kremlin.

Din păcate, nu putem schimba geografia, nu putem ignora amenințările, nu putem spera că, dacă privim în altă parte, ele vor dispărea și ne putem ascunde de consecințele acestui război. De aceea, trebuie să fim pregătiți să ne protejăm frontierele, să apărăm infrastructura critică, să investim în sisteme moderne de apărare, inclusiv împotriva dronelor. Dar putem face toate acestea producând mai mult în Europa și în România, protejând în același timp nivelul de trai al populației.

Țara mea resimte costurile mari în a fi la frontiera Uniunii, inclusiv cele generate de dezinformare. Chiar astăzi am avut un protest al fermierilor unde și-au exprimat nemulțumirile, dar aceste proteste au fost deturnate. De aceea, Europa trebuie să facă mai mult și mai repede, să acționeze, sprijinind sectoarele afectate, operaționalizând hubul de securitate la Marea Neagră și având o prezență militară de ultimă generație în zona de est a Europei.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, nous débattons sur les menaces, les guerres, les attaques hybrides qui menacent l'intégrité territoriale, la protection, la sécurité et la démocratie de l'UE. Comprenons-nous bien, je ne remets pas en cause la nécessité de lutter contre ces menaces, mais votre hypocrisie, car il a fallu que cela touche le continent européen pour susciter votre réaction, alors que depuis des décennies, les Outre-mer français subissent ces attaques hybrides.

Je veux ici dénoncer les tentatives de déstabilisation de l'Azerbaïdjan en Martinique et en Guadeloupe, avec la complicité – ou la facilité – de certains députés de la France insoumise, ou plutôt soumis par haine de la France, qui se vendent comme de vulgaires traitres.

On peut aussi prendre l'exemple des Comores, qui revendiquent ouvertement Mayotte, 101ᵉ département de France, et utilisent la submersion migratoire comme un outil de déstabilisation pleinement assumé.

Mais votre hypocrisie ne s'arrête pas là. Vous, l'UE, vous financez ceux qui attaquent notre territoire. En 2025, c'est 200 millions pour l'Azerbaïdjan et 46 millions pour les Comores. La lutte contre les menaces hybrides oui, mais l'hypocrisie: stop.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues: 2 attacks in 2022, 34 in 2024. By this September, the tally in Europe has passed 189 attacks: it’s growing exponentially.

This year we have seen rockets fired at the power substation outside Berlin, a weapons factory in Bulgaria set ablaze, an ammunition plant near Rome blown up, a drone factory in Tallinn torched, explosives on the runway at Leipzig. Then there's the ongoing situation in Netherlands when it comes to railroads, and this is only in August and September.

Europe stands frozen. But you know that fear has never made Moscow stop: 22 consulates closed since 2022, dozens still open, doing exactly what they were built to do. Though 700 intelligence officers have been expelled, every service in EU knows that’s a fraction of what remains.

We are under attack.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, România se află astăzi în prima linie a războiului hibrid dus de Kremlin la Marea Neagră și pe flancul estic.

Incursiunile repetate ale dronelor rusești pe teritoriul românesc, violările de spațiu aerian și dezinformarea constantă nu sunt simple accidente sau erori. Sunt o campanie deliberată de intimidare și testare a coeziunii noastre europene.

Securitatea României este securitatea întregii Uniuni Europene. Avem nevoie urgentă de fapte și acțiuni: operaționalizarea rapidă a Inițiativei europene de apărare împotriva dronelor, desfășurarea sistemului Eastern Flank Watch și fonduri dedicate în viitorul buget multianual pentru apărarea aeriană stratificată și protecția frontierelor.
Trebuie să trecem de la reacție la descurajare activă. Frontiera României este frontiera Europei.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, every now and then some dubious drone makes an appearance, or a drone is conveniently found somewhere. We had that in Bulgaria, while Ursula von der Leyen was circling around, and now in Leipzig. Likewise, the so-called hybrid attacks with the drifting balloons in Belarus.

No one can coherently explain what a so-called hybrid attack even means. It is just one of those EU-approved words for us to repeat, since we cannot point to any real attacks on the EU by Russia. So the EU desperately needs to convince the people about why we should send more billions to Ukraine.

We, on the other hand, are really attacking Russia. We engage in piracy on the open sea by any standards of international law. These actions are real hostilities and they are not hybrid. And no matter how you stand through this war, one thing is certain, war is always the enemy of the people, of all people. And this makes me question why so many of my colleagues here are promoting this very enemy of the people by using these dubious attacks to promote escalation with Russia rather than diplomacy.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señora alta representante, en el año 2021, los enemigos de Europa lanzaron a 8 000 personas desde Bielorrusia contra las fronteras de Polonia, Finlandia y los países bálticos. Los países del Este llevan décadas resistiendo a la presión que Putin y sus aliados ejercen sobre ellos con todo tipo de ataques y provocaciones.

El pasado 30 de julio, la Unión Europea comprendió que tiene un nuevo frente abierto: el flanco sur. La invasión del territorio de Ceuta por parte de 80 000 personas desde Marruecos constituye un ataque de guerra híbrida inequívoco. Por eso, para defender el flanco sur, hay muchas lecciones que aprender de nuestra frontera Este: necesitamos mejores medios físicos en frontera, leyes que permitan echar ágilmente a quienes cruzan ilegalmente y una estrategia diplomática contundente para garantizar la seguridad del territorio.

La Unión Europea y los países del Este están dando una lección de resistencia y protegiéndose de Rusia. Copiemos estrategias. Hagamos lo mismo con los nuevos desafíos que comienzan a aparecer por el sur.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Powiedzmy sobie szczerze: jesteśmy na wojnie hybrydowej. I nie ma tutaj chyba żadnych wątpliwości i żadne eufemizmy na pewno tutaj nie pomogą, a raczej zaszkodzą. Dla przykładu każdego dnia w Polsce dochodzi od 2 do 4 tysięcy cyberataków, na szczęście w większości odpieranych. Putin nie tylko chce nas przestraszyć, ale przede wszystkim – nas podzielić. I widać to także na tej sali. Widać to także w polityce.

Nie brakuje Putinowi pożytecznych idiotów, którzy w tę pułapkę bardzo łatwo, niestety, wpadają, którzy częściej krytykują Unię Europejską niż Rosję, którzy częściej widzą wroga w Brukseli niż w Rosji. A przecież to nie włoskie drony spadają na Polskę. To nie niemiecka flota cieni niszczy infrastrukturę na Bałtyku. To nie francuskie trolle atakują Hiszpanię. To wszystko robi Rosja. Dlatego Europa zawsze wygrywa, kiedy jest zjednoczona, a przegrywa, kiedy jest podzielona. Nie dajmy się podzielić Putinowi.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señora alta representante, me sumo a la consternación por los ataques de guerra híbrida rusos pero debo dedicar el tiempo a un ataque de guerra híbrida en marcha que lleva a cabo Marruecos desde julio.

Primero, usa estrategias y tácticas no convencionales, utiliza a su propia población como arma, como hizo en su día en la Marcha Verde, y agentes de la seguridad marroquí han organizado y guían la invasión.

Segundo, emplean a proxies como las mafias del tráfico de personas y las ONG que les dan cobertura a los invasores, que hacen negocio con la invasión mientras ignoran el sufrimiento, el dolor y el miedo del pueblo ceutí.

Tercero, sobornan, chantajean y compran lealtades. La traición empieza por el propio Pedro Sánchez. Pregúntense qué le debe Sánchez a Marruecos para comportarse como su perro faldero mientras territorio de la Unión Europea es invadido y encima le agradece la cooperación a Marruecos.
Exigimos la condena unánime de la Unión, la expulsión de los invasores, la suspensión de todos los acuerdos con Marruecos y de los pagos pendientes con ese país.

paragraphs.text: Κύριε Πρόεδρε, υβριδικός πόλεμος είναι ο πόλεμος με μη στρατιωτικά μέσα με στόχο την αποσταθεροποίηση, τον εξαναγκασμό και την υπονόμευση της κυριαρχίας ενός κράτους. Κυβερνοεπιθέσεις, προπαγάνδα, χειραγώγηση ΜΚΟ, κατασκοπεία και δολιοφθορές, ακόμη και εργαλειοποίηση των λαθρομεταναστών αποτελούν πλέον τα σύγχρονα όπλα.

Η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση οφείλει να αποκτήσει έναν σαφή οδικό χάρτη για ενεργοποίηση του άρθρου 42.7, ώστε η ρήτρα αμοιβαίας άμυνας να μπορεί να εφαρμόζεται άμεσα και αποτελεσματικά. Δεν μπορεί, όμως, να υπάρξει ευρωπαϊκή άμυνα χωρίς συνέπεια και αξιοπιστία. Όταν η ηγεσία της Επιτροπής εναγκαλίζεται με την κυβέρνηση της Τουρκίας και εσείς, κυρία Kallas, την αποκαλείτε εταίρο. Εταίρο της Ευρώπης των δήθεν αρχών και αξιών; Ένα κράτος με ποινικό μητρώο, υπόλογο για γενοκτονίες, για παραβιάσεις ανθρωπίνων δικαιωμάτων, που διεξάγει υβριδικό πόλεμο εναντίον μας και κατέχει ευρωπαϊκά εδάφη της Κυπριακής Δημοκρατίας;
Κυρία Kallas, προσέχετε όταν κάνετε χειραψία με χέρια που είναι βαμμένα με το αίμα εκατοντάδων χιλιάδων αθώων ανθρώπων.

Domnule președinte, stimați colegi, atacurile hibride ale Rusiei lovesc din plin dincolo de granițele Ucrainei. Dar să stai noaptea în pat să auzi sirenele și să te întrebi dacă mai ești în siguranță în propria casă nu ar trebui să facă parte din viața nimănui. Din păcate, aceasta este teama cu care trăiesc astăzi tot mai mulți români din localitățile aflate la granița cu Ucraina. Nu mai este vorba de un război hibrid.

România se află într-o zonă de importanță strategică deosebită pe flancul estic al NATO și al Uniunii Europene. La Marea Neagră și la frontiera cu Ucraina, incidentele repetate cu drone ne demonstrează că amenințarea rusească nu mai este una îndepărtată, ci este deja prezentă la granițele noastre.

În acest context, trebuie să înțelegem, doamnă comisar, că securitatea României înseamnă, de fapt, securitatea întregii Uniuni Europene. Protejarea spațiului aerian al României nu poate rămâne însă doar responsabilitatea țării noastre. Avem nevoie de un răspuns european coordonat, de relocarea de îndată a unor capacități adecvate de apărare și de soluții moderne, care să permită detectarea și neutralizarea rapidă și eficientă a dronelor.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, comme un poison lent, nous nous sommes habitués aux attaques russes et nous sommes maintenant au seuil de la guerre. Ce matin encore, un navire russe a tiré deux fusées sur un hélicoptère danois. Hier, un drone explosif, toujours russe, était découvert à l'aéroport de Leipzig.

Après la sidération, l'heure de la prise de conscience a sonné et il y a urgence. Mobilisons notre arsenal législatif: législation sur les services numériques, le règlement sur l’intelligence artificielle contre les plateformes qui laissent proliférer la désinformation russe. Bannissons les fournisseurs à haut risque qui ont permis à la Chine d'espionner un drone naval britannique. Reprenons le contrôle sur le port du Pirée et la ligne Budapest-Belgrade laissés aux mains de la Chine. Et pendant ce temps-là, l'extrême-droite en Saxe-Anhalt nous propose rien de moins que de lever les sanctions et d'apprendre le russe.
Nous avons un ennemi de l'intérieur. Nous ne les laisserons pas faire et fouler aux pieds nos valeurs démocratiques. Car tous ensemble, notre Europe est forte quand elle est unie.

paragraphs.text: Pane předsedající, migrace, drony a sabotáže, to je každodenní realita hybridních útoků v Evropě. Tisíce migrantů využívaných k nelegálnímu překročení hranic Evropské unie, k vytváření tlaku na naše služby a k rozdělování našich společností. Tak to mimochodem vypadalo na polsko-běloruské hranici a jasně nám to ukázalo, že silné hranice znamenají bezpečnou Evropu. Útoky posledních dnů na kritickou infrastrukturu Německa nám zase ukázaly, jak důležitá je ochrana energetických sítí, komunikačních kabelů, které musí být schopny odolat sabotáži, kybernetickým útokům i útokům drony.

Evropa musí posílit své schopnosti v oblasti protivzdušné a protidronové ochrany. I proto podporuji vyšší investice do obrany, ale tyto prostředky musí směřovat do výzkumu, inovací a moderních technologií. Potřebujeme silný evropský obranný průmysl, který bude vyrábět v Evropě, bude vytvářet pracovní místa v Evropě a zároveň bude posilovat konkurenceschopnost Evropy.
Bezpečnost Evropy už neleží pouze na bojišti. Začíná na našich hranicích, postupuje ochranou naší infrastruktury a končí v soběstačnosti našich ekonomik.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Szanowni Państwo! Polska i państwa bałtyckie, a także Rumunia są dziś na pierwszej linii wojny hybrydowej prowadzonej przez Rosję. W Polsce wschodniej, na Lubelszczyźnie, gdzie mieszkam, otrzymujemy alerty o treści: „Uwaga! Zagrożenie atakiem z powietrza″. Dodatkowo akty sabotażu, podpalenia, dywersje, dezinformacja, ataki dronowe, a także rosyjska rakieta Ch-101 – to nasza rzeczywistość. Dziennie w Polsce dochodzi do ok. 3000 ataków hybrydowych.

Rosja chce siać strach, destabilizować nasze państwa, testować odporność NATO i osłabiać pomoc dla Ukrainy. Dlatego potrzebujemy dziś absolutnej jedności sojuszniczej, większego zaangażowania państw członkowskich w działania rozpoznawcze, skutecznej obrony powietrznej i przeciwdronowej oraz dalszego wzmacniania naszych zdolności obronnych.
Jeśli Ukraina przegra, Rosja może uderzyć pełnoskalową wojną w Unię Europejską. Nie możemy do tego dopuścić.
Dziękuję bardzo sprawozdawczyni.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Rosja jest wrogiem zachodniego ładu i demokracji. Destabilizuje porządek świata. Prowadzi wojnę z państwami Unii Europejskiej, na razie hybrydową. Dlaczego Putin to robi? Bo może. Bo mu na to pozwalacie.

Pytam: dlaczego w Niemczech znaczący politycy CDU i AfD co chwilę domagają się odbudowy Nord Stream, który finansował wojnę, agresję na Ukrainę i stanowił szantaż gazowy wobec Europy? Czy policzyliście, ile francuskich czy niemieckich firm zarabia, daje zarobić Rosji i wspiera budżet Putina?

Szukajcie sprawców dywersji i ataków hybrydowych pośród Rosjan, którym państwa Unii Europejskiej wydają wizy bez większych przeszkód. Tylko w 2025 r. 600 tysięcy Rosjan przyjechało do Europy. Niektórzy prosto z frontu spod Kramatorska czy Słowiańska, a niektórzy prosto z siedziby rosyjskiego wywiadu.

Aby Putin zrozumiał, że wojna hybrydowa ani żadna inna mu się nie opłaca, potrzebne są odważne decyzje polityczne na szczeblu Unii, jak i państw członkowskich. Potrzeba realnego odizolowania Rosji i jej gospodarki. Wy ciągle chcecie zarabiać z Rosją i dla Rosji. Mówicie jedno, a robicie drugie.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, quanto accaduto stanotte nei cieli lituani, dove i caccia NATO hanno abbattuto l'ennesimo drone sospetto, ci ricorda che la sicurezza non è un concetto astratto ma riguarda le nostre case, le nostre imprese, l'energia che utilizziamo, i trasporti.

I droni, i sabotaggi, i cyberattacchi, la disinformazione, gli attacchi alle nostre infrastrutture dimostrano che le minacce sono già intorno a noi e non possiamo aspettare un'emergenza per reagire. Dobbiamo investire nella nostra sicurezza e rafforzare sempre più il rapporto di cooperazione tra l'Unione europea e la NATO.

Quando stipuliamo un'assicurazione, non lo facciamo perché siamo certi che accadrà qualcosa ma perché vogliamo essere protetti nel caso accada. La difesa funziona allo stesso modo: prepararsi non significa volere la guerra; significa fare di tutto perché non accada.

E allora, difendere l'Europa significa proteggere la libertà e la quotidianità dei nostri cittadini. E la sicurezza ha un costo? Sì, certamente. Ma non essere preparati, ve lo garantisco, ci costerà molto di più.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, thank you for this valuable debate. What I want to say is that the EU has significantly stepped up the response in recent years. You know, just consider where we are coming from, including the new hybrid sanctions regime since 2024. And it is targeting those who undermine our democracies, those who sabotage or threaten critical infrastructure and public services and also those who carry out FIMI operations and malicious cyber activities and those who instrumentalise migration, because everything is weaponised nowadays.
So we are also building an international coalition when it comes to the protection of the seabed infrastructure, because we see that these kinds of threats and sabotage are more likely.

The question we need to ask ourselves is whether we are acting at the necessary speed and scale. Many of you mentioned this: we are doing the right things but we are not doing them fast enough, and we are not realising fast enough.

So what we must do, and what we are doing, is to continue reinforcing Europe's resilience by protecting critical infrastructure, securing our democratic processes, also strengthening cyber defence – all the things that are being attacked. We need to build our resilience. And, of course, we need to also increase our capacity to detect and counter foreign information manipulation and interference, because it is also a battle of narratives.

We also need to be more assertive. On FIMI, for example, we are increasing in speed and scale and the impact of our response. And what we also need to see is that hybrid attacks cannot remain in a grey zone without consequences. And that is why it is very important that we combine resilience with attribution, sanctions, action against hostile networks operating on our soil and, of course, all of this in close cooperation with the Member States, with NATO and like-minded partners, including those partners that are more likely exposed. And we need to keep supporting our neighbourhood when we are asked to do so. As we saw in Moldova last year, Russia's meddling with elections can be beaten. Also Armenia. We need to keep communicating also to our citizens about the benefits of EU membership and also what citizens stand to gain because very often we are talking about enlargement only in terms of what these countries are receiving when they join but it's actually our side that is also benefiting.

Finally, I want to say to those who were talking about peace: let me be very clear, nobody wants peace more than Ukrainians. And they have agreed to multiple ceasefires for a very long time. But we also need to be clear-eyed. Russia is not agreeing to these things; quite the opposite – they are escalating with the attacks on civilians in Ukraine, but also the attacks on our territories. So we need to be very clear-eyed about these things. And I also do not agree with those who say: why don't you just give up the territory and there would be peace? It's never about territories. It's always about the people who are suffering also in these territories. If aggression pays off, then we will see more of it.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Rosja nie musi pokonać Europy militarnie. Wystarczy, że podzieli Europejczyków. I podczas tak ważnej dyskusji, tak ważnej debaty słyszę po raz kolejny na tej sali głos Putina. Są tutaj, na tej sali ludzie, którzy cały czas nam mówią: nie pomagajcie Ukrainie, niech każdy odpowiada za siebie, róbmy biznes z Rosją. To są ci, którzy nadają ton Putinowi.

Tymczasem ja pochodzę z Polski. Powiem, co się dzieje w ostatnich godzinach. W rejonie plaży nad Morzem Bałtyckim służby podjęły rosyjski dron bezzałogowy typu Gerbera. Dzień wcześniej zaatakowano 2 km od granicy pociąg relacji Kijów–Warszawa. Drugi atak uderzył w stację benzynową kilkaset metrów od granicy. Przed nami najtrudniejsze momenty tej wojny podczas zimy na Ukrainie. Wszyscy musimy być zjednoczeni w Europie. Tylko silna, mocna Europa może postawić tamę Rosji.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señora alta representante, (palabras inaudibles) hay que sacar conclusiones.
La primera es que los ataques híbridos no conciernen solo a los países que, como el suyo, tienen frontera con Rusia: hay que ampliar el foco.

La segunda es que el neologismo del ataque híbrido alude a una agresión no convencional contra nuestra soberanía y nuestros proyectos estratégicos y requiere respuestas no convencionales: requiere ciberseguridad y el muro europeo antidrones, pero también una comunidad europea de inteligencia —que ahora brilla por su ausencia—.

Y la tercera es que, si decimos tener vocación geopolítica, tenemos que poner los instrumentos —no solamente desarrollar el artículo 42, apartado 7, del Tratado de la Unión Europea o la cooperación estructurada—. Y, en su defecto, necesitamos un grupo pionero que esté dispuesto a invertir lo suficiente en defensa y seguridad. Pero, sobre todo, necesitamos la superación de la unanimidad que lo hace imposible en estos momentos, y eso requiere una reforma institucional.

Por tanto, la superación de la unanimidad es la condición indispensable para que la Unión Europea adquiera, de una vez, una voz que sea audible y digna de ser escuchada y respetada en la comunidad internacional, particularmente ante quienes nos amenazan. Y esa voz audible requiere una reforma institucional antes de que se consume la ampliación.

paragraphs.text: Szanowny Panie Przewodniczący! Szanowni Państwo! Putin jest wrogiem wolnych narodów Europy – ale Putin również nim był od samego początku. Kiedy szanowni państwo zrozumieją, że Rosja nie jest częścią cywilizacji zachodniej? Jest odwiecznym imperium, które żywi się podbojem i zabieraniem wolności innym narodom.

Wiedzą o tym Finowie, wiedzą o tym Bałtowie. Wiemy o tym najlepiej my, Polacy. I to nie my, jak Angela Merkel, prowadziliśmy politykę z Putinem. I Putin dzisiaj ma pieniądze na swoją armię i na swoje czołgi – które zabijają Ukraińców, które grożą Polakom, które grożą Łotyszom, Litwinom i Estończykom – z pieniędzy, które zostały wypłacone z zachodniej Europy.

Ja się bardzo cieszę, że państwo wreszcie zmienili zdanie. Tylko od debat w Parlamencie Europejskim Putin się nie przestraszy. Przestraszy się odważnych działań. Za to wy wydajecie pieniądze na nakrętki w butelkach.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, I welcome this report and its emphasis on resilience and deterrence. Europe must move from reacting to individual incidents towards a proactive strategy that anticipates, disrupts and raises the costs of hostile operations.
Together with our allies, we must be also ready to take the initiative in the grey zone and develop the capacity to act below the conventional conflict.

One dimension can be stated more clearly. That is ideology. What Russia promotes as the Russian world has evolved into Russian fascism or 'Ruscism'. It systematically denies the sovereignty of Ukraine, the Baltic states and other nations formerly dominated by the Russian Empire and the Soviet Union.

Finally, I welcome the call for a stronger European pillar of NATO and a European Defence Union. Ukraine must be a part of it. Defence integration could be a first practical step towards EU membership while bringing to Europe Ukraine's unique defence innovation and experience.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, si hablamos de las amenazas a Europa, hablemos de todas. Nadie ha dicho nada de la amenaza internacional reaccionaria dirigida por Trump y Netanyahu. Trump nos amenazó con una invasión en Groenlandia.

Nadie ha dicho nada de la máquina de desinformación de Israel o de los ataques con drones a Francia, Italia o España. Porque sí, según el Derecho internacional —lo han reconocido los jueces europeos, españoles— cuando se atacó a los barcos europeos que llevaban ayuda humanitaria a Gaza, se estaba atacando el territorio europeo.

Y sí, la derecha, Pascual de la Parte y Buxadé, hoy nos hablaban de lo que llaman ellos guerra híbrida de Marruecos, pero no nos han dicho nada de la internacional reaccionaria de la cual forman parte ellos y también Marruecos.

El señor Girauta ha dicho que el presidente Sánchez debe juzgarse por traición a la patria. Pero si los traidores son ellos, si votaron el otro día, además, en contra de devolver el DNI a los saharauis, a diferencia de los socialistas y de nosotros; ellos son los que están al servicio de otras potencias.
Y se ha demostrado —lo ha dicho el propio expresidente Aznar del Partido Popular— que Israel estaba detrás de lo de Ceuta. Y de eso no han dicho nada.

paragraphs.text: Нискоинтелигентни манипулации като тази, че руснаците били поставили дрон на летището в Лайпциг, имат една цел - да накарат европейските граждани да повярват, че най-голямото зло на света е Русия и че едва ли не сме длъжни да се бием с нея.

Само че мнозинството от европейските граждани съвсем не сме толкова безмозъчни, за каквито ни мислят евроръководителите, и никой от нас няма желание да повтаря печалната съдба на войниците на Наполеон и на Хитлер, само и само за да задоволим антируските страсти на шефовете на Евросъюза. Сигурен съм, че дори и хората в тази зала, които най-истерично призовават да бъде подкрепян с всички пари и оръжия на света режимът на Зеленски, няма да отидат да се бият на Източния фронт, за да бъде сразен злият Путин, защото истерията си е истерия, но инстинктът за самосъхранение е по-силен.

А иначе напълно съм съгласен, че трябва да пазим демокрацията в Европа, каквото е заглавието на днешния дебат. И най-добрият начин да съхраним европейската демокрация е да отстраним от власт сегашните управляващи. В Германия този процес започна. Скоро ще го видим и в други държави.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Pani Komisarz! Chcę bardzo wyraźnie powiedzieć: naszym celem, podstawowym celem w Parlamencie Europejskim jest zapewnienie naszym krajom bezpieczeństwa. I jest coraz cieńsza bariera, która dzieli Rosję od rozpoczęcia kinetycznego konfliktu z NATO. Rosja eskaluje. Rosja prowokuje. I jedyną odpowiedzią Europy musi być siła. Bierzemy odpowiedzialność za gotowość obronną Europy.

Przede wszystkim – mobilność wojskowa. Pracujemy nad regulacją, która przyspieszy w znaczący sposób transport wojska i transport sprzętu. Ułatwienia dla przemysłu obronnego. Po to jest omnibus. I wreszcie budżet po roku 2028: gigantyczne środki, które muszą przypłynąć na projekty obronne i mobilność wojskową, infrastrukturę, która będzie wykorzystywana w sposób „dual use”. Dziękuję za to wsparcie. Prosimy o więcej. To, co się działo w ostatnich dniach w Polsce, tuż przy polskiej granicy, jest bardzo niebezpieczną sytuacją, na którą musimy odpowiedzieć.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, hybrid attacks against EU Member States include cyberattacks, sabotage of critical infrastructure, undersea cables, drone incursions, instrumentalisation of migration flows and much more. The ongoing Russian aggression against Ukraine and various forms of hybrid attacks against Member States is a primary source of real threat.

However, hybrid attacks are also taking place for years by the neo-Ottoman Erdoğan regime against Member States in the eastern Mediterranean, for which the High Representative, I'm sorry to say, never talks. This is not European unity that makes us stronger. This is hypocrisy that weakens us, and that's what feeds the extreme right wing.
I would agree fully with the rapporteur: making Article 42.7 workable and operational would be something in support of Member States.
And a final comment, Madam High Representative, a word of honesty: your double standard policy is increasing part of the problem.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, two days ago I was on a train full of European politicians returning from Ukraine. As we crossed into Poland, a Russian drone hit a train on the spot where we were just moments before.
Last year, Russian drones entered Polish airspace and I warned that every escalation without a response from us is an invitation for Putin to continue.

Today, a drone shot down in Lithuania. A Russian frigate shoots a flare at a Danish helicopter. More and more and more attempts to scare us, and these attacks will not stop until Russia knows that every escalation has consequences.

Each attack should have a response. A drone on European soil? We give Ukraine 10 long‑range missiles. An attempt to bomb an airport? We give Ukraine money from the frozen Russian assets. Every time Putin tries to sow fear, we should meet it with determination instead.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Szanowni Państwo! Ataki hybrydowe Rosji mają konkretne konsekwencje gospodarcze, szczególnie dla regionów graniczących z Rosją, Białorusią, Ukrainą, dla takich regionów jak region, z którego pochodzę i w którym się urodziłem (województwo lubelskie w Polsce wschodniej). Tam następuje dramatyczny odpływ kapitału, zatrzymanie inwestycji, brak chęci inwestorów zewnętrznych do inwestowania w tych regionach. Rodzimi przedsiębiorcy zastanawiają się nad podwyższonym ryzykiem inwestowania w tych regionach.

Pani Kallas pytała dzisiaj tutaj, czy możemy zrobić więcej? Tak, nie mam wątpliwości, że na pewno. Ale Komisja Europejska, która zaproponowała pakt dla regionów wschodnich, który miał je wesprzeć w tej trudnej sytuacji, niestety ogranicza się tylko do jakiegoś zaliczkowania bądź szybszych procedur. Nie tędy droga.

Jeśli natychmiast nie wesprzemy tych regionów także finansowo, szczególnie jeśli chodzi o inwestycje, inwestycje publiczne i prywatne, to i tak będziemy musieli w przyszłości te regiony wspomóc, ale koszty tej pomocy będą stukrotnie wyższe niż w tej chwili.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, thank you, Rasa, for the great report. I must be brutally honest: out of fear of escalation, we have enabled escalation. To be very precise, the Council did; our Member States did. A weak response, or the absence of one, is an invitation; it's an encouragement. Every attack must deepen our support for Ukraine urgently, including Sky Shield, more deep strike capabilities and air defence. Europe needs to be united, extremely united, in its response. What must be predictable is that a response will follow, while the form of that response should remain unpredictable.

We must move beyond the simple attribution of single incidents and look at the trend. Our deterrence gap also depends on our willingness to manage escalation more assertively. Dear HR/VP, dear Kaja, a vast majority of this Parliament agrees with you on the analysis and on the solutions. The reality is that real actions depend on the Council. Feel supported, dear HR/VP, in underlining the urgency – or the lack of urgency – in the Council. We can and must do more faster.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, can we claim to be serious about stopping Russia if in the fifth year of a real war in Europe, Russian Houses – like the one in Berlin that was closed only after Leipzig – are still operating? They are still in Austria, Belgium – in Brussels, Bulgaria, France, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Luxembourg, Malta, Cyprus, Spain, Slovakia. These are Russian spy centres operating against the EU and orchestrating FIMI operations. When these institutions are closed, then I will believe that those countries are seriously determined to defeat Putin's Russia.

After the recent Russian attack in a train near the Polish border, after a drone was shot down by a fighter jet in my country and after Danish events, it is no longer accurate to describe everything happening against the EU as hybrid warfare. We need to change our thinking to hybrid defence – strong hybrid defence. Wars are won first and foremost in the minds.

Thank you to the majority of my colleagues here for their support. But we heard the words of open Russian agents here now. This is a dangerous game. It is neither democracy nor free speech when open supporters of the war criminal Putin spread lies from this podium. I very much hope that this report will be read across EU institutions and capitals, and that it will help us in Europe start looking in the same direction.

paragraphs.text: Magdalena Adamowicz (PPE), na piśmieJeśli bardzo agresywny napastnik pluje, a my odwracamy wzrok, to za chwilę rzuci kamieniem. Potem kopnie najsłabszą osobę w grupie, a na końcu uderzy kolejną w twarz. Żaden taki napastnik nie zatrzymał się dlatego, że ofiary starały się nie eskalować.Rosja przeszła tę drogę na naszych oczach. Zaczęła od dezinformacji i szła dalej, ponieważ nie potrafiliśmy tych kłamstw powstrzymać. Dziś wysadza tory kolejowe w Polsce, wysyła rakiety i drony, ponieważ nadal nie ponosi za to dość mocnych konsekwencji. Bezkarność napędza reżim Putina.Artykuł 42 ust. 7 Traktatu o Unii Europejskiej zobowiązuje nas do wspólnej reakcji dopiero w razie napaści zbrojnej. Dlatego potrzebujemy nowego mechanizmu, który zadziała poniżej progu wojny. Jeśli Rosja zaatakuje jedno państwo Unii – cyberatakiem, dywersją czy dronem – wszystkie odpowiadają razem i automatycznie.Równolegle potrzebujemy trzech rzeczy: ciągłych ćwiczeń NATO na jego wschodniej flance, broni dla Ukrainy finansowanej z zamrożonych aktywów rosyjskiego banku centralnego oraz sankcji całkowicie odcinających Rosję od pieniędzy na wojnę. Rachunek za tę wojnę ma urosnąć tak wysoko i tak szybko, żeby reżim Putina przestał być w stanie go płacić.Upadek reżimu Putina będzie wtedy także końcem jego europejskiej agentury wpływu i rosyjskich farm trolli, które od lat atakują nas każdego dnia.

paragraphs.text: Mihai Tudose (S&D), în scrisRaportul trece în revistă incidentele recente de pe Flancul Estic, inclusiv cele care au vizat infrastructura militară din România și proiectul românesc de exploatare a gazelor offshore. De la sabotaj la război informațional, de la atacuri cibernetice la cele hibride, împotriva infrastructurii critice a UE – rezoluția evidențiază amenințările cu care se confruntă statele UE și minusurile în pregătirea răspunsului. E nevoie, în primul rând, de consolidarea sistemului de alertă rapidă și a capacității de reacție, de o mai bună coordonare și de eficientizarea capacităților strategice, precum rezerva UE pentru securitate cibernetică. Un accent aparte trebuie pus pe protejarea infrastructurilor critice - energetică, de transport, inclusiv cea pentru mobilitatea militară, precum și de comunicații. Cablurile submarine rămân o vulnerabilitate strategică și nu avem încă o infrastructură digitală a UE, care să fie rezilientă și competitivă. Fragmentarea ne afectează în cazuri sensibile, cum sunt cele de instrumentalizare a migrației, pentru a destabiliza un stat membru și a pune presiune pe UE. De aceea, trebuie să trecem la o etapă superioară de coordonare și cooperare, atât între statele membre, cât și între UE și NATO.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear Commissioner, dear colleagues, I believe that after what we just heard and the past few months, every European understands why we need to make sure that the EU has the capabilities to protect itself. We have seen Russian drones over our airports, our infrastructure sabotaged, arson in our cities, and that is just a taste of what might be coming.

Europe needs to speed up its own protection and we need to do it fast. We hear it over and over again. Member States have increased their defence spending in recent years, but what has not changed is the speed and the fragmentation.

Take permits, for instance. In some Member States, a permit for an ammunition line or a repair facility has taken up to two years. Manufacturers hit the same wall every single time if they want to expand. A company building in three Member States does different paperwork in three different places three times over. 27 different requirements, 27 different deadlines.
But with this regulation, we are creating fast‑track permit procedure for defence readiness projects across the EU and it rests on three elements.
Firstly, one contact point for everybody in the country. Every defence readiness project will have one authority to deal with, from the first question to the final decision.
Secondly, deadline. It will be only one: 42 working days from the moment the application is complete, what can be extended only in exceptional cases.

Thirdly, the mechanism that gives the deadline its actual weight: the tacit approval. If the deadline for the authority to respond passes and the authority has still not decided, the permits will be granted automatically. An administration can no longer stay silent and let the project wait indefinitely.

As a rapporteur, my priority was also transparency because of where I am coming from. I am coming from Slovakia. We cannot allow any Member State to abuse these rules and grant permits to some business friends. The Member States will therefore report on how many permits are granted and then the Commission will assess whether the fast track works or not.

Colleagues, from now on, investment shall go where the capacity can actually be built. And yes, a lot is depending on individual governments. A government that is running a fast‑track procedure well will get new factory lines, the jobs and the supply chain. A government that keeps a slow national permitting structure will watch investments go elsewhere.

But let me also bring a little bit of a realistic outlook into this legislation and it is about governments. The Commission has introduced a very ambitious defence omnibus package, but Member States watered it down. Maybe not on the sites of permits that much, but certainly in the area of intra‑EU transfer licences.

No, we will not be able to create a real European Defence Union if the protectionism of Member States, including those biggest ones, is not dismantled. Nevertheless, me and my colleagues, co‑rapporteur Henrik Dahl, as well as most of the shadow rapporteurs have pushed as much as we were able to.

Without this package, we will continue to scramble to raise money and then spend it at the pace of peacetime. The defence omnibus ends this and it is the first real step towards the European Defence Union.

paragraphs.text: Hr. Formand! Vi kan beslutte at bruge flere penge. Vi kan vedtage ambitiøse planer, men pengene bliver først til forsvarsevne, når fabrikken producerer, når kasernen bliver taget i brug, når soldaterne står med materiellet i hænderne, og derfor hænger de enkelte filer i forsvarsomnibussen nøje sammen.

Tilladelser og sagsbehandling lyder måske ikke som de mest afgørende spørgsmål i europæisk sikkerhedspolitik. Men de to ting minder lidt om elektricitet i kontakten og vand i vandhanen. Det er ikke noget, man tænker over nogensinde, indtil det holder op med at virke.

Derfor er der mindre afstand imellem bureaukrati og sikkerhedspolitik, end man skulle forestille sig. Vi kan ikke på én gang kræve, at Europa handler som om, at situationen er alvorlig, og administrere som om, at vi har hele evigheden foran os til at godkende forsvarsprojektet.

Med den her del af forsvarsomnibussen gør vi godkendelser hurtigere og mere forudsigelige. Vi sætter klare frister for sagsbehandlingen, og vi skaber bedre rammer for, at vi kan gennemføre forsvarsprojekter. Nu er det op til medlemslandene - vi har gjort vores opgave.
Det her er en konkret opgave, hvor EU kan gøre en forskel. Vi kan fjerne forhindringer for medlemslandenes forsvarsevne i stedet for at føje endnu flere lag af administration til.

For de virksomheder, der skal udvide produktionen, er forudsigelighed afgørende. De skal kunne planlægge deres byggeri, bestille maskiner, ansætte medarbejdere. Det er svært, hvis de ikke ved, hvornår myndighederne træffer en afgørelse. Og for vores forsvar er det jo ikke nok, at den nødvendige kapacitet kommer på et eller andet tidspunkt i fremtiden. Den skal være der, lige præcis når der er brug for den.

Så den her fil handler ikke om at holde op med at stille nødvendige krav. Den handler om at skelne imellem de krav, der tjener et formål, og de forsinkelser, der ikke giver nogen mening. Grundig sagsbehandling og hurtig sagsbehandling - det behøver ikke at være modsætninger. Men det kræver, at vi indretter reglerne efter den opgave, vi faktisk skal løse.

Så tillad mig at samle op; Troværdig afskrækkelse - det kræver mere end politisk vilje. Det kræver, at vi kan omsætte viljen til handling. En fabrik, der venter på tilladelse, kan ikke levere ammunition. En kaserne, der kun findes på en tegning, kan ikke huse nogen soldater.
Derfor er det overhovedet ikke nok at spørge, som vi ofte gør, hvor meget vi vil investere i vores forsvar. Vi skal også spørge om, hvor hurtigt investeringerne rent faktisk kan blive til kapacitet.

Jeg vil gerne takke mine kolleger rigtig mange gange, og jeg vil også gerne takke mine forhandlingspartner rigtig mange gange for samarbejdet omkring den her fil. Det har været en fornøjelse at arbejde med alle. Hvis det bare var så nemt hver gang.

Men det løser ikke alle Europas forsvarsproblemer. Det fjerner kun en hindring, som det er vores ansvar som lovgivere at gøre noget ved. Vores opgave er ikke slut, før pengene er bevilget, og reglerne er vedtaget. Der skal også handling bag ordene. Det er først, når de er løst, at Europa kan forsvare sine borgere. Det er det, som filen her bidrager til. Så jeg siger tak for det store arbejde endnu en gang.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear Commissioner, dear colleagues, over the past few years, Europe has finally realised the fact that not only is there an active war on our continent, but we are also involved. Since we are supporting Ukraine's legal and rightful defence, we are now the target of Russia's hybrid war and very possibly the target of Russia's next military aggression.

Therefore, defence has obviously become a much more important part of the EU agenda. This is a necessary development, but having defence simply on the agenda is not enough. We need to look at what we are actually able to deliver.

The Defence Readiness Omnibus is a good example. We have agreed on practical changes to make it easier to produce, purchase and move defence equipment within Europe. We simplified intra-EU transfers of defence products, software and technology. New general transfer licenses could now reduce processes to days – before it took months.

We also made procurement much more flexible. Framework agreements can run up to ten years, giving defence companies more certainty when deciding whether to invest in additional production capacity. And we have made it easier for Member States to participate in cooperative defence programmes.

These are useful changes, but during the negotiations, we unfortunately also saw how difficult it can be to get Member States to go further. Member states, quite rightly, want to retain a strong role in defence policy, but that role also comes with responsibility. We cannot ask Europe to do more on defence and then weaken common solutions when they conflict with narrow national interests.

Military mobility is another very practical example. We already know many of the obstacles that made it difficult to move troops and military equipment across Europe. Some are related to infrastructure, others are more administrative: different national procedures and permits, etc. The EU can provide funding and help coordinate the rules, but in the end, Member States have to remove many of the obstacles themselves. If moving military equipment from one Member State to another still requires unnecessary paperwork and delays, announcing another European defence initiative will not solve the problem.

The same applies to the defence industry. Europe needs significantly more production capacity, but our companies will not make millions of euros of investment simply because we ask them to. They need predictable demands from us. Member States therefore need to coordinate their procurement better, make more joint purchases, and give the industry a clearer, long-term picture of what Europe actually intends to buy. The next MFF and the European competitiveness fund can support this work, but at the same time, we should not measure success simply by how many millions are allocated to defence.

The real questions are more practical. Do we get bang for our buck? Are we producing enough equipment? Can procurement processes be faster? Are our critical supply chains secure enough? Can troops and equipment move across Europe when they are needed?

The Commission also has work to do. The Commission must prepare the legislation, together with military experts, the industry and Member States from the very beginning. Defence cannot be treated simply as another sector of the single market, and all of the knowledge is not in the Commission – 'cooperation' is the key word here.

And the EU should not try to build competitive structures with NATO. NATO remains the cornerstone of our collective defence, while the EU should concentrate to add real value to industrial policy, financing, sensible regulation and infrastructure. We should aim to build a European defence capability that also aims to strengthen NATO, not to duplicate structures that we already have.

If the Member States want a strong European contribution to defence, they also have to be prepared to make the necessary decisions themselves. We have enough strategies and initiatives. Now what we need is for Member States to implement what has been agreed, remove the practical obstacles and invest in the capabilities that Europe needs. This is what the Defence Readiness Omnibus package delivers.

Some are related to infrastructure, others are more administrative: different national procedures and permits, etc. The EU can provide funding and help coordinate the rules, but in the end, Member States have to remove many of the obstacles themselves. If moving military equipment from one Member State to another still requires unnecessary paperwork and delays, announcing another European defence initiative will not solve the problem.

The same applies to the defence industry. Europe needs significantly more production capacity, but our companies will not make millions of euros of investment simply because we ask them to. They need predictable demands from us. Member States therefore need to coordinate their procurement better, make more joint purchases, and give the industry a clearer, long-term picture of what Europe actually intends to buy. The next MFF and the European competitiveness fund can support this work, but at the same time, we should not measure success simply by how many millions are allocated to defence.

The real questions are more practical. Do we get bang for our buck? Are we producing enough equipment? Can procurement processes be faster? Are our critical supply chains secure enough? Can troops and equipment move across Europe when they are needed?

The Commission also has work to do. The Commission must prepare the legislation, together with military experts, the industry and Member States from the very beginning. Defence cannot be treated simply as another sector of the single market, and all of the knowledge is not in the Commission – 'cooperation' is the key word here.

And the EU should not try to build competitive structures with NATO. NATO remains the cornerstone of our collective defence, while the EU should concentrate to add real value to industrial policy, financing, sensible regulation and infrastructure. We should aim to build a European defence capability that also aims to strengthen NATO, not to duplicate structures that we already have.

If the Member States want a strong European contribution to defence, they also have to be prepared to make the necessary decisions themselves. We have enough strategies and initiatives. Now what we need is for Member States to implement what has been agreed, remove the practical obstacles and invest in the capabilities that Europe needs. This is what the Defence Readiness Omnibus package delivers.

paragraphs.text: Herr talman! Kommissionär. Europa behöver stärka sitt försvar. Varje medlemsland behöver göra mer. Varför? Jo, för att Ryssland kommer att utgöra ett långsiktigt hot mot Europa också efter den dagen när Putins anfallskrig mot Ukraina tar slut.

När vi stärker vårt försvar och vår förmåga att stå på egna ben handlar det ytterst om att värna vår frihet, vår säkerhet, vårt sätt att leva och bo i Europa. Därför måste vi nu se över vårt regelverk så att medlemsländerna kan göra mer tillsammans, snabbare och utan onödig byråkrati. Genom att stärka vår avskräckningsförmåga minskar vi också risken för att bli anfallna.

Putins brutala anfallskrig pågår natt som dag i Ukraina. Civila drabbas av drönarattacker. Människor dödas och familjer får sina hem förstörda. Europa har stött Ukraina allra mest. Men vi behöver göra mer, och behovet av luftförsvar är akut. Samtidigt måste vi stärka vår egen försvarsförmåga, satsa på vår försvarsindustri och innovation samt förenkla vår inre försvarsmarknad.

För mig är frågan om Europas försvar också personlig. I Finland vet vi vad det innebär att kämpa för sin självständighet och frihet mot Ryssland. I vinterkriget och fortsättningskriget slogs vi finländare för att försvara vår självständighet. Min far, liksom så många av hans jämnåriga, skickades till fronten. Min mor, liksom så många andra unga sjuksköterskestuderande, tog hand om sårade soldater på krigssjukhus runt om i vårt land. I dag är det Ukrainas folk som utkämpar samma kamp som mina föräldrar och deras generation. Ukraina behöver vårt stöd varje dag.

Men vår inre försvarsmarknad är alltför splittrad. Våra processer är alltför långsamma. Det behövs action för att vår industri snabbt ska kunna leverera de stridsvagnar, flygplan, drönare, luftvärnssystem, ammunition och den teknologi som vi behöver för att försvara oss. Därför är den här försvarsomnibusen ett väldigt viktigt startskott, ett första steg för att göra vår inre försvarsmarknad redo för den krävande tid vi lever i. I omnibusen fyrdubblar vi nu tröskelvärdet för upphandlingar till 2 miljoner euro. Det här minskar onödig byråkrati. Vi skapar flera allmänna licenser som sparar månader av tid när försvarsprodukter flyttas från ett EU-land till ett annat. Det här gynnar också små och medelstora företag, någonting som är väldigt viktigt för oss också i Team Europe.

Bästa kollegor. Det är ingen hemlighet att vi här i Europaparlamentet var mera ambitiösa än rådet – vi ville mera. Medlemsländerna har fortfarande hemläxor att göra. Nu är faktiskt inte rätt tid att förhala processer. Nu är inte rätt tid att bara tänka på sitt eget land. Nu är det rätt tid att agera och skapa ett starkt Europa, för vi behöver mera tillit till varandra, vi behöver starkare incitament för att utveckla försvarsteknologi och innovationer i Europa, och vi måste bli snabbare på att ta dem i bruk.

Försvarsomnibusen hjälper Europa att agera snabbare, och det är vår uppgift att skydda våra invånare. Det här är ett väldigt viktigt första steg. Tack till kommissionär Kubilius för också kommissionens viktiga insatser.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, Europe's security can no longer be taken for granted. Russia's war against Ukraine, growing geopolitical instability and increasingly sophisticated hybrid threats have fundamentally changed the security environment around us. Europeans understand this. According to a recent Eurobarometer poll, 68 % of Europeans believe their country's security is threatened by the current international situation, while 81 % support a common European defence and security policy. Obviously, we have a responsibility to protect our citizens, our territories, our democracy, and our security and prosperity. But what is also clear is that Europe's security can no longer be outsourced either. We need an autonomous capacity to plan, develop, produce, deploy and sustain the capabilities that are necessary for our own defence. That is not an inexpensive feat, so we need to put real money on the table, but strengthening European defence is not simply about spending more. EU defence expenditure reached EUR 418 billion in 2025, and it is projected to rise further. Yet only 24 % of equipment procurement was collaborative, well below the long‑standing 35 % European benchmark.

So we also have to change the way we spend, we have to change what we buy and how we cooperate. I do believe that joint procurement and European preference must become central principles of our long‑term defence investment, including in the Defence Procurement Directive and the future European competitiveness fund. This is also why the Defence Readiness Omnibus matters. It is part of translating defence readiness by 2030 into practice by removing unnecessary regulatory barriers, accelerating procedures and making our existing instruments better suited to today's security and industrial reality. The package is intended to facilitate defence investment, accelerate permitting and simplify intra‑EU transfers and procurement.

For the defence readiness file, we have secured important improvements to the European Defence Fund. I particularly welcome the strong inclusion of Ukraine. Cooperation with Ukrainian entities for testing activities can be supported through the EDF when it strengthens the competitiveness, efficiency and innovation capacity of the European defence industrial base. We also ensure that simplification does not come at the expense of quality, maintaining strong safeguards for how EDF funding is awarded. We also reached a compromise on access rights that responds to the legitimate interests of national authorities while protecting industry's intellectual property and incentives to innovate.

At the same time, we should acknowledge where we did not go far enough. The omnibus was also an opportunity to make real progress on simplifying intra‑EU transfers and defence procurement. It is disappointing that we were not able to deliver the same level of ambition here. We must also pay much closer attention to how our defence instruments work in practice, particularly for innovative start-ups and SMEs. Europe cannot afford to invest in promising technologies, only to see them fall into the so-called valleys of death, struggling to move from innovation to product, and from the product to actual orders and production. SMEs and start-ups are essential to Europe's defence industrial base. They bring specialised technologies, innovation and critical components. Our funding and procurement systems must therefore give them genuine access to finance, contracts and cross-border European supply chains.

Finally, let me stress that a stronger European defence industry is not only about security, and it does not only affect the expenditure side of the budget. It does not only take money out of our budget; it also strengthens innovation in technological sovereignty, competitiveness, skilled employment and our security of supply. So it's a win‑win if we do it right.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, oggi discutiamo un provvedimento sulle semplificazioni in materia di appalti di difesa, che probabilmente è utile ma è molto lontano da ciò che serve oggi all'Europa, anche perché gli Stati nazionali hanno annacquato i tentativi della Commissione e del Commissario Kubilius di avere una prima governance condivisa dei progetti.

Quando parliamo di difesa europea, dobbiamo pensare a una difesa comune. Nessun Paese si salva da solo in questo quadro internazionale e, anche dal punto di vista economico, il riarmo nazionale è inefficiente e inadatto alle sfide che abbiamo davanti.

Dobbiamo andare rapidamente verso una cooperazione rafforzata tra chi è disposto a condividere una politica estera comune e, quindi, una politica di difesa comune per essere al fianco dell'Ucraina e per esercitare al meglio una vera deterrenza contro qualsiasi azione diretta ai danni dei Paesi dell'Unione europea.

Questo pacchetto rende più semplice le procedure dei 27 Stati nazionali. Questo è positivo ma non può essere questa la via maestra. Troppo spesso gli Stati membri sviluppano separatamente la stessa capacità e acquistano separatamente gli stessi equipaggiamenti. Il risultato è semplice: spendiamo di più e otteniamo di meno.

Gli appalti congiunti devono diventare la regola, non l'eccezione. Ma c'è una condizione fondamentale: questi investimenti devono rafforzare l'industria europea. Per questo chiediamo che in tutti i posti in provvedimenti ci sia una European preference. Non possiamo parlare di autonomia strategica e allo stesso tempo utilizzare il nostro potere di spesa per creare nuove dipendenze industriali e tecnologiche.

In questo quadro, l'Ucraina deve essere un partner strategico dell'Europa. Sta difendendo con coraggio il proprio Paese ed è una nostra frontiera. Deve essere parte attiva di tutti i nostri progetti e, spero prima possibile, anche parte integrante della nostra Unione europea.

Andando al merito del provvedimento, che ho seguito come relatore in Commissione ENVI, in particolare riguardo alle deroghe sulle sostanze chimiche per i prodotti della difesa, ricordo l'importanza di trovare un giusto punto di equilibrio tra la necessaria prontezza e flessibilità del settore, senza rinunciare alle tutele ambientali. È questo d'altronde il senso di semplificare: eliminare gli ostacoli superflui ma non le garanzie necessarie. Quindi procediamo con questo omnibus.

Ringrazio ovviamente tutti gli altri relatori e relatori ombra ma lancio l'appello alla Commissione e ai 27 governi dei nostri Stati membri: costruiamo davvero l'Europa della difesa comune! Un'Europa che nasce da una politica estera comune, che stanzia budget ampi e condivisi, che fa appalti congiunti e laboratori scientifici transnazionali e che valorizza un sistema industriale europeo capace di garantire pace, sicurezza e innovazione.
Non limitiamoci a facilitare gli appalti per l'acquisto di prodotti che spesso sono stranieri: scegliamo invece la strada dell'Europa della difesa comune che crea un'industria della difesa comune.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Europe's next defence challenge is turning spending into military power. We must build faster while focusing on quality, interoperability and the capabilities we actually need today and tomorrow.

The priorities are clear. We need to scale up the production of ammunitions, missiles, drones and air defence systems, strengthen European defence manufacturing and supply chains, invest in intelligence, ISR, space, cyber and electronic warfare, increase investment in military mobility and logistics, and buy more jointly and reduce fragmented national programs. We must also rapidly build a stronger European pillar of NATO, capable of doing more without assuming that the US will do it for us. The goal is simple: a Europe that can credibly deter and, if necessary, also defend itself. More money is necessary, and this needs to be a joint effort between the public and private sectors. But speed, scale and coordination will determine whether that spending actually makes us safer.

On hybrid threats: we must respond with resilience, deterrence and attribution rather than treating every hybrid attack as a purely military problem. Russia should not be allowed to believe that operating below the threshold of conventional war means operating below the threshold of consequences. We must protect our critical infrastructure, strengthen Europe's technology base and cyber defence, improve intelligence and attribution, counter foreign interference, and ensure that hostile actions – from sabotage to cyberattacks – face a coordinated European response.

Technology and data are crucial part of defence. Europe cannot be strategically secure while remaining critically dependent on foreign providers for cloud, for software, for semiconductors and cybersecurity. In most sensitive sectors, we need trusted and secure supply chains, stronger European alternatives and clear rules to reduce dangerous dependencies on high-risk vendors. We should use European investment and public procurement much more strategically to help European technologies to scale.

At the same time, we need interoperability and open standards so that governments, armed forces and critical infrastructure operators are never locked into a single provider they cannot replace. Cyber defence must also become much more operational. We need stronger European capabilities to detect attacks early, share threat intelligence in real time, protect critical networks and rapidly recover when systems are compromised.

Technological resilience must become part of deterrence, and adversaries must know that attacking Europe's digital infrastructure will not paralyse us, and that such attacks will be detected and met with consequences.

Ultimately, European defence is not just about tanks, aircrafts and missiles. It is about factories, supply chains, satellites, software, data, networks and the resilience of our societies. Strategic security requires strategic capacity and capabilities and this is what we are here to support. This is what we are here to deliver.
