paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, for our defence readiness, we often need more: more money, more production, more weapons, more equipment. But sometimes we need less: less complication, less restrictions, less red tape. When it comes to regulating the defence industry, as the saying goes: less is more. And I know you agree. So I thank you for your provisional agreement with the Council on the Defence Readiness Omnibus and the massive majorities in the committees, which show that we are as one for the defence of Europe.

When I started as Commissioner, I called for a big bang in defence. And in the last two years we created a big bang in financial resources: EUR 150 billion in SAFE loans, EUR 60 billion in the Ukraine support loan for defence and Member States pledged trillions by 2035. But for production to ramp up, money alone is not enough. As our friend, NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte, says: we are not at war, but not at peace either. Ukraine shows: when war comes, you need to scale up very quickly.

Our goal is to keep peace on the European continent. And to that end, we need to prevent war and deter aggression. And our deterrence depends on speed. If we are slow and inefficient, Putin will not hesitate to test us. That is why we are updating our peacetime rulebook for these dangerous times and drastically cutting red tape for our defence industry with the Defence Readiness Omnibus. This is the beginning of simplification. Big bang in defence.

So I thank the rapporteurs: Lucia Yar and Henrik Dahl on fast track permitting; Pekka Toveri and Anna-Maja Henriksson on intra-EU transfers; and Sven Mikser and Aura Salla on defence investment. I thank you and all the shadow rapporteurs. I was there at every trilogue. We had good negotiations, a good result. So thank you for doing a great job – a great job for Europe's defence readiness.

First with new, simpler permitting rules. In some Member States right now, it can take industry four years – not two years but four years – to get a permit to build a new factory. So basically, if you ask for the permit now, you can, maybe, start building four years from now. That undermines our defence readiness. We are putting an end to these dangerous delays, with a maximum 42-working-day permitting deadline, maximum 102 days in complex cases. And tacit approval: no answer – you are good to go. Putting an end to uncertainty so industry can speed up investment and expand production.

Second, we are helping industry to ramp up by making sure industry can access critical chemicals. Our defence readiness depends on chemicals – chemicals for explosives and firing ammunition. We provide exemptions to allow use of chemicals for defence readiness and greater legal clarity. We have found the right balance between defending the environment and defending Europe from Russian aggression.

Third, we are encouraging innovation, by simplifying procedures for the European Defence Fund – a European success story for research and development. New, simpler rules will make the European Defence Fund even more attractive for small, innovative companies and allow for quick response to meet urgent defence needs and to meet real battlefield needs by allowing testing in Ukraine, making our defence industry stronger and bringing also quality jobs all over Europe.

Defence ramp up depends also on demand, from Member States, governments and armies. We have made it easier for them to buy defence products with higher limits in procurement rules, so governments can focus on the biggest, most important orders and also possibilities for joint procurement, for big European orders that industry needs.

Finally, intra-EU transfers. Today, a true EU defence market does not exist. Defence products can be stuck on the border between two Member States, sometimes for months, even if they are fully co-produced and co-licensed – that will not help our defence readiness. But here too, we made progress. We have made it easier to move defence products between two Member States. We reduced barriers and introduced new general transfer licences. I know that both of us would have liked to be still more ambitious, but for me this is a good compromise.

Also, because we all agree: work on the European defence market must continue. In its June conclusions, the European Council stressed the importance 'of the proper functioning and further integration of the European defence market across the Union' – this is a quote from the conclusions. And in March you, the European Parliament, called for a stronger and more integrated defence market in an excellent own initiative report. Together we will make it happen. Before the end of the year, the Commission will present our defence market package.

And just to conclude: honourable Members, dear colleagues, dear friends, as I said in the beginning, less is more. I call on you in the vote this week. Vote for much less red tape, which means much more defence readiness. Our ability to defend ourselves depends on it. Our ability to deter aggression, to prevent war, depends on it.

interventions.speaker_label: Vytenis Povilas Andriukaitis, rapporteur for the opinion of the ENVI Committee.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: rapporteur for the opinion of the ENVI Committee

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear Commissioner Andrius, colleagues, it is important to highlight that defence, public interest and social protection are not in conflict with each other. The purpose of defence spending is to safeguard citizens' well-being, dignity and democracy.

Last night, a NATO jet shot down a drone over Lithuania and a Russian warship fired two emergency flares at a Danish helicopter. In a war, drones fly far and attacks can reach every European Union Member State.

Therefore, we need to streamline our defence capabilities to ensure the protection of our citizens. The so‑called defence omnibus gives the initiative a more European character with enhanced cross‑border cooperation, access for small and medium enterprises, start‑ups and our partners from Ukraine.
We need to make sure we have the resources and ability to shield and protect ourselves. Otherwise, non-EU in defence will cost a lot.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Salvatore De Meo, a nome del gruppo PPE.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, l'omnibus sulla difesa rappresenta un passo importante per rendere l'Europa più autonoma, più pronta, più competitiva e in grado di rispondere tempestivamente alle minacce di una situazione politica sempre più complessa.

Semplificare le procedure, rendere più efficienti e congiunti gli appalti significa voler accelerare la realizzazione delle infrastrutture necessarie per rispondere a quelle che sono le nostre esigenze di sicurezza ma soprattutto superare i tempi burocratici che la sicurezza europea non può più permettersi.

Come relatore ombra del PPE all'interno della Commissione IMCO, voglio ringraziare i relatori per l'ottimo lavoro fatto, per aver voluto dare un lavoro con cui voler armonizzare le procedure in tutti gli Stati, con scadenze chiare e uguali per tutti, individuando un punto unico nazionale e, soprattutto, favorire così l'impegno delle piccole e medie imprese nella realizzazione delle infrastrutture necessarie.

Anche sull'approvazione tacita abbiamo difeso un principio chiaro: le eccezioni devono restare eccezioni. Non possiamo introdurre procedure più veloci e poi lasciare scappatoie che rischiano di riportarci alle vecchie lentezze.

Questo provvedimento evidenzia la nostra esigenza di semplificare le procedure, perché abbiamo un quadro troppo complesso e soprattutto serve a far capire che l'Europa ha bisogno di acquisire autonomia, di essere meno dipendente, perché solo in questo modo – lo diceva bene il Commissario – possiamo garantire ai nostri cittadini, alle nostre imprese, alla nostra economia, quell'autonomia e quella credibilità che ci permette di recuperare uno spazio importante e credibile sullo scenario geopolitico internazionale.

interventions.speaker_label: Γιάννης Μανιάτης, εξ ονόματος της ομάδας S&D.

paragraphs.text: Κυρία Πρόεδρε, κύριε Επίτροπε, θα ήθελα να ξεκινήσω ευχαριστώντας τους εισηγητές για την πολύ καλή συνεργασία. Κατά τη διάρκεια των διαπραγματεύσεων για την αναθεώρηση των δύο οδηγιών για τις ενδοενωσιακές μεταφορές και τις δημόσιες προμήθειες στην άμυνα, αναδείχθηκε, δυστυχώς, η απροθυμία του Συμβουλίου να κατανοήσει το νέο γεωπολιτικό περιβάλλον στο οποίο βρισκόμαστε. Μπλόκαρε κάθε ουσιαστική αλλαγή που πρότεινε η Επιτροπή και το Κοινοβούλιο, πηγαίνοντας απέναντι και στο πνεύμα της απλοποίησης, που ήταν ο στόχος της νομοθετικής πρότασης. Όμως, χωρίς περισσότερη συνεργασία, χωρίς κοινές προμήθειες, χωρίς αυτοματοποιημένες αναγνωρίσεις και χωρίς ισχυρή ρήτρα ευρωπαϊκής προτίμησης για την ενίσχυση της ευρωπαϊκής παραγωγής και τη μείωση των εξαρτήσεων από τρίτες χώρες, δεν θα πετύχουμε τον στόχο μας. Δεν αρκεί μόνο να αυξήσουμε τους αμυντικούς προϋπολογισμούς. Αν θέλουμε να έχουμε μια ισχυρή Ευρώπη, πρέπει να κάνουμε και περισσότερα, αλλά και μαζί. Για τον λόγο αυτό, αγαπητέ Επίτροπε, πρέπει να παρουσιάσετε άμεσα νέες νομοθετικές προτάσεις που θα θέσουν τις βάσεις για μια πραγματικά κοινή ευρωπαϊκή αγορά για την άμυνα.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Pierre-Romain Thionnet, au nom du groupe PfE.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, investir davantage dans la défense, réduire nos dépendances extérieures, produire plus et plus vite: tout cela est nécessaire dans le contexte international, et tout cela exige de créer un environnement réglementaire, normatif et financier ultra-favorable à l'industrie de défense.

Chacun doit être à sa place ici. Les États avec un rôle décisionnaire central, et même unique. La Commission comme intendance, comme organe chargé de mettre en application les dispositions ou de débloquer les fonds convenus entre États. Cette subsidiarité, inscrite dans nos traités, doit être respectée scrupuleusement.

C'est le cas avec cet omnibus de simplification consacré au secteur de la défense. Il comporte de nombreuses modifications de bon sens, revendiquées et soutenues par nos industriels, nos entrepreneurs, en particulier par nos PME. Les lourdeurs administratives doivent être réduites à leur strict minimum. Les États qui souhaitent coopérer ou acheter ensemble ne doivent pas être gênés par des lourdeurs bureaucratiques.

La Commission européenne, encouragée par certains groupes politiques du Parlement, a tenté d'utiliser cet omnibus pour s'attribuer des compétences en matière de gouvernance. Elle a échoué. Son échec nous prouve une chose: il est parfaitement possible de faciliter l'activité de l'industrie de défense et la coopération entre États sans transférer de pouvoirs supplémentaires à Bruxelles. Il est parfaitement possible d'être plus productif sans aller vers plus d'intégration.
Les choix nationaux et la structure confédérale européenne ne sont pas des obstacles. Ils sont la seule solution non seulement légitime, mais efficace.

interventions.speaker_label: Reinis Pozņaks, on behalf of the ECR Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the ECR Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, the goal of Omnibus V was to simplify military transfers and procurement procedures, and we succeeded on this. At the same time, we also tried to strengthen the European defence industry. We tried to hit two birds with one stone but almost dropped it on our own foot.

Europe's defence autonomy is the right goal – it is a must. But we cannot force long-term goals into a short-term time frame. We are losing too much time on debates trying to do so. And time is the most limited resource we have.

Countries close to Russia simply do not have the time to wait until Europe develops all the capabilities we need, and I am glad that we managed to keep our defence market open to our strategic defence partners. Countries like Canada, the United Kingdom and Norway – whose soldiers, by the way, are already on the ground defending Europe's eastern flank.
We need to build a stronger European defence industry for tomorrow, but without limiting our ability to defend Europe today.

interventions.speaker_label: Nikola Minchev, on behalf of the Renew Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Renew Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Mr Commissioner, dear colleagues, tomorrow we vote on three important pieces of defence legislation that can help us move faster in closing our defence investment and capability gaps. In practice, this means less paperwork, faster procurement and fewer obstacles to moving equipment across the EU, so getting the right capabilities to the right place at the right time.

Russia's war against Ukraine has reminded us of something we should never forget: peace can never be taken for granted and we must be ready to act. In terms of spending, Member States are already stepping up. Defence spending increased by 20 % last year, reaching EUR 418 billion. But spending more is only part of it; the key is to invest smarter and make the most of working together, closing the gaps and avoiding duplications. We cannot afford 27 separate efforts pulling in different directions. We are stronger when we work together, coordinate and cooperate. That is our strength, and that is how we build a Europe that is ready to protect its citizens, defend its interests and contribute to peace and stability, not just on paper, but also on the ground.

interventions.speaker_label: Reinier Van Lanschot, on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, getting the capabilities to protect ourselves is a huge task, as if we are running a marathon together. Money alone is not enough. We remain fragmented and slow. These new defence laws could have made us go full sprint.

On the permits we succeeded. This will slash lead times from years to months, but we will not buy equipment together. There will still be no real single market for defence. Because of our stubborn national leaders, we are not running, we have stumbled over the first steps.

These national leaders make big promises in public and then block ambitious European action behind closed doors. Like ostriches, they hide their heads in national soil and hope the danger will go away.

Russia will only attack us if we are weak and we know how to become strong: with the real European Defence Union. So, national leaders, get out of your nationalistic trenches and start sprinting. Let's not wait for war to unite us. Let's unite to prevent war.

interventions.speaker_label: Marc Botenga, au nom du groupe The Left.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: au nom du groupe The Left

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, vous parlez de sécurité, mais moi, je veux quand même vous poser la question: quand vous célébrez la flexibilisation des règles – moins de règles, moins de procédures – à la sécurité de qui est-ce que vous pensez?

Parce que nous avons aujourd'hui une loi qui limite en Europe l'utilisation des polluants éternels, genre PFAS. Clairement, la loi ne suffit pas, si on voit le nombre de cancers provoqués par le PFAS partout en Europe. Et qu'est-ce que vous proposez? C'est de dire que désormais, cette évaluation, elle sera moins sévère et on pourra passer outre si jamais c'est dans l'intérêt des profits des entreprises de l'armement.

Nous avons une loi européenne qui oblige les entreprises à un minimum de transparence par rapport aux produits toxiques qu'ils utilisent – essentiel pour la santé des travailleurs et des riverains. Et qu'est-ce que vous dites? On va réduire cette transparence pour les usines de l'armement. Les gens seront désormais empoisonnés sans le savoir.

Et finalement, un gouvernement qui veut vérifier la toxicité pour une installation, il n'aura plus que 42 jours au lieu de 2 à 3 ans. Et vous célébrez cela? Je ne crois pas qu'il y ait quoi que ce soit à célébrer. Ce texte va tuer et vous allez tuer au profit des actionnaires de la guerre.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, thanks a lot for a very good debate and thanks a lot, really, for the job which was done, as I said at the beginning, for the provisional agreement on the Defence Readiness Omnibus.

I definitely agree with those who are saying that speed in the development of our defence readiness is a crucial matter. That is why, in my view, this omnibus, which we did now, is just the beginning.

It will take time for us to adapt despite the fact that the dangers and threats are imminent. But, definitely, we are still living with a lot of old rules which were made during peacetime. During peacetime, the needs of defence are sometimes forgotten, and now we are, as Mark Rutte was saying and I will repeat again, not at war but not at peace either – so that is why defence is a necessity.

We need to take that very seriously and look through all our rules which, perhaps, were good for peacetime, but are not so good for a time when we need to be ready for our defence. And that is why we were looking for compromises, even when we are talking about environmental protection and chemicals.

Now, second, what we need to understand is that what we are living through in defence is something which is happening once in a hundred years' time. There is now some kind of need to look into how the structures and the whole collective defence architecture in Europe, which was created back in 1949 when NATO was created, can be transformed, taking into account what our transatlantic partners are deciding in their National Defense Strategy and National Security Strategy and what they are speaking about when they talk about NATO 3.0.

So this is a very big task for us, for our generation: to be ready to build a European collective defence architecture, which will be much more European. And that is why, when we talk about either Brussels grabbing power or something like that, that there is no need to change anything – this is the wrong approach. All of us together, we need to build such a structure which would allow us to be really ready to defend ourselves in such a way as to deter any kind of threats which can come to our continent.

So, I myself say that we are living through what they would call a 'status quo crisis'. As it was until now, it will not be anymore. So we need to be ready for that change. But as I am always quoting, Jean Monnet always said that the European Community will be built during the crises. So this is a time for us to build a European community for defence.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Szanowni Państwo! Ja nie chcę dzisiaj mówić o rynku wewnętrznym. Chcę mówić o tym, że Putin ma przegrać. Rosja ma przegrać, bo musi przegrać. To jest nasze główne zadanie, a cała reszta to są po prostu szczegóły. Przecież już we wrześniu zeszłego roku na polskim niebie pojawiły się drony nad domami, w których spali ludzie. Dzwonili do mnie ludzie i mówili, że wychodzili na podwórko sprawdzać, czy coś tam spadło. Bali się. I wy też się boicie tej nocy, która nie będzie ćwiczeniem alarmu. Takiego strachu nie ma się co wstydzić.

Mówię wam o tym wszystkim, bo wiemy, co trzeba zrobić, żeby pokonać Rosję. Zobaczcie, czego boi się Putin. On się boi, że się ogarniemy i jeszcze bardziej się zjednoczymy. Bo on liczy, ile miesięcy zajmuje nam przewiezienie komponentu z Francji do Polski. I jak liczy, że długo, to myśli sobie OK, można będzie lecieć dalej, jak już przejdzie do drugiej fazy wojny.

I teraz zobaczcie. Nasz rynek wewnętrzny, to nie jest jakiś wymysł. To jest nasza broń. Bo żeby Putin przegrał, będziemy musieli produkować i kupować szybciej, niż on niszczy. I pierwsze kroki w deregulacji zrobiliśmy dobrze, ale przed nami uproszczenie zamówień publicznych. Na to się teraz umówiliśmy. I teraz wszyscy: parlament, państwa, prezydencja, komisja musimy tego pilnować i się z tego wywiązać. Tak będzie dobrze, kiedy w zamówieniach publicznych zamienimy miesiące na dni. Putin ma przegrać. Działamy dalej.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señor comisario, los ataques rusos cada vez se sienten más cerca de nuestras casas, y esto nos tiene que enfrentar a la realidad que todavía no parece que asumamos, que es nuestra responsabilidad; porque Rusia intenta generar miedo, probar nuestros límites y, sobre todo, dividirnos.

Necesitamos más Europa, más cooperación y una industria europea con menos dependencias estratégicas. No se trata de gastar más ni de que cada país vaya por su lado: tenemos que invertir mejor, hacerlo juntos, reforzando así nuestra capacidad industrial y tecnológica; porque la guerra ha cambiado: hoy se hace con misiles y drones, pero también con sabotajes, ciberataques y desinformación.
Además, estamos solos. Europa ya no puede dar por hecho que otros garanticen siempre su seguridad. Necesitamos autonomía, precisamente, para proteger nuestra democracia y nuestro modelo social.
En definitiva, tenemos que dejar de mirarnos de reojo entre nosotros e ir todos a una en la defensa europea, porque en este barco vamos todos juntos: o nos salvamos todos o nos hundimos todos.

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedající, balíček legislativy týkající se obranného omnibusu respektuje jeden základní princip, a to, že obrana zůstává především odpovědností členských států. Komise nesmí získávat větší pravomoci nad citlivými rozhodnutími o převodech nebo zadávání zakázek, nesmí nahrazovat rozhodování na národní úrovni. Proti tomu jsme se při projednávání tohoto balíčku jasně vymezili a tyto pravomoci nakonec do legislativy zahrnuty nebyly.

Podle nás ale mohlo být nařízení odvážnější, zejména v podpoře malých a středních podniků. Právě ty jsou důležitým zdrojem inovací v evropském obranném průmyslu. Menší firmy stále narážejí na příliš mnoho překážek při zadávání zakázek, při přístupu k financování i při zapojování do evropských dodavatelských řetězců.

Evropská obranná politika nemůže být nastavena hlavně ve prospěch největších dodavatelů a nesmí se stát další záminkou pro větší centralizaci v Bruselu. Podporujeme proto opatření, která obrannému průmyslu usnadní výrobu, spolupráci a dodávky. Naše priority ale zůstávají jasné a stejné. Méně byrokracie, silnější a nezávislé národní obranné průmysly, lepší podmínky pro malé a střední podniky a především zachování rozhodovacích pravomocí v rukou členských států.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, we cannot fight on two fronts at the same time. The EU and its Member States are rightly spending resources on supporting Ukraine and building up our defence. The other front is bureaucratic, sometimes more vicious than the first one. Our defence industry cannot be expected to deliver more, produce faster and compete globally while being tied down by excessive green Brussels bureaucracy.

That is why I welcome the compromise we have reached. It is not perfect, but it creates more opportunity for European businesses and gives our defence industry greater room to invest, innovate and increase production. We need European companies that can respond quickly. Putin will not wait until we will fight the right form, so we need to go forward.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, Europe must be able to defend itself. For that, we need a strong, competitive and innovative European defence industry.
The defence omnibus is an important step forward. Less bureaucracy, faster procedures and better conditions for our companies to invest and cooperate.

We also are improving the European Defence Fund by supporting SMEs and strengthening cross‑border cooperation. And when Member States co‑finance defence projects, they should be able to negotiate appropriate access to the results they helped finance.
Our goal is clear: use European taxpayers money effectively, reduce dependence on third countries and strengthen Europe's ability to take responsibility for its own security.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, the Russian aggression is testing us too. Drone attacks, disinformation, low-level agents, the need to scale up our defence industry and the costs that come with it. And when a challenge becomes too big for Member States, such as this one, they call on Europe to fix it, and rightly so, because together we are stronger and together is the only chance we have.

But what do Member States do after calling on Europe to act? They deny Europe the money and the powers and the information to do the job, and then they block every little progress behind closed doors in council, as they did on these files, and then they go home and blame Europe for failing.
This is not how you protect European citizens, nor how you deter Russia. This is how you undermine the only solution you have.

So to Paris, Madrid, The Hague, Rome and everyone else: stop asking Europe to deliver while denying Europe the means to deliver. Let's prepare, produce, deter together and give this House the powers it needs to provide proper oversight over all of this.
And dear Commissioner, you can very well be more ambitious.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, Euroopan puolustusvalmiutta on vahvistettava, mutta nopeampi ei saa tarkoittaa heikommin valvottua.

Venäjän hyökkäyssota Ukrainassa on osoittanut, että Euroopan on kyettävä tuottamaan tarvitsemiaan puolustusmateriaaleja ja toimimaan kriittisissä kriiseissä nykyistä nopeammin. Siksi lupamenettelyjä on perusteltua sujuvoittaa, puolustusmateriaalin siirtoja jäsenmaiden välillä helpottaa ja eurooppalaista tuotantokykyä vahvistaa.

Mutta kiire ei oikeuta luopumaan ympäristöasioista, avoimuudesta tai demokraattisesta valvonnasta. Julkisten miljardien käytön on oltava läpinäkyvää, ja siihen on vahvistettava Euroopan omaa osaamista ja teollista kapasiteettia. Turvallisuus ei myöskään synny siitä, että 27 jäsenmaata hankkii kiireessä kukin omansa. Tarvitsemme enemmän yhteistä suunnittelua, yhteisiä hankintoja ja omavaraisuutta.
Puolustusvalmius ei rakennu vain aseista. Se rakentuu osaamisesta, teollisuudesta, logistiikasta, huoltovarmuudesta ja ennen kaikkea eurooppalaisesta yhteistyöstä.

paragraphs.text: Г-жо Председател, искам да кажа, че свършихме наистина добра работа по това законодателство, и специално поздравявам и благодаря на нашите докладчици, нашите представители в преговорите за това, че постигнаха и много добър резултат в преговорите с правителствата в рамките на Съвета на Европейския съюз. Резултат над очакванията ни.

Но ще бъда съвсем откровен. Аз не се надявам, не съм оптимист, че това законодателство лесно ще се превърне в действително по-малко бюрократични пречки за предприятията, а още по-малко в това, което е целта му - обща, жива, динамична европейска отбранителна индустрия, която заедно да покрие нуждите на общата европейска отбрана.

Повече от две години след като започнахме активно да говорим за обща европейска отбрана, се чувствам по-скоро обезсърчен, по-скоро загрижен, отколкото оптимист, защото виждам как продължават да надделяват национални и корпоративни тънки сметки, как ревността на национално ниво продължава да надделява над общия ни интерес. Сякаш повечето правителства остават загрижени за своите фирми, за своите бюджети, а това не е обща отбрана. Нужна ни е рамка, това нямаме - рамка, в която действително да видим европейски отбранителен съюз в много близко бъдеще.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, colleagues, we support the aim of the regulation to speed up permits for defence readiness projects. Europe is investing more in defence, and we need to turn that investment into real capabilities and infrastructure to support them faster. But speed cannot come at the expense of safety. We have worked to make sure that shorter deadlines do not mean weaker environmental or labour standards, or greater risk to people's health and lives. The procedures should be faster, but the quality of the assessment must remain the same. That too is part of security. A strong European defence must make Europe safer and more resilient while preserving the social model, public health and democratic values that we are trying to defend.

If Europe can make procedures faster and more predictable in defence, we should aim for the same efficiency in other strategic areas, such as healthcare, water, transport and critical infrastructure. Security is multidimensional, which means being able to defend European territory, but also having strong societies, resilient infrastructure and the capacity to protect people when crises come. Defence readiness and social resilience must go hand in hand. And now it is time for governments to implement and deliver.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Európa védelmi képességének fejlesztése nyilvánvaló stratégiai szükségszerűség. Első és szinte kizárólagos feladatunk az európai polgárok biztonságának a megerősítése, de nem mindegy, hogy ezt hogyan tesszük. Az Európai Védelmi Alap célja nem az, hogy egy Unión kívüli háborús konfliktus finanszírozásának eszközévé váljon. Erre nagyon sok más, megszavazott, jóváhagyott módozat van. Legyen világos: az európai védelmi képességek megerősítése nem keverhető össze az orosz agresszió következtében kialakult valóban tragikus ukrajnai háborús helyzettel.

De van itt még egy alapvető probléma, a visszamenőleges hatály. Az Unión kívül végzett védelmi eszközök tesztelésének költségei utólag, 2025. január 1-jével válhatnak elszámolhatóvá. Egy súlyos kérdést vet fel a jogbiztonság és a tisztességes verseny szempontjából. Ha most visszamenőleg megváltoztatjuk a szabályokat, akkor az egyik projekt utólag olyan pénzügyi előnyhöz jut, amit a másik projekt gazdája nem is tudott róla. Nem fogadhatjuk el, hogy az Európai Unió utólag változtassa meg a finanszírozás szabályait, az EU hitelességét ássa alá a gazdasági szereplők között. Igen, Európa biztonságát szinte mindenáron erősíteni kell, de ne úgy, hogy közben feladjuk a jogbiztonságot, az átláthatóságot és az európai adófizetők értékeit.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Szanowni Państwo! Bardzo cieszę się z tego, że jestem posłem do Parlamentu Europejskiego z Bydgoszczy – z miasta i regionu kluczowego dla przemysłu zbrojeniowego nie tylko w Polsce i Europie, ale także na świecie. W Bydgoszczy i jej sąsiedztwie znajdują się Zakłady Chemiczne „Nitro-Chem” – największy w Europie i jeden z największych na świecie producentów trotylu i materiałów wybuchowych, kluczowy dostawca dla armii państw NATO, Wojskowe Zakłady Lotnicze nr 2 – remontujące i modernizujące wojskowe statki powietrzne, nie tylko polskie, ale natowskie, i Bydgoskie Zakłady Elektromechaniczne „Belma”, producent min.

Jeśli chcemy wzmacniać bezpieczeństwo, musimy stworzyć warunki dla szybkiego rozwoju zdolności produkcyjnych. Dlatego szczególnie w sektorze obronnym trzeba ograniczać zbędną biurokrację, którą oczywiście ograniczać trzeba wszędzie. Nasz przemysł zbrojeniowy potrzebuje możliwości szybkiego zwiększenia produkcji i inwestowania, a nie zbędnych barier administracyjnych.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, Chairman, on Sunday, Russia carried out yet another attack close to the Polish border. Another reminder that Russia is not only brutally attacking Ukraine. The threat to Europe is growing and we need to act.
We need a stronger European defence industry. With NATO becoming less predictable, we need to think differently about capacity building. We need to build capabilities here in Europe together.
But faster cannot mean careless. We must be able to produce more without exposing our citizens to dangerous chemicals, unstable production, or creating new dependencies on other powers.
That is why I am proud of the compromise we have reached. We can build faster, we can build more and we can still protect the people we seek to protect. This is the Europe we can trust.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, everyone tells Brussels to cut the red tape. And when we try, they say no. I support the defence omnibus. Europe needs to build defence equipment faster together, but let's be honest: if the goal was ten times better, we got maybe two. Parliament wanted to move fast. The problem sits in our capitals, where defence is still treated only as a national matter, not a European one. Here is one simple picture: a company wants to send drone parts across the border inside our own Union. It still needs separate national paperwork, and almost every time we asked for these rules to be the same throughout Europe, our governments said no. So what does that mean? Our soldiers are asked to stand together while our industries are left apart and buried in paperwork. This file, like every file like it, should make Europe stronger together, and our Member States need to wake up.

paragraphs.text: Madam Chair, this law says it all about the EU's obsession with militarisation. It calls the war on Ukraine a possibility to test weapons in a 'live experience of modern warfare'. European citizens are deeply supportive of Ukraine, but they expect the EU to be working towards a just and lasting peace. Instead, we are letting the defence industry make Ukraine their testing ground and paying them to do it. We are making exemptions to allow the defence industry to use toxic chemicals – this endangers those exposed during testing and all workers in the defence industry.

In the negotiations, Council officials could provide no examples of when these exemptions could be essential for national security, but still had no qualms in extending them even to products that could be used by civilians.
This legislation is about boosting the enormous profits of the defence industry with no concern for societal needs. So tomorrow, support our amendment and reject this war-mongering text.

Nihče si ni predstavljal, da je vojna v 21. stoletju na evropskih tleh mogoča, ampak se je zgodila. In ko govorimo o obrambi in obrambnih izdatkih, dejansko govorimo o suverenosti Evropske unije.

Doslej smo bili popolnoma odvisni od naših prijateljev v Združenih državah Amerike in zlasti tisti, ki govorite in si želite naše strateške suverenosti, je prva stvar, ki bi jo morali podpreti, povečane obrambne izdatke. Da zgradimo tisto, kar v zadnjih desetletjih nismo.

Še zlasti, če se bodo Američani pomaknili proti Pacifiku, je nujno, da si zgradimo zmogljivosti, da se bomo sposobni sami sebe braniti, ker le na takšen način bomo prihodnjim generacijam zagotovili mir.

In obrambni omnibus, ki je danes pred nami, razumem kot dokument, kako lahko naredimo skupaj in več. In to je tista prava smer, ki jo zagovarjam, ki jo podpiram, vendar je pred nami še dolga pot. Ne smemo zapraviti niti dneva. Gre za varnost in prihodnost naših otrok.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, signor Commissario, cari colleghi, ancora una volta l'Europa è chiamata a una scelta: restare una somma di 27 sistemi nazionali oppure diventare finalmente più forte, anche nella capacità di garantire la propria sicurezza.
Una vera Unione europea della difesa significa mettere insieme risorse, competenze, ricerca e capacità industriali, favorire gli acquisti comuni e superare frammentazioni e duplicazioni.

Perché la difesa comune non riguarda soltanto la sicurezza, riguarda anche quale Europa vogliamo costruire: più autonoma, più capace di innovare, di creare lavoro qualificato e di valorizzare tutti i suoi territori da nord a sud. E questa è la direzione del programma di prontezza alla difesa per il 2030.
Non si tratta soltanto di spendere di più ma di spendere meglio, insieme e in Europa, perché essere più forti significa essere più liberi nelle nostre scelte, più credibili nel difendere la pace.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Wir sollten diesen Verteidigungsomnibus vielleicht besser Panzer nennen. Das wäre etwas ehrlicher, auch den Menschen gegenüber. Aber eines muss man, glaube ich, hier auch einmal festhalten: Wir sind hier kein Verteidigungsbündnis, geschätzte Kollegen – und auch Herr Kommissar, denn wenn man Ihnen zugehört hat, dann ist einem das ein bisschen so vorgekommen, als ob wir das wären. Dafür gibt es eine andere Organisation, und wer das behauptet, hat die Verträge wohl nicht durchdringend verstanden.

Und, geschätzte Kollegen, dieser Bericht enthält einen entlarvenden Satz. Dort steht nämlich: Verteidigungsbereitschaft ist auf einen sicheren, leistbaren und widerstandsfähigen Zugang zu Energie angewiesen. Plötzlich kommt also die Brüsseler Nomenklatur darauf, dass wir vielleicht auch leistbare Energie in Europa brauchen könnten. Sobald es um Aufrüstung und um Kriegsvorbereitung und Kriegstreiberei geht, brauchen wir günstige Energie. Für unsere Bürger aber und für die Industrie wurde nie etwas – jahrelang nicht – für eine günstige Energie getan, sondern ideologisch vergiftete Klimapolitik betrieben.

Der russische Angriff auf die Ukraine ist klar zu verurteilen. Doch wer Milliarden für Waffen und Sanktionen bereitstellt, während Diplomatie zur Randnotiz wird, betreibt keine Friedenspolitik, sondern verschärft nur die Eskalation. Die Rechnung zahlen Familienbetriebe und Arbeitnehmer in Europa mit hohen Preisen, Unsicherheit und verlorenen Industrieplätzen. Leistbare Energie darf kein Privileg der Aufrüstung sein. Sie ist Grundlage für Wohlstand und Frieden.
Schluss mit dieser Doppelmoral, die hier seit Jahr und Tag gespielt wird! Europa braucht Diplomatie statt Kriegstreiberei und Energiepolitik für die Menschen, die sie leistbar macht.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, la fotografia di famiglia di questo fine settimana è stata India, Cina e Russia insieme in India.

Commissario Kubilius, lei è uno dei pochi Commissari con un approccio molto pratico e oggi ce l'ha ribadito. Non è tempo né di pace né di guerra ed è in crisi lo status quo. Allora noi non possiamo chiedere all'industria europea di produrre per la nostra sicurezza, mentre con altre politiche, sempre dentro la Commissione, rendiamo economicamente impossibile produrre in Europa.

Io apprezzo e sosterremo le semplificazioni di Omnibus e tutti gli altri atti che seguiranno perché oggi dobbiamo avere la capacità di produrre in Europa, di investire in ricerca in Europa, di fare prototipi, di fare test che possano salvaguardare la nostra capacità di stare in autonomia.

Ma, d'altra parte, stiamo perdendo capacità. L'automotive è collegato; le raffinerie, la siderurgia, le filiere manifatturiere sono collegate all'industria della difesa, perché i carri armati non vanno a batteria, gli aerei militari hanno bisogno di carburante e un sistema d'arma non si costruisce senza acciaio.
E con questo approccio noi sosteniamo tutte le semplificazioni che lei vorrà fare.

paragraphs.text: Priekšsēdētāja kungs, dārgais komisāra kungs! Sabotāža, dronu uzlidojumi, dedzināšana kļūst par mūsu ikdienas realitāti. Un, ja daudzi Eiropā joprojām domā, ka Ukraina – tas ir kaut kur tur, ļoti, ļoti tālu, tad Putina Krievija jau atklāti runā, ka tā ir karā ar kolektīvajiem Rietumiem, kā viņi to sauc.

Es domāju, ka tas ir jāuztver nopietni. Tikai vienoti mēs būsim stipri, un Eiropas sadrumstalotība ir ārkārtīgi, ārkārtīgi bīstama. Es domāju, ka šajā perspektīvā Omnibus ir solis ļoti pareizā virzienā. Tagad, protams, uzdevums ir tikai ieviest to dzīvē.

Es atgādināšu, kāda ir situācija. 80% aizsardzības iepirkumu joprojām ir tīri nacionāli. Pie tam vienu un to pašu preci dažādas valstis pērk no dažādiem piegādātājiem, tādā veidā vienkārši neizmantojot kopējas iepirkšanas iespējas. Valdības lolo savus nacionālos čempionus. Licencēšana ir ārkārtīgi smaga, ārkārtīgi birokrātiska, arī tehnoloģiju nodošana, kas Eiropas kopējās aizsardzības spējas, protams, ignorē.

Tagad mūsu uzdevums pēc Omnibus ir skatīties, lai to ieviestu dzīvē, un, otrām kārtām – iespējams, pat svarīgāk – raudzīties, lai nākamajā daudzgadu budžetā ir pietiekami daudz naudas kopīgiem iepirkumiem, kopīgai ražošanai, kopīgām inovācijām.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, in a world where imperialist Russia launches military attacks or otherwise destabilises all neighbours it considers weak, we must be able to defend ourselves. It is also important that we stand with Ukraine and help it defends its people.

But in a world where the United States attacks us by all non-military means, where Israel carries out ethnic cleansing and genocide, we must break away from these countries' military systems. That is why I support many of the aims of defence readiness.

However, I cannot accept that, in the name of these objectives, the protection of the environment and people is being neglected. Nor do I understand why Parliament sought to strip Member States of their rights over the projects they fund, acting in the interests of the largest arms companies and against the common good.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señor comisario, cuando hablamos de preparar nuestra defensa europea pensamos en baterías antimisiles, carros de combate y hasta en cazas de última generación. Pero a veces la realidad es mucho más sencilla.

El pasado 30 de julio 80 000 personas invadieron territorio europeo desde Marruecos, porque la ciudad de Ceuta no estaba preparada para poder resistir el ataque. No había personal, no había equipos y no había medios para frenar un ataque sin precedente en nuestra historia reciente. Pero lo que faltó fundamentalmente fue la voluntad política, que es siempre el primer paso para una defensa, que tiene que ser creíble, que tiene que ser contundente y disuasoria.

Señorías, Europa no puede seguir reaccionando tarde y confiando en que las amenazas vayan a desaparecer solas. Necesitamos capacidades, inversión y, sobre todo, voluntad política. Ha llegado el momento de elegir: o seguimos mirando hacia otro lado ante nuestras vulnerabilidades o construimos una Europa capaz de hacerse respetar y defenderse. Tiene todo nuestro apoyo, comisario.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, tämän lakikokonaisuuden myötä Euroopan puolustuskyky vahvistuu. Eurooppalaiset puolustusmarkkinat voivat kehittyä. Hyvä niin.

Erityisen merkittävää on, että annamme tässä tilaa myös pk-yrityksille osallistua eurooppalaisen puolustusmarkkinan syntymiseen, myös pienten maiden toimijoille. Vahvuutemme on, että eurooppalainen osaaminen pääsee kukoistamaan tämänkin lakiuudistuksen myötä.
Merkittävää on myös, että julkisin varoin rahoitettujen projektien tiedot ovat avoimia rahoittajille ja että ne, jotka osallistuvat rahoitukseen, saavat nämä hankkeiden kehitystiedot käyttöönsä.

Lopuksi haluaisin antaa erityisen kiitoksen puolustuskomissaari Kubiliukselle. Teillä on ollut sinnikkyyttä ajaa näitäkin joskus pieneltä tuntuvia, joskus enintään keskisuuria hankkeita eteenpäin, ja samalla olette uskoneet eurooppalaisen puolustuksen kehittämisen tärkeyteen. Tässä meidän pitää katsoa kansallisten rajojen ylitse.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner Kubilius, Europe defence readiness is not only about spending more; money alone is not enough if we cannot turn investment into production capabilities quickly enough.

Commissioner, you just rightly said that deterrence also depends on speed. This package is therefore an important step: faster permitting, simpler intra-EU transfers, easier procurement and less administrative burden, especially for SMEs, will help our industry scale up faster. We also need a clear strategic direction.

The forthcoming European security strategy must translate our assessment of threats into concrete priorities and capabilities, while strengthening the European pillar of NATO. At the same time, we must strengthen security of supply, innovation and a more integrated European defence market. Our goal is clear: less red tape, faster production and stronger European defence.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, domnule comisar, vă felicit pentru ceea ce încercați să faceți și să promovați la nivelul Uniunii Europene. Pentru cineva însă, ca Putin, dacă stă și ascultă dezbaterile din acest Parlament cu ocazia diferitelor proiecte legislative, nu poate decât să râdă.

Pentru că în cadrul acestei dezbateri vin o serie de europarlamentari și spun că trebuie să mutăm și să creștem producția pe apărare în Europa, dar, pe de altă parte, susțin o serie de măsuri economice care alungă industria și firmele din Europa, cum e CBAM-ul, cum e ETS-ul.

Întrebarea mea pentru dumneavoastră este totuși: în cadrul acelei Comisii Europene, discutați despre lucrurile acestea? Sau fiecare comisar vine aici și își prezintă câte o ideologie pe care o are, mai ales comisarii care reprezintă grupuri de stânga? Pentru că e halucinant ce auzim aici.
Cu toții suntem de acord că avem nevoie de un sector de apărare mai puternic, care să producă în Europa, dar nu poți produce mai mult suprataxând, suprareglementând și alungând industria din Europa.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, imagínense a Trump. Tiene uno de sus arrebatos, uno de sus delirios —no es tan extraño— y decide cumplir sus amenazas e invadir Groenlandia.

¿Qué haríamos nosotros? ¿Qué haría Dinamarca? Poca cosa: la mayoría de sus aviones están fabricados y controlados tecnológicamente por los Estados Unidos. Y esto no ocurre solo en Dinamarca, sino también en el resto de países europeos: Grecia acaba de comprar a Israel un sistema de defensa antimisiles por 3 000 millones de dólares, y cuando le ha pedido acceso a su código fuente Israel le ha dicho que no.

¿Qué clase de soberanía defensiva es esa? Tener soberanía defensiva es producir y controlar el sistema de defensa nosotros; no es lo que ustedes están proponiendo: una rendición estratégica, seguir haciendo negocios con terceros países que nos amenazan y, encima, depender de ellos para defendernos. Eso no es soberanía defensiva.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, Senhor Comissário Kubilius, a proposta de omnibus da defesa que hoje discutimos significa uma via verde para a corrida aos armamentos. As propostas que são feitas de simplificação de procedimentos, desregulação e eliminação de requisitos ambientais e sociais significam uma via verde para o investimento na corrida aos armamentos, para a produção de armas.

Significa também que saiu o Euromilhões ao negócio da guerra. Aqueles que fazem lucros com a produção de armas, que fazem lucros com a morte e com a destruição têm neste pacote legislativo da União Europeia o verdadeiro Euromilhões, com o acesso simplificado a fundos europeus para a fabricação de armas, com mais financiamento dos Estados e menos controlo do uso dos dinheiros públicos, que são desviados para o negócio da guerra.

Significa também que aos povos saiu a fava do bolo-rei. Em Portugal, esse bolo de Natal tem um brinde e uma fava. Claro que toda a gente quer o brinde, não quer a fava. Este omnibus da defesa significa que aos povos saiu a fava, porque vão ser os povos que vão ser prejudicados com as opções que aqui estão feitas. Inclusivamente o povo ucraniano...

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, într-adevăr, trebuie să ne înarmăm. Ce să înarmăm în România? România care nu mai are armată. Am avut și noi un sistem Patriot și am fost obligați de Comisia Europeană să-l donăm Ucrainei. Ucraina, care astăzi a închis o clasă în limba română în Odesa, deși acolo e populație majoritară românească.

Mai mult decât atât, România, de la 1 iulie, este în incapacitate de plată. De trei, patru luni, instituții din România nu primesc salariu. Din octombrie nu mai există niciun ban pentru pensii și salarii. În schimb, înarmăm jandarmeria și poliția.

Astăzi, în Piața Victoriei din București, în fața Guvernului României, s-au adunat zeci de mii de oameni, împreună cu ciobanii cărora le-ați omorât oile și le-ați interzis exportul, care nu mai au cum să trăiască. Ce au făcut jandarmii înarmați de Uniunea Europeană? Au bătut și gazat ciobanii și populația română care manifesta pașnic.
Deputații S.O.S. România, partidul pe care îl conduc în opoziție în Parlamentul României, au fost acolo. Au fost bătuți și gazați de jandarmii înarmați de Uniunea Europeană...

interventions.speaker_label: Andrius Kubilius, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, thanks a lot for a very good debate. It went perhaps even broader than just quite technical issues related with the omnibus, but that really clearly shows how important defence is and how important it is for all of us to understand what is at stake. So thanks a lot to those who were working in negotiations and who were supporting now the omnibus. We shall continue in the same direction, we shall come very soon with new proposals on the development of a defence single market, with procurement changes and things like that, so that's what we shall do. We see our very clear agenda.

Now just a few comments on some statements which sound here quite strange, but I would like to stress very clearly: we race to peace, not to war. That's very simple because let's remember the old Roman saying: 'if you want peace, prepare for war'. If we shall not be prepared to defend ourselves, we shall have a war. So I don't agree with those who are arguing that we should not invest into our defence because our people will suffer. Our people will suffer if we do not invest into defence, because war can come very easily.

Second, here was quite an interesting debate about Member States, the Commission, Parliament and so on. Well, definitely all institutions and councils have differences, but what we need, perhaps, to see very clearly is that, as I said, we are going through quite a deep transformation and definitely after 80 years of such a collective defence system where Member States were taking all the responsibilities, it still continues to influence all our way of thinking. But I think that we shall find the best ways how to become much more effective in Europe.

And here I would say again, Mr Terheş, you put a very good strategic question: how can we do our defence if we are not taking care about the competitiveness of our economy? Well, I would not agree with your major point that we are not taking care about our competitiveness, because if you will look into the Global Competitiveness Index, which is published each year, you will see a very clear issue: Europe is quite different. There are Member States – like, for example, Denmark, Sweden and Finland – which are at the top of that international index, which means that they are able to be very competitive even with what Brussels is doing, what we are putting in our new legislation, on climate change and so on and so on. But there are countries – including even your country and even my country – which could be much better in that index, which means that on a national level, we are not doing enough to be so competitive as we need to be.

Well, I would not agree with your major point that we are not taking care about our competitiveness, because if you will look into the Global Competitiveness Index, which is published each year, you will see a very clear issue: Europe is quite different. There are Member States – like, for example, Denmark, Sweden and Finland – which are at the top of that international index, which means that they are able to be very competitive even with what Brussels is doing, what we are putting in our new legislation, on climate change and so on and so on. But there are countries – including even your country and even my country – which could be much better in that index, which means that on a national level, we are not doing enough to be so competitive as we need to be.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, thank you to everyone who has spoken in support of this package. I expect it will receive broad, cross‑group support tomorrow, and it should, because on the question of security, this House has been much more united than the governments we have negotiated with.

Where the omnibus package as a whole falls short is the lack of harmonised rules for intra‑EU transfer licences and procurement. We have heard this today and I will say it once again: the work is not finished and I expect the Council to actually come back to the table.

Europe needs to speed up – we have heard this also many times in security, in building industrial capacity, in competitiveness – to keep up with the rest of the world. These are important words and we need to live up to them.

One more thing which I noticed during this debate is that the far right was not prepared. They were not present. They were not present during the negotiations. They were not present during this debate. To all of your voters of the far right, this is exactly how they represent you here. They do not care about your jobs. They do not care about the economy. They do not care about the industry or security. They are not even here.

Colleagues, let's stop treating security as something that competes with everything else that we care about. There is no prosperity without security. There is no social contract, my colleagues from left, without security. Security is the condition for all of it.
This package removes some of the barriers and it is long overdue. What it cannot do is supply the urgency. That has to come from the 27 capitals and, so far, it has come very unevenly.

So, let's not pretend that we have time. The threat is here, it is deliberate and it does not pause while we consult or bicker here. Every day we spend deciding is a day when Russia spends producing more drones and missiles. Tomorrow, we can fix a part of that.

paragraphs.text: Hr. Formand! Jeg nåede at høre cirka en time af den forrige debat om Ruslands hybride krig mod Europa, og derfor glæder det mig, at de to eller tre parallelle universer, som Europa-Parlamentet var splittet op i, nu i den her debat heldigvis har været samlet til en enkelt fælles virkelighed. Tusind tak for det.

Der er et sted i Bibelen, hvor Jesus siger til sine disciple "Ånden er rede, men kødet er skrøbeligt". Jeg vil ikke strække sammenligningen alt for langt, det skal vi ikke her. Men EU befinder sig på mange måder det samme sted; Vi er klar i ånden, men kødet er skrøbeligt.
Nu styrker vi den praktiske, konkrete dimension. Det, synes jeg, er meget, meget positivt, og det vil jeg gerne sige tak til alle for at have været med til at bidrage til.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, thank you for the good discussion and supportive words about this omnibus. In this discussion, only the left and the right told the normal excuses to leave Europe and Ukraine defenceless and to be attacked, raped and pillaged by Russia.

Luckily, the vast majority of this House supports the development of Europe's defence. The problem is clearly not our Parliament, but the Member States who do not see the big picture and stick to the narrow national interest.

Therefore, I hope that all our Members not only support this omnibus tomorrow in the voting, but also take this message to our national governments. Let's speak, let's find less excuses and take action. Our people and our security demands it. And as my dear colleague, Ms Yar, said, the work is not done yet. This is just the first step on our long road to the real European defence-industrial capability to support our forces and secure Europe.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, Russia will remain a long‑term threat to Europe, even after the war in Ukraine ends. We must continue and increase our support to Ukraine while strengthening our own capacity to deter aggression and defend ourselves. And we must all understand – also you on the right wing – that there will be no Europe as we know and love it unless we are prepared to defend it. We are not merely defending our borders; Ukraine is not merely defending theirs; we are defending our people, our safety and our democracy. We are defending peace, prosperity and our European way of life, and Ukraine knows this. My parents and their generation knew this too. It was why they defended Finland's independence against the same aggressor in their time. Now it is our time to shoulder our responsibility for Europe's defence.

This defence omnibus is an important starting point, but it should only be considered as that – a starting point. Thank you also to Commissioner Kubilius, because you have been very clear that it is a starting point. We have to do more and we have to do it together. For Renew Europe, it has been very important that this defence omnibus strengthens our EU defence readiness by cutting bureaucracy, speeding up defence procurement and simplifying intra‑EU transfers of defence‑related products.

Listening now to all of you here, almost all of you, I think that we have a big majority for this tomorrow when we vote. So please also tell your Member States that our leaders in our capitals also have to do more, because it is now up to the Member States whether we succeed with this in the future. Thank you, Mr Kubilius, for all your efforts and look forward to your next proposal.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, approving this omnibus legislation, which I am sure will happen tomorrow, is an important step.

Obviously, the negotiations were a mixed success. We were quite successful in some areas, perhaps fell a bit short in others. But let me say that actually easing the regulatory burden is relatively straightforward and, I would say, the easy part of a much bigger, bigger picture.

In order to actually get to where we want to be with regard to European defence, we need to be able to create a genuine defence single market, which is somewhat more difficult. We need to be able to provide all the necessary financial resources, both on the European level as well as on the level of Member States, which is quite a challenge.

And obviously we need to be able to keep all our people on board. This, I think, is the biggest challenge because, as I said, our people understand the importance of defence. They are ready to pay more for defence, but they want to see that it is done in a socially fair and just way so that nobody is left behind. That actually requires a truly holistic approach to defence, a whole‑society approach to defence.

This said, I would like to thank all my co‑rapporteurs and shadow rapporteurs. I congratulate them and congratulate Commissioner Kubilius at writing this very important intermediate station because we do have a long way to go yet.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, suomalaisena reservin ylikersanttina ymmärrän, että puolustusmenojen lisääminen on välttämätöntä, mutta yhtä tärkeää on käyttää ne rahat järkevästi. Meidän on investoitava suorituskykyihin, joita tarvitsemme sekä nyt että tulevaisuudessa.

EU vähentää nyt hallintoa, helpottaa investointeja ja parantaa yritysten mahdollisuuksia kasvattaa tuotantoaan. Seuraavaksi tämän pitää näkyä konkreettisesti yritysten arjessa. Meidän on tuotettava nopeammin ammuksia, ohjuksia, drooneja ja ilmapuolustusjärjestelmiä. Tarvitsemme vahvempaa tiedustelua, valvontaa sekä avaruus-, kyber- ja elektronisen sodankäynnin kykyjä.

Suomi ilmoitti liittyvänsä Ranskan vetämään eurooppalaiseen ydinpeloteyhteistyöhön. Kannustan kaikkia jäsenmaita samaan. Meidän on rakennettava vahvempi Naton eurooppalainen pilari ja otettava suurempi vastuu omasta puolustuksestamme.

Sama koskee Euroopan kokonaisturvallisuutta laajemmin. Hybridiuhkien osalta kannattaa unohtaa armeijassa meihin iskostettu ohje "ei saa ennakoida". Meidän on opittava tunnistamaan vihollisen pienetkin signaalit, rakennettava vahva pelote, resilienssi ja selviytymiskyky sekä reagointi sen sijaan, että jokaista hybridihyökkäystä kohdeltaisiin puhtaasti sotilaallisena ongelmana.

Venäjän ei myöskään pidä antaa uskoa, että tavanomaisen sodankäynnin kynnyksen alapuolella toimimisesta ei koidu seurauksia. Kun Eurooppaan kohdistuu vihamielisiä toimia, niihin on vastattava uskottavasti ja koordinoidusti.

Monet Euroopan maat ja ukrainalaiset yritykset tekevät jo tiivistä yhteistyötä droonien ja muiden miehittämättömien alusten kehittämisessä ja tuotannossa. Tätä yhteistyötä on tärkeää lisätä ja saada Ukraina EU:n sisämarkkinoiden piiriin.

Vahvempi Eurooppa edellyttää vahvaa kokonaisturvallisuuden ajattelumallia, yhteisen tilannekuvan jatkuvaa päivittämistä sekä meiltä poliitikoilta uskallusta tehdä strategisesti rohkeita ja kauas katsovia päätöksiä. Euroopan on aika seisoa omilla jaloillaan nyt.

paragraphs.text: Riho Terras (PPE), kirjalikultOn viimane aeg lihtsustada kaitsevaldkonnaga seonduvat liigset bürokraatiat, mida me ei saa endale lubada praeguses julgeolekuolukorras. Me peame olema võimelised relvastust ja laskemoona kiiremini tootma, ostma ja EL riikide vahel müüma. Sestap on positiivne, et Euroopa Rahvapartei eestvedamisel võtsime vastu paketi mis lihtsustab ja kiirendab mitmeid olulisi aspekte nagu lubade väljastamist uute kaitserajatiste ja taristu loomiseks, hangete läbiviimist kaitsevaldkonnas ning kaitsetööstuse toodangu, tarkvara ja tehnoloogiate liikumist EL liikmesriikide vahel. Kui varem pidid firmad ootama kaks kuni neli kuud, et saada luba kaitsetööstuse toodangu teise liikmesriiki saatmiseks, siis nüüd saab osadel juhtudel vastava loa loetud päevadega. Kahjuks pean nentima, et toodangu liikumise osas ühest EL liikmesriigist teise oleks saanud olla palju ambitsioonikam. Paraku jäid peale osade liikmesriikide huvid, mis läbirääkimistel suruti läbi Euroopa Liidu Nõukogu poolt. Paraku Prantsusmaa vaatab endiselt praegust olukorda läbi tööstuspoliitika prisma, mitte julgeolekukaalutluste. Üritatakse tekki iga hinna eest enda poole tõmmata isegi siis kui see ei paku kaugeltki kõige kiiremat ega efektiivsemat lahendust, mida Euroopa hetkel hädasti vajab.

interventions.speaker_label: Kaja Kallas, Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, first on the title of this debate: 'escalation in the Middle East'.

Yes, to some extent it describes recent trends. For example, the Houthis, with the support of Iran, have now extended their grip along the critical coast of Yemen, potentially choking another crucial strait, Bab al Mandab, with dire implications for the global economy. And this, at least in part, is why today's debate is necessary.

But the title of the debate is also misleading. What we are now witnessing in Yemen and elsewhere – in Iran, but also in the West Bank, for example – is also part of the same arc of instability that has plagued the region for far too long. The Houthi attacks in the Red Sea against Yemen and Saudi Arabia, as well as their threats against the freedom of navigation, while unlawful, are a predictable development.

That is why the European Union has maintained consistent messaging to the parties of the conflict, calling for de-escalation, restraint, the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, the cessation of Iran's indiscriminate attacks, full support to the countries of the region affected by those attacks, and respect for international law, including freedom of navigation in the Straits of Hormuz and Bab al Mandab.

The European Union is also working to mitigate the impact together with international partners. Our EU naval operation, ASPIDES, continues to escort vessels in the Red Sea and we will reinforce our coordination with the multinational maritime coalition that Saudi Arabia has launched recently. But we need to do more, in particular to support the Yemeni Government and to fight smuggling.

Honourable Members, with regard to Iran, repression is widespread and the number of executions of young Iranians is now increasing at an alarming pace. That is why we have imposed new sanctions and conveyed clear messages to the Iranian authorities that such behaviour will have consequences. We will continue responding with all the tools we have available, including by increasing support for Iranian civil society.

At the same time, the Iranian nuclear issue has remained a constant challenge and the European Union's position has not changed: Iran must never have a nuclear weapon, and Iran must comply with its legally binding nuclear safeguard obligations under the Non-Proliferation Treaty.

In the West Bank, settlement and outpost expansion is increasing, along with more forced displacements and record levels of settler violence. On top of three packages of sanctions against extremist settlers, discussions are now ongoing in the Council on possible further designations. Accountability is a prerequisite for reining in violent settlers.

At the same time, it is important that the European Union remains consistent and coherent in our position, collectively calling for the respect of international law. This means repeating our calls, along with our international partners, including the UK, for the suspension of settler expansion, including the E1 project, which seriously threatens the viability of the two-state solution.

In Gaza, what is escalating is an already dire humanitarian situation. As winter approaches, overcrowded sites for displaced people are at risk of flooding and disease, and there is a ceasefire in name only. People are still being killed and wounded. The conditions for the implementation of the Gaza peace plan are unchanged. For progress to be possible, the international community must continue to call for the permanent disarmament of Hamas and all other non-state armed groups and the withdrawal of Israeli forces from the Gaza Strip.

The EU continues to do its part for the implementation of the UN Security Council Resolution 2803. We are using all the instruments at our disposal: security through our CSDP missions, EUBAM Rafah and EUPOL COPPS; support to the Palestinian Authority and its governance and reforms; and assistance with early recovery and reconstruction.

The Palestinian Donor Group, organised by the Commission last July, launched the Team Gaza Initiative, which raised initially EUR 900 million of funds for early recovery, together with 15 international partners.

The Israeli elections next month and the Palestinian legislative elections scheduled for November could be important turning points. We stand ready to assist in any way we can, notably when it comes to the Palestinian elections.

Honourable Members, in a region where war and conflict dominate every facet of life – be it in Yemen, Iran or the West Bank – the only chance we have of breaking the cycle of violence is if we double down on our support for the rule of law and continue to pursue every diplomatic opening and champion democracy.

interventions.speaker_label: Hildegard Bentele, on behalf of the PPE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PPE Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, High Representative, colleagues, the Houthis are advancing again in Yemen. They have taken new territory near the Bab al Mandab Strait, one of the world's most important shipping routes. This is not just a local conflict. It is a movement with an anti-American, antisemitic agenda hitting strongly our economy, and it is gaining ground.

Washington is stepping back. Saudi Arabia asked the United States for direct military help, the answer was 'no'. We are witnessing rebels in sandals moving very strategically, while also revealing that armies existed only on paper. For decades, America has shaped the security architecture in this region. Now it is motionless and that leaves a gap.

Europe cannot ignore that gap. Both straits are under pressure now, and alternative routes are few. This week, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was struck by drones from Iraq from a group not yet identified, and the human cost is high, with more than 80 000 people displaced since the start of the month.

Europe is already engaged. Our naval mission ASPIDES protects merchant shipping in the Red Sea, we back Yemen's recognised government and an inclusive UN-led political process. As America pulls out, these efforts matter more and need to be strengthened.

But colleagues, we also need to think much bigger. The sudden Houthi advancement did not happen by coincidence. It is part of the bigger agenda to destabilise the West. The only answer can be to stay united and to stabilise the West again by all means.

interventions.speaker_label: Γιάννης Μανιάτης, εξ ονόματος της ομάδας S&D.

paragraphs.text: Κύριε Πρόεδρε, κυρία Ύπατη Εκπρόσωπε, οι τελευταίες εξελίξεις στην Αραβική Χερσόνησο είναι ιδιαίτερα ανησυχητικές. Επίθεση δρόνων στον αγωγό Ανατολής-Δύσης στη Σαουδική Αραβία. Οι Χούθι απειλούν την ελεύθερη ναυσιπλοΐα στην Ερυθρά Θάλασσα —χαίρομαι πάντως για τη συμμετοχή του ελληνικού Πολεμικού Ναυτικού στην επιχείρηση ασπίδας στην Ερυθρά Θάλασσα. Η συμφωνία της Μέκκας αποδεικνύεται περισσότερο δήλωση προθέσεων.

Η κατάσταση στη Γάζα παραμένει δραματική. Η Ευρώπη αδυνατεί να πάρει οποιοδήποτε μέτρο κατά των παράνομων εποικισμών και των παραβιάσεων του διεθνούς δικαίου από την κυβέρνηση Νετανιάχου. Υπάρχει ανάγκη μιας ολοκληρωμένης στρατηγικής για τη Μέση Ανατολή που θα επιτρέπει στην Ευρώπη ουσιαστικό ρόλο στη διαμόρφωση των εξελίξεων, για να μπορούμε να υπερασπιστούμε τις αρχές, το διεθνές δίκαιο και τα συμφέροντά μας. Γιατί όποιος δεν είναι στο τραπέζι είναι συνήθως στο μενού. Δεν επιτρέπεται να αποφασίζουν άλλοι για εμάς και εμείς απλώς να πληρώνουμε τον λογαριασμό.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Mathilde Androuët, au nom du groupe PfE.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, depuis des mois l'escalade au Moyen-Orient démontre ce que produit l'absence de compromis. D'un côté, une stratégie américaine dont l'issue politique demeure incertaine. De l'autre, un régime iranien qui poursuit l'affrontement et l'étend par l'action de ses alliés, notamment les Houthis.

Cette guerre est une tragédie humaine, mais ce qui se passe à Ormuz et en Mer Rouge a aussi un prix pour les Européens: un pétrole au-dessus de 100 dollars, des carburants plus chers et une nouvelle poussée inflationniste qui se profile. Au bout du compte, c'est la menace d'un prix à la pompe de 3 Euros par litre et des agriculteurs étranglés par le prix des fertilisants.

Cette crise rappelle combien notre dépendance énergétique nous rend vulnérables à des conflits sur lesquels nous n'avons pratiquement aucune prise. Face à cela, l'Europe ne doit pas ajouter des discours sur une intervention militaire, mais retrouver une voie diplomatique tout en ajoutant des mesures d'urgence sur les prix de l'énergie. Notre intérêt est clair: favoriser la désescalade, la liberté de navigation et le retour à la négociation. L'Europe ne doit être ni belligérante, ni rester spectatrice des événements.

interventions.speaker_label: Jacek Ozdoba, w imieniu grupy ECR.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Szanowni Państwo! Mamy do czynienia z jednym z największych kryzysów geopolitycznych i problemów związanych z oddziaływaniem na rynki europejskie poprzez zablokowanie do Europy dostaw gazu i ropy. Arabia Saudyjska, Bahrajn, Kuwejt, Zjednoczone Emiraty Arabskie – dobrzy partnerzy, nasi przyjaciele – zostali zaatakowani i mamy do czynienia z czymś, co jest dzisiaj sytuacją bezprecedensową.

Ataki na obiekty cywilne oraz infrastrukturę energetyczną dowodzą tego, że reżim w Teheranie, ale nie tylko, pozwala sobie na coraz więcej. Jest to również atak na nasze gospodarki Po tym, co się wydarzyło na Ukrainie, i tak mamy problem z oddziaływaniem wojny. Teraz kolejny – widmo wojny na Bliskim Wschodzie prowadzi do kryzysu energetycznego. Dlatego musimy być solidarni i EKR proponuje rezolucję, która da wyraźny sygnał, że Europa stoi razem z Arabią Saudyjską, Zjednoczonymi Emiratami Arabskimi, Bahrajnem oraz Katarem, ponieważ nie możemy tolerować przemocy i ataków na obiekty cywilne.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Renew Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, High-Representative, Europe keeps saying that the two-state solution is the only path to peace. But while we repeat these words, the possibility of two states is disappearing before our eyes. In the West Bank settlements continue to expand, Palestinians are being driven from their land and, with the olive harvest approaching, families risk losing their livelihood.
High-Representative, you have said yourself that these settlements are illegal. So stop trade with illegal settlements, sanction those responsible for settler violence.

And in Gaza, the humanitarian situation is dramatic and we are failing the generation that could rebuild Palestine. Thirteen Palestinians have scholarships to Belgian universities. Salwa should be studying at my alma mater, KU Leuven, and Essam should be Ghent preparing to help rebuild Gaza's water system. Instead, they remain trapped and even my own country, Belgium, cannot agree to bring them to safety. What message colleagues, are we sending to them? Study. Believe in your future. Believe in peace. But don't expect Europe to help you to reach it.
Colleagues, let's be clear: yes, the terrorist organisation Hamas must lay down its arms. And yes, Israel has the right to live in security. So please, try to come to the two-state solution.

interventions.speaker_label: Mounir Satouri, au nom du groupe Verts/ALE.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, le Moyen-Orient est à feu et à sang. Le gouvernement de Netanyahou entretient cette fuite en avant. Colonisation, annexion des territoires palestiniens occupés, destruction de Gaza et déplacement de tout un peuple constituent sa feuille de route.

Les États-Unis de Trump soutiennent et l'Europe regarde. À Gaza, les preuves de génocide s'accumulent. En Cisjordanie, un régime d'apartheid se consolide. Au Liban, les crimes de guerre se multiplient. Pourtant, l'Union européenne persiste dans sa politique du «deux poids, deux mesures». Face aux crimes de Poutine en Ukraine: 21 paquets de sanctions. Face aux crimes de Netanyahou en Palestine: l'impunité. Alors que valent nos principes si nous ne les défendons pas lorsqu'ils nous arrangent? Que vaut le droit international s'il ne s'applique pas à tous?

Madame la Haute représentante, les Palestiniens n'ont plus besoin de promesses. Ils n'ont plus le temps. Si l'Europe veut encore pouvoir parler de paix, de justice, de droits humains, ses actes doivent enfin être cohérents avec ses propres valeurs. Alors assez de silence, assez de contradictions, place aux actes.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: thar ceann an Ghrúpa The Left

paragraphs.text: A Uachtaráin, tá daoine ag fáil bháis mar thoradh ar bheartas na hEorpa. Tá forghabháil Iosrael ar an Liobáin ag dul i méid. Tá cinedhíothú in Gaza fós ar siúl. Tá an Bruach Thiar á ghoid os comhair ár súl. Tá Rialtas Iosrael soiléir faoina chuspóirí. Tá sé ag iarraidh Gaza agus an Bruach Thiar a ghlanadh ar bhonn eitneach. Tá sé ag iarraidh stát dá gcuid féin a shéanadh ar mhuintir na Palaistíne. Is mian leis forlámhas a ghlacadh ar an Liobáin. Tá sé á dhéanamh seo gan aon iarmhairtí.
Member States continue to arm Israel. We still give them privileged access to the EU market. We continue to trade with the illegal settlements.
Europe's crime is not being too slow to respond. Europe's crime is complicity. Until words of condemnation are met with action, Europe will be an accomplice in Israel's crimes.
So, no more double standards – sanction Israel, ban settlement trade and stop the weapons flowing from Europe to slaughter Palestinians.

Member States continue to arm Israel. We still give them privileged access to the EU market. We continue to trade with the illegal settlements.

Europe's crime is not being too slow to respond. Europe's crime is complicity. Until words of condemnation are met with action, Europe will be an accomplice in Israel's crimes.

So, no more double standards – sanction Israel, ban settlement trade and stop the weapons flowing from Europe to slaughter Palestinians.

paragraphs.text: Г-н Председател, в продължение на години Европейският съюз реагира на кризите в Близкия изток със санкции, изолация и политически натиск. Днес петролът отново се търгува над 100 долара за барел и се очаква да расте, а ситуацията в Близкия изток остава непредсказуема и взривоопасна.

Сега приоритетът е защитата на европейската икономика, която ще понася нови силни удари от нарушените вериги на доставки и галопиращите цени на енергийните ресурси. Тепърва ще плащаме данък логистика. Югоизточна Европа може да има ключова роля. Инвестициите в пристанища, железопътни връзки и логистични центрове, развитието на коридор №8 и свързаността в Черно море могат да превърнат региона в стратегическа врата за европейската търговия. Нужни са диверсифицирани доставки и национални стратегически резерви от ключови ресурси.
Това е прагматичната политика, от която Европа се нуждае - по-малко идеология и повече защита на собствените икономически интереси.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, thank you very much. Europe must decide. Either we help shape the future of the Middle East with the right partners, or its instability will shape ours. The threat is Iran. The threat is its proxies.

High Representative, I heard you talk about the settlers and sanctions. What about the Houthis? I mean, the Council talked about it, fantastic, because we have to put them in the black terrorist list of the European Union because they are a terrorist organisation. It is something obvious that we are saying here, but I guess that you will put the pressure on the governments to reinforce this idea.

Thank you very much for talking about the reinforcement of operational speeds, we need to do it. But let me add also collaboration with our partners in the Gulf and other regions like Jordan, Egypt, whatever, also through the Abraham agreements, I think that would be very good. Let's, for once, do it in the appropriate way. Thank you very much.
And consequences about the Houthis are there. Many of the colleagues have spoken about it. This is a direct threat for all of us.
